## Reviewer's Guide Refactors cron job UI to match Settings patterns and gate it via runtime serverConfig enableBusinessFeatures, introduces a new Skill Detail modal system with reusable providers and icons, adds Electron desktop File menu actions and navigation bridge, restructures desktop build/packaging scripts and workflows (including a static i18n codemod for Electron), and adds new SWR hooks and APIs for listing Klavis/LobeHub tools plus localization and copy updates. #### Sequence diagram for Electron File menu actions to renderer navigation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant OSMenu as ElectronMain_FileMenu participant BrowserMgr as BrowserManager participant MainWin as MainWindow participant IPC as NavigationBroadcast participant Renderer as DesktopFileMenuBridge participant Router as ReactRouter participant HomeMenu as useCreateMenuItems participant AgentStore as useAgentStore User->>OSMenu: Select NewTopic / NewAgent / NewAgentGroup / NewPage OSMenu->>BrowserMgr: getMainWindow() BrowserMgr-->>OSMenu: mainWindow OSMenu->>MainWin: show() alt NewTopic OSMenu->>MainWin: broadcast(createNewTopic) else NewAgent OSMenu->>MainWin: broadcast(createNewAgent) else NewAgentGroup OSMenu->>MainWin: broadcast(createNewAgentGroup) else NewPage OSMenu->>MainWin: broadcast(createNewPage) end MainWin->>IPC: emit event IPC-->>Renderer: useWatchBroadcast(callback) par DesktopFileMenuBridge handlers Renderer->>AgentStore: activeAgentId, inboxAgentId Renderer->>HomeMenu: createAgent, createEmptyGroup, createPage end alt createNewTopic Renderer->>Router: navigate(SESSION_CHAT_URL(targetAgentId,false)) else createNewAgent Renderer->>HomeMenu: createAgent() else createNewAgentGroup Renderer->>HomeMenu: createEmptyGroup() else createNewPage Renderer->>HomeMenu: createPage() end ``` #### Sequence diagram for opening Skill Detail modal and connecting ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant SkillItem as SkillListItem participant ModalFactory as createLobehubSkillDetailModal participant Modal as SkillDetailModal participant Provider as LobehubDetailProvider participant DetailCtx as DetailContext participant Store as useToolStore participant SWR as useFetchProviderTools participant Header as SkillDetail_Header participant ConnectHook as useSkillConnect participant ToolsAPI as toolsClient_market_connectListTools User->>SkillItem: Click skill item SkillItem->>ModalFactory: createLobehubSkillDetailModal(identifier) ModalFactory->>Modal: createModal(children=LobehubSkillDetailContent) Modal->>Provider: render(identifier) Note over Provider,Store: Provider resolves static config and connection state Provider->>Store: lobehubSkillStoreSelectors.getServers Store-->>Provider: serverState(status,...) Provider->>Store: useFetchProviderTools(identifier) Store->>SWR: useSWR(lobehub-skill-tools-identifier,...) SWR->>ToolsAPI: connectListTools.query({provider}) ToolsAPI-->>SWR: {tools:[...]} SWR-->>Provider: tools, toolsLoading Provider->>DetailCtx: DetailContext.Provider(value) Modal->>Header: render(type=lobehub) Header->>ConnectHook: useSkillConnect({identifier,type}) User->>Header: Click Connect Header->>ConnectHook: handleConnect() ConnectHook->>Store: createLobehubSkillServer / openOAuthWindow Store-->>ConnectHook: connection established ConnectHook-->>Header: isConnected=true Header-->>Modal: close() via useModalContext ``` #### Class diagram for Skill Detail modal, providers, and store hooks ```mermaid classDiagram class DetailContextValue { <> +string author +string authorUrl +any config +string description +string_or_ReactComponent icon +string identifier +string introduction +boolean isConnected +string label +string localizedDescription +string localizedIntroduction +string serverName +Array tools +boolean toolsLoading } class DetailContext { +DetailContextValue Provider } class KlavisDetailProvider { +KlavisDetailProvider(children,identifier,serverName) -config -klavisServers -serverState -isConnected } class LobehubDetailProvider { +LobehubDetailProvider(children,identifier) -config -lobehubSkillServers -serverState -isConnected } class SkillDetailInner { +SkillDetailInner(type) -TabKey activeTab } class Header { +Header(type) -handleConnectWithTracking() -renderIcon() -renderConnectButton() } class Nav { +Nav(activeTab,setActiveTab,mobile) } class Overview { +Overview() } class Schema { +Schema() -ModeType mode } class KlavisSkillDetailContent { +KlavisSkillDetailContent(identifier,serverName) } class LobehubSkillDetailContent { +LobehubSkillDetailContent(identifier) } class createKlavisSkillDetailModal { +createKlavisSkillDetailModal(identifier,serverName) } class createLobehubSkillDetailModal { +createLobehubSkillDetailModal(identifier) } class useSkillConnect { +useSkillConnect(params) +handleConnect() +boolean isConnecting +boolean isConnected } class KlavisStoreAction { <> +useFetchServerTools(serverName) SWRResponse } class LobehubSkillStoreAction { <> +useFetchProviderTools(provider) SWRResponse } class klavisRouter { +getTools(input) query } class toolsClient_klavis { +getTools.query(params) } class toolsClient_market { +connectListTools.query(params) } class KlavisSkillIcon { +KlavisSkillIcon(icon,label,size) } class LobehubSkillIcon { +LobehubSkillIcon(icon,label,size) } class useControls KlavisDetailProvider ..|> DetailContextValue LobehubDetailProvider ..|> DetailContextValue KlavisDetailProvider --> DetailContext : provides LobehubDetailProvider --> DetailContext : provides SkillDetailInner --> DetailContext : useDetailContext() Header --> DetailContext : useDetailContext() Overview --> DetailContext : useDetailContext() Schema --> DetailContext : useDetailContext() SkillDetailInner --> Header SkillDetailInner --> Nav SkillDetailInner --> Overview SkillDetailInner --> Schema KlavisSkillDetailContent --> KlavisDetailProvider KlavisSkillDetailContent --> SkillDetailInner LobehubSkillDetailContent --> LobehubDetailProvider LobehubSkillDetailContent --> SkillDetailInner createKlavisSkillDetailModal --> KlavisSkillDetailContent createLobehubSkillDetailModal --> LobehubSkillDetailContent Header --> useSkillConnect KlavisDetailProvider --> KlavisStoreAction : useFetchServerTools LobehubDetailProvider --> LobehubSkillStoreAction : useFetchProviderTools KlavisStoreAction --> toolsClient_klavis : getTools.query LobehubSkillStoreAction --> toolsClient_market : connectListTools.query KlavisSkillIcon <.. useControls : used in tools menu LobehubSkillIcon <.. useControls : used in tools menu ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Cron job feature is now gated by a runtime server config flag and its UI is redesigned using Settings-style FormGroup layouts. |
  • Replace compile-time ENABLE_BUSINESS_FEATURES guard with serverConfigSelectors.enableBusinessFeatures when fetching/rendering cron data and actions.
  • Update AgentCronJobs, ProfileEditor, and Cron sidebar to respect the runtime flag and avoid SWR calls when disabled.
  • Redesign CronJobScheduleConfig and CronJobContentEditor to use FormGroup, createStaticStyles/cssVar, weekday button toggles, execution limit checkbox, and improved hourly/time controls.
  • Simplify CronJobHeader layout to a large 28px borderless title input with a single LobeSwitch toggle and tweak CronJobSaveButton padding/width.
| `src/store/agent/slices/cron/action.ts`

`src/locales/default/setting.ts` | | Skill store and skill settings views gain a new Skill Detail modal with shared styling, provider-specific context, and image-based icons reused across settings and chat controls. |
  • Replace IntegrationDetailModal usage with new createLobehubSkillDetailModal/createKlavisSkillDetailModal helpers and remove old IntegrationDetailModal implementation.
  • Introduce SkillDetail layout (Header, Nav, Overview, Schema) plus DetailContext, provider wrappers, and reuse MCP schema viewer to show tools/capabilities.
  • Refactor LobehubSkillItem, KlavisSkillItem, McpSkillItem, and SkillStoreContent to use the new detail modal, shared styles, and clickable rows opening details.
  • Extract KlavisSkillIcon and LobehubSkillIcon components (image or vector) for both AgentTool and ChatInput tool menus, and centralize list item styles in settings/skill/style.ts.

`src/locales/default/plugin.ts` | | Desktop Electron app build and packaging flow is restructured, with dedicated scripts, workflow changes, and a new codemod that statically wires i18n resources for Electron builds. |
  • Replace old desktop build scripts (build:electron, desktop:build, desktop:build-next, etc.) with build:main, desktop:build:renderer, desktop:package:* commands and update manual/pr/release workflows to use desktop:package:app.
  • Add verify-electron-codemod GitHub workflow that runs scripts/electronWorkflow/modifiers/index.mts, and extend modifiers to include a new convertI18nDynamicToStatic step.
  • Implement i18nDynamicToStatic.mts to generate static locale namespace maps and UI resources, emit __electronI18nMap and __electronUiResources, and rewrite loadI18nNamespaceModule/getUILocaleAndResources to avoid dynamic imports.
  • Adjust apps/desktop package.json/README and root package.json scripts to match the new build/package commands and move node-mac-permissions to optionalDependencies.

  • Add createNewTopic/createNewAgent/createNewAgentGroup/createNewPage entries to NavigationBroadcastEvents and hook them up in Linux, macOS, and Windows menu implementations with platform-appropriate accelerators.
  • Introduce DesktopFileMenuBridge React component that listens for the new broadcast events and uses routing/create menu hooks to open the appropriate views.
  • Register DesktopFileMenuBridge in the main layout alongside existing desktop-only bridges and adjust TitleBar rendering to be wrapped in Suspense.

  • Extend klavisRouter with a public getTools endpoint and add KlavisStoreAction.useFetchServerTools plus LobehubSkillStoreAction.useFetchProviderTools to fetch tool lists via SWR.
  • Wire new hooks into KlavisDetailProvider and LobehubDetailProvider to populate SkillDetail Schema tab, and refactor useSkillConnect dependency array formatting.
  • Tweak various UI details: remove ToolsList avatar margin override, make ReadFileView preview scrollable, enlarge skill store button, add full-width icons to view-mode menus, make desktop hotkey hook selection stable, gate AuthRequiredModal with desktop onboarding completion, and update copyright year in onboarding and email templates.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Sets the NVIDIA model provider configuration to always proxy requests through the server by enabling the root-level disableBrowserRequest flag, avoiding direct browser calls that hit a CORS-restricted NVIDIA API endpoint. #### Sequence diagram for NVIDIA provider requests with disableBrowserRequest enabled ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant BrowserApp participant BackendServer participant NvidiaAPI User ->> BrowserApp: Initiate NVIDIA chat completion BrowserApp ->> BackendServer: POST /api/chat (provider nvidia) BackendServer ->> NvidiaAPI: POST /v1/chat/completions NvidiaAPI -->> BackendServer: Chat completion response BackendServer -->> BrowserApp: Normalized AI response BrowserApp -->> User: Render NVIDIA model reply %% Behavior is driven by provider config: disableBrowserRequest true ensures no direct BrowserApp -> NvidiaAPI call ``` #### Class diagram for updated NVIDIA ModelProviderCard configuration ```mermaid classDiagram class ModelProviderCard { string id string description string checkModel boolean disableBrowserRequest ModelListConfig modelList string modelsUrl } class ModelListConfig { boolean showModelFetcher } class Nvidia { } Nvidia --|> ModelProviderCard ModelProviderCard o--> ModelListConfig %% Nvidia instance example: %% id = nvidia %% checkModel = meta/llama-3.2-1b-instruct %% disableBrowserRequest = true %% modelList.showModelFetcher = true %% modelsUrl = https://build.nvidia.com/models ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Force NVIDIA provider traffic through server-side proxy instead of browser to avoid CORS issues. |
  • Add a root-level disableBrowserRequest: true flag to the NVIDIA ModelProviderCard config so browser-originated requests are disabled for this provider.
  • Document in code comments that the NVIDIA chat completions endpoint currently has CORS issues and therefore browser request mode is disabled.

paradedb_postgresql Postgres-->>Docker: healthcheck ready Docker->>Postgres: stop (after init step) SetupScript->>Docker: docker compose up -d Docker->>Network: start network_service Docker->>Redis: ## Reviewer's Guide Implements a Home starter "write" flow that creates a document and routes the user into a page-specific agent chat, removes the legacy image starter mode, and stabilizes related e2e and unit tests (agent exec threadId, placeholder hour generator) and chat input UX. #### Sequence diagram for Home starter write flow creating document and invoking PageAgent ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant HomePage as HomePageStarterList participant HomeStore as HomeInputStore participant ChatInput as InputAreaUseSend participant DocService as documentService participant Router as navigate participant AgentStore as AgentStore participant ChatStore as ChatStore User->>HomePage: clickWriteStarter HomePage->>HomeStore: setInputActiveMode(write) User->>ChatInput: typeMessage(帮我写一篇关于人工智能的文章) User->>ChatInput: pressEnter ChatInput->>HomeStore: getState().inputActiveMode ChatInput->>HomeStore: sendAsWrite(message) HomeStore->>AgentStore: getAgentStoreState() AgentStore-->>HomeStore: agentState HomeStore->>AgentStore: builtinAgentSelectors.inboxAgentId(agentState) AgentStore-->>HomeStore: inboxAgentId HomeStore->>AgentStore: agentSelectors.getAgentConfigById(inboxAgentId) AgentStore-->>HomeStore: inboxConfig(model, provider) HomeStore->>DocService: createDocument(editorData "{}", fileType "custom/document", title from message) DocService-->>HomeStore: newDoc(id) HomeStore->>Router: navigate(/page/newDoc.id) HomeStore->>AgentStore: builtinAgentSelectors.pageAgentId(agentState) AgentStore-->>HomeStore: pageAgentId alt hasPageAgent alt hasModelAndProvider HomeStore->>AgentStore: updateAgentConfigById(pageAgentId, model, provider) end HomeStore->>ChatStore: sendMessage(context agentId pageAgentId scope page, message) end HomeStore->>HomeStore: set inputActiveMode null HomeStore-->>ChatInput: return newDoc.id ChatInput-->>User: documentEditorShownWithPageAgent ``` #### Class diagram for updated Home ## Reviewer's Guide Adds emoji reaction support for messages, including metadata schema, CRUD actions to add/remove reactions, UI components to pick and display reactions, localization for the reaction action, and a context-engine processor that converts reactions into textual feedback injected into assistant messages. #### Sequence diagram for adding an emoji reaction to a message ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant MessageUI as MessageItem participant ReactionPicker participant MessageCRUD as MessageCRUDSlice participant Selectors as dataSelectors participant Store as updateMessageMetadata User->>MessageUI: Hover over message MessageUI->>ReactionPicker: Render trigger User->>ReactionPicker: Click add reaction ReactionPicker->>ReactionPicker: onSelect(emoji) ReactionPicker->>MessageUI: onSelect callback(emoji) MessageUI->>MessageCRUD: addReaction(messageId, emoji) MessageCRUD->>Selectors: getDisplayMessageById(messageId) Selectors-->>MessageCRUD: message with metadata.reactions MessageCRUD->>MessageCRUD: compute newReactions MessageCRUD->>Store: updateMessageMetadata(messageId, { reactions: newReactions }) Store-->>MessageCRUD: Promise resolved MessageCRUD-->>MessageUI: Promise MessageUI->>MessageUI: Rerender with updated reactions MessageUI-->>User: Updated reaction chips displayed ``` #### Sequence diagram for ReactionFeedbackProcessor injecting feedback into assistant messages ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Engine as ContextEnginePipeline participant Processor as ReactionFeedbackProcessor participant Context as PipelineContext Engine->>Processor: doProcess(context) Processor->>Processor: config.enabled check alt config disabled Processor->>Processor: markAsExecuted(context) Processor-->>Engine: context else config enabled Processor->>Processor: cloneContext(context) loop for each message in clonedContext.messages Processor->>Processor: check message.role and metadata.reactions alt message is assistant with reactions Processor->>Processor: convertReactionsToFeedback(reactions) Processor->>Processor: getEmojiSentiment for each emoji Processor->>Processor: build feedbackText alt feedbackText not empty and content is string Processor->>Context: append "[User Feedback: feedbackText]" to message.content Processor->>Processor: increment processedCount end end end Processor->>Context: set metadata.reactionFeedbackProcessed = processedCount Processor->>Processor: markAsExecuted(clonedContext) Processor-->>Engine: body:
### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/95e310d195ef0aaa1985421580d4b60178d982e4/src/features/DesktopFileMenuBridge/index.tsx#L25-L28 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Clear active topic when handling “New Topic”** When the File menu triggers `createNewTopic`, this handler only navigates to the agent route. If the user is already on that same agent, React Router won’t change the route and `AgentIdSync` only resets `activeTopicId` when the agent id changes, so the current topic is reused and no new conversation is created. This means the new menu item silently fails for the common case of “new topic” while staying in the same agent. Consider explicitly calling `useChatStore.getState().switchTopic(null, { skipRefreshMessage: true })` (or an equivalent new-topic action) before/after navigation.

## Reviewer's Guide Adjusts OpenAI response input conversion so that assistant message content only includes valid image parts with image_url, and adds a regression test for mixed OpenAI/Claude reasoning messages. #### Sequence diagram for filtering non image_url parts in convertOpenAIResponseInputs ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant convertOpenAIResponseInputs participant convertMessageContent Caller->>convertOpenAIResponseInputs: messages activate convertOpenAIResponseInputs loop for each message alt message.content is string convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->Caller: include content as string else message.content is array loop for each contentPart alt contentPart.type == text convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->convertOpenAIResponseInputs: map to type input_text else contentPart is non text convertOpenAIResponseInputs->>convertMessageContent: convertMessageContent(contentPart) activate convertMessageContent convertMessageContent-->>convertOpenAIResponseInputs: imagePart deactivate convertMessageContent alt imagePart.image_url.url exists convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->convertOpenAIResponseInputs: map to type input_image with image_url else imagePart.image_url.url missing convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->convertOpenAIResponseInputs: return undefined for this part end end end convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->convertOpenAIResponseInputs: filter(Boolean) to remove undefined parts convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->Caller: include filtered array content end end deactivate convertOpenAIResponseInputs ``` #### Class diagram for updated OpenAI response input conversion ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +string role +string~string_or_parts~ content +ReasoningMetadata reasoning } class ReasoningMetadata { +string content +number duration +string signature } class MessageContentPart { +string type +string text +ImageUrl image_url +string signature +string thinking } class ImageUrl { +string url } class ResponseInputItem { +string role +string~string_or_parts~ content +string type +SummaryPart[] summary } class SummaryPart { +string type %% e.g. summary_text +string text } class OpenAIContextConverter { +Promise~ResponseInputItem[]~ convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages) +Promise~MessageContentPart~ convertMessageContent(contentPart) } OpenAIChatMessage "1" --> "*" MessageContentPart : content_parts MessageContentPart "0..1" --> "1" ImageUrl : image ResponseInputItem "0..1" --> "*" MessageContentPart : content_parts ResponseInputItem "0..1" --> "*" SummaryPart : summary OpenAIContextConverter ..> OpenAIChatMessage : reads OpenAIContextConverter ..> ResponseInputItem : produces OpenAIContextConverter ..> MessageContentPart : maps_and_filters ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Update OpenAI response input conversion to skip non-image parts when constructing input_image entries and to normalize text/image content via an intermediate variable. |
  • Introduce processedContent to pre-process message.content before constructing the final item.
  • Convert text parts to input_text as before, but run them through the new processedContent pipeline.
  • Call convertMessageContent for non-text parts and return undefined when the resulting image part has no image_url.url.
  • Filter out undefined entries from processedContent before assigning to item.content, preventing input_image entries without image_url.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/openai.ts` | | Add a regression test to cover mixed OpenAI and Claude reasoning messages and validate converted result shape. |
  • Define a mixed message sequence including system, user, and assistant messages with reasoning metadata and thinking/text parts.
  • Call convertOpenAIResponseInputs with the mixed messages.
  • Assert that the converted output maps system to developer, preserves user content, extracts reasoning summary, and formats assistant reply as input_text without image parts.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Switches SSO provider account linking to use the generic OAuth2 `oauth2.link` API for non-built-in providers while retaining `linkSocial` for built-in ones, and exposes `oauth2` from the auth client. #### Sequence diagram for the updated SSO provider account linking flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant SSOProvidersList participant AuthClient participant LinkSocialAPI participant OAuth2LinkAPI User->>SSOProvidersList: clickLinkSSO(provider) SSOProvidersList->>SSOProvidersList: handleLinkSSO(provider) SSOProvidersList->>SSOProvidersList: guard enableAuthActions alt Auth actions disabled SSOProvidersList-->>User: no action else Auth actions enabled SSOProvidersList->>SSOProvidersList: normalizedProvider = normalizeProviderId(provider) SSOProvidersList->>AuthClient: import linkSocial, oauth2 alt Builtin provider SSOProvidersList->>LinkSocialAPI: linkSocial(callbackURL:/profile, provider:normalizedProvider) LinkSocialAPI-->>SSOProvidersList: account linked else Generic OIDC provider SSOProvidersList->>OAuth2LinkAPI: oauth2.link(callbackURL:/profile, providerId:normalizedProvider) OAuth2LinkAPI-->>SSOProvidersList: account linked end SSOProvidersList-->>User: redirected to /profile end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Adjust SSO linking logic to distinguish between built-in and generic OIDC providers and route to the appropriate linking API. |

  • Normalize the provider identifier before use to ensure consistent handling across built-in and generic providers.

  • Use `linkSocial` with the normalized provider for built-in providers and keep the callback URL pointing to the profile page.
  • Call `oauth2.link` with the normalized provider ID and profile callback URL for non-built-in (generic OIDC) providers.

  • Introduce a new Jest test suite exercising buildOidcConfig across happy-path and failure scenarios
  • Verify default OIDC behavior such as scopes, PKCE-related settings, and derived configuration values
  • Test issuer URL normalization, including handling of trailing slashes, whitespace, and .well-known discovery paths
  • Cover validation failures for missing or invalid inputs such as empty client credentials and whitespace-only values
  • Assert support for configuration overrides and provider-specific configurations for major IdPs like Google, Azure AD, and Keycloak

## Reviewer's Guide Implements multiple fixes and refinements around the Resource Manager write flow, desktop Electron build and menu integration, skill store UX, and i18n/static resource loading, plus adds an end‑to‑end scenario for Home starter write and cleans up unused starter image mode. #### Sequence diagram for Home starter write-to-page flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant HomePage participant HomeStarterList participant HomeInputStore participant DocumentService participant Router participant AgentStore participant ChatStore participant PageEditor User->>HomePage: Open Home HomePage->>HomeStarterList: Render starter buttons User->>HomeStarterList: Click write button HomeStarterList->>HomeInputStore: setInputActiveMode(write) User->>HomePage: Type prompt "帮我写一篇关于人工智能的文章" User->>HomePage: Press Enter HomePage->>HomeInputStore: useSend() HomeInputStore->>HomeInputStore: inputActiveMode === write HomeInputStore->>HomeInputStore: sendAsWrite(message) HomeInputStore->>AgentStore: getAgentStoreState() AgentStore-->>HomeInputStore: inboxAgentId, pageAgentId, inboxConfig(model,provider) HomeInputStore->>DocumentService: createDocument({ editorData: "{}", fileType: "custom/document", title: message.slice(0,50) }) DocumentService-->>HomeInputStore: newDoc(id) HomeInputStore->>Router: navigate(/page/{newDoc.id}) Router-->>PageEditor: Mount page editor for newDoc HomeInputStore->>AgentStore: updateAgentConfigById(pageAgentId,{model,provider}) AgentStore-->>HomeInputStore: updated pageAgent config HomeInputStore->>ChatStore: sendMessage({ context:{agentId:pageAgentId,scope:page}, message }) ChatStore-->>PageEditor: Deliver user message to Page Agent PageEditor-->>User: Show Page Agent conversation and generated content ``` #### Sequence diagram for desktop File menu shortcuts to renderer actions ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ElectronMenu as ElectronMainMenu participant BrowserMgr as BrowserManager participant MainWindow participant Renderer as RendererApp participant Bridge as DesktopFileMenuBridge participant CreateMenu as useCreateMenuItems participant Router User->>ElectronMenu: Select File > New Page ElectronMenu->>BrowserMgr: getMainWindow() BrowserMgr-->>ElectronMenu: mainWindow ElectronMenu->>MainWindow: show() ElectronMenu->>MainWindow: broadcast(createNewPage) MainWindow-->>Renderer: IPC createNewPage Renderer->>Bridge: useWatchBroadcast(createNewPage) Bridge->>CreateMenu: createPage() CreateMenu-->>Router: navigate to new page editor Router-->>User: Display blank page editor User->>ElectronMenu: Select File > New Topic ElectronMenu->>BrowserMgr: getMainWindow() BrowserMgr-->>ElectronMenu: mainWindow ElectronMenu->>MainWindow: show() ElectronMenu->>MainWindow: broadcast(createNewTopic) MainWindow-->>Renderer: IPC createNewTopic Renderer->>Bridge: useWatchBroadcast(createNewTopic) Bridge->>CreateMenu: compute target agentId CreateMenu->>Router: navigate(SESSION_CHAT_URL(agentId,false)) Router-->>User: Show new chat topic for agent ``` #### Class diagram for SkillStore detail and tool fetching ```mermaid classDiagram class SkillDetailInner { +type: string +activeTab: TabKey +render() } class Header { +type: string +handleConnectWithTracking() -renderIcon() -renderConnectButton() } class Nav { +activeTab: TabKey +setActiveTab(tab) } class Overview { +render() } class Schema { +mode: ModeType +activeKey: string[] +setMode(mode) +setActiveKey(keys) } class DetailContext { <> +author: string +authorUrl: string +description: string +icon: any +identifier: string +introduction: string +isConnected: boolean +label: string +localizedDescription: string +localizedIntroduction: string +serverName: string +tools: Tool[] +toolsLoading: boolean } class LobehubDetailProvider { +identifier: string +children: ReactNode +value: DetailContextValue } class KlavisDetailProvider { +identifier: string +serverName: McpServerName +children: ReactNode +value: DetailContextValue } class useSkillConnect { <> +handleConnect() +isConnecting: boolean +isConnected: boolean } class ToolStore { <> +useFetchProviderTools(provider): SWRResponse +useFetchServerTools(serverName): SWRResponse } class toolsClient_klavis { +getTools.query(params) } class toolsClient_market { +connectListTools.query(params) } class KlavisSkillDetailContent { +identifier: string +serverName: McpServerName } class LobehubSkillDetailContent { +identifier: string } class createKlavisSkillDetailModal { +createKlavisSkillDetailModal(options) } class createLobehubSkillDetailModal { +createLobehubSkillDetailModal(options) } class SkillStore_SkillList_LobeHub_useSkillConnect { } DetailContext <.. ### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/c5925164dba6f9089a60bc9963380e65259bd729/src/store/home/slices/homeInput/action.ts#L199-L202 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Preserve per-document page chat isolation** Using `pageAgentId` for the page scope context means the message map key collapses to a single `page_` bucket when no `topicId` is set (see `messageMapKey` in `src/store/chat/utils/messageMapKey.ts`). That makes the initial “write” message for a newly created document land in the same conversation as other pages, so users can see prior page history bleed into new documents. Previously this was isolated by using the document ID as the `agentId`. Consider including the new document ID (e.g., as `agentId` or `topicId`) so each page gets its own conversation history.

body:
## Reviewer's Guide This PR introduces a new shared SSE fetch package, hardens media fetching against SSRF, adds structured reasoning support for DeepSeek/OpenAI-style messages, updates Ollama and multiple providers to use the new utilities, and bumps core dependencies and docs for the 1.143.2 release. #### Sequence diagram for DeepSeek reasoning handling and OpenAI response inputs ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant MessageCleanupProcessor as MessageCleanup participant DeepSeekChat as DeepSeek_params.chatCompletion participant OpenAIContext as OpenAI_convertOpenAIResponseInputs Client->>MessageCleanupProcessor: raw OpenAIChatMessage[] (with reasoning) MessageCleanupProcessor-->>Client: cleaned messages (reasoning preserved) Client->>DeepSeekChat: payload { messages, model, stream? } activate DeepSeekChat DeepSeekChat->>DeepSeekChat: map messages alt message has reasoning.content DeepSeekChat-->>Client: payload with messages.reasoning_content else reasoning without content DeepSeekChat-->>Client: payload with reasoning removed end deactivate DeepSeekChat Client->>OpenAIContext: convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages) activate OpenAIContext loop for each message alt message.reasoning.content exists OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: push ResponseReasoningItem end alt role == assistant and tool_calls OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: push function type items else role == tool OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: push tool_output items else role == system OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: push developer role item else OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: push default message item end OpenAIContext->>OpenAIContext: delete reasoning from item end OpenAIContext-->>Client: OpenAI.Responses.ResponseInputItem[] deactivate OpenAIContext ``` #### Sequence diagram for SSRF-safe media URL to Base64 conversion ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UserCode as ProviderOrContextBuilder participant ImageUtils as imageUrlToBase64 participant SSRFNode as ssrfSafeFetch_node participant SSRFBrowser as fetch_browser UserCode->>ImageUtils: imageUrlToBase64(imageUrl) activate ImageUtils ImageUtils->>ImageUtils: detect isServer alt isServer == true ImageUtils->>SSRFNode: ssrfSafeFetch(imageUrl) SSRFNode-->>ImageUtils: Response else browser ImageUtils->>SSRFBrowser: fetch(imageUrl) SSRFBrowser-->>ImageUtils: Response end ImageUtils->>ImageUtils: blob() and arrayBuffer() alt isServer ImageUtils->>ImageUtils: Buffer.from(arrayBuffer).toString(base64) else browser ImageUtils->>ImageUtils: btoa(from Uint8Array) end ImageUtils-->>UserCode: { base64, mimeType } deactivate ImageUtils ``` #### Class diagram for updated chat message and reasoning flow types ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +UserMessageContentPart[] content +string role string name string tool_call_id MessageToolCall[] tool_calls ReasoningMeta reasoning } class ReasoningMeta { string content number duration } class MessageCleanupProcessor { +process(messages: OpenAIChatMessage[]) OpenAIChatMessage[] } class DeepSeekParams { +DeepSeekChatCompletionConfig chatCompletion } class DeepSeekChatCompletionConfig { +handlePayload(payload: ChatCompletionPayload) ChatCompletionPayload } class ChatCompletionPayload { OpenAIChatMessage[] messages string model boolean stream } class OpenAIContextBuilder { +convertOpenAIMessages(messages: ChatCompletionMessageParam[]) ChatCompletionMessageParam[] +convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages: OpenAIChatMessage[]) ResponseInputItem[] } class ResponseInputItem { string type string role string content } class ResponseReasoningItem { string type ReasoningSummary[] summary } class ReasoningSummary { string type string text } MessageCleanupProcessor --> OpenAIChatMessage : preserves reasoning OpenAIChatMessage --> ReasoningMeta DeepSeekParams --> DeepSeekChatCompletionConfig : chatCompletion DeepSeekChatCompletionConfig --> ChatCompletionPayload : transforms ChatCompletionPayload --> OpenAIChatMessage OpenAIContextBuilder --> OpenAIChatMessage : input OpenAIContextBuilder --> ResponseInputItem : output ResponseReasoningItem --> ReasoningSummary OpenAIContextBuilder --> ResponseReasoningItem : adds for reasoning ``` #### Class diagram for new fetch-sse and SSRF-safe media fetching ```mermaid classDiagram class FetchSSEModule { +fetchSSE(url: string, options: FetchSSEOptions) Promise~void~ +getMessageError(response: ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a comprehensive Vitest test suite for the markdownToTxt utility, covering basic markdown stripping, complex/nested structures, edge cases, error handling behavior, real-world content, and whitespace handling to lock in current behavior and improve confidence in future refactors. #### Sequence diagram for executing a markdownToTxt unit test ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Dev participant Vitest participant markdownToTxt Dev->>Vitest: run test markdownToTxt basic markdown conversion Vitest->>markdownToTxt: markdownToTxt('# Heading 1') markdownToTxt-->>Vitest: 'Heading 1' Vitest->>Vitest: expect(result).toBe('Heading 1') Vitest-->>Dev: report test passed ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add comprehensive unit tests for markdownToTxt behavior across markdown features, edge cases, and real-world usage. |
  • Introduce a Vitest test suite organized into describe blocks for basic markdown conversion, complex markdown, edge cases, error handling, real-world examples, and whitespace handling.
  • Verify that common markdown constructs (headers, bold, italics, links, images, lists, blockquotes, code blocks, tables, horizontal rules) are converted to expected plain-text representations or stripped.
  • Assert behavior for empty and whitespace-only input, very long input, special characters, unicode, and emoji to ensure stable output and trimming behavior.
  • Test error-handling and defensive behavior, including malformed markdown and null/undefined inputs returning safe values instead of throwing.

data: { id: predictionId } } Submit-->>Img: predictionId Img->>Poll: asyncifyPolling(checkStatus, pollingQuery, options) loop Until completed or failed Poll->>Query: pollingQuery(predictionId, message group ID. #### Sequence diagram for cancelling a compressed message group ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as CompressedGroupMessage participant Store as ConversationStore participant FEsvc as FrontendMessageService participant Lambda as lambdaClient_message participant Router as messageRouter_cancelCompression participant BEsvc as ServerMessageService participant Repo as CompressionRepository participant Model as MessageModel User->>UI: Click Uncompress button UI->>UI: modal.confirm UI->>Store: cancelCompression(id) Store->>Store: getDisplayMessageById(id) Store->>Store: validate compressedGroup and context Store->>FEsvc: cancelCompression({agentId, groupId, messageGroupId, threadId, topicId}) FEsvc->>Lambda: message.cancelCompression.mutate(params) Lambda->>Router: cancelCompression(input) Router->>BEsvc: cancelCompression(messageGroupId, context) BEsvc->>Repo: deleteCompressionGroup(messageGroupId) Repo-->>BEsvc: success BEsvc->>Model: query(context, getQueryOptions()) Model-->>BEsvc: messages BEsvc-->>Router: {messages, success: true} Router-->>Lambda: {messages} Lambda-->>FEsvc: {messages} FEsvc-->>Store: {messages} Store->>Store: replaceMessages(messages) Store-->>UI: state updated UI-->>User: Original messages restored ``` #### ER diagram for messages table index on messageGroupId ```mermaid erDiagram messages { id uuid PK content text threadId uuid agentId uuid groupId uuid messageGroupId uuid } %% New index on messageGroupId to optimize queries restoring original messages ``` #### Class diagram for cancelCompression feature across layers ```mermaid classDiagram class CompressedGroupMessage { +id string +handleCancelCompression() void } class ConversationStore { +context any +replaceMessages(messages UIChatMessage[]) void +cancelCompression(id string) Promise~void~ } class FrontendMessageService { +cancelCompression(params CancelCompressionParams) Promise~CancelCompressionResult~ } class   • Create AgentItem component rendering a compact outlined block with avatar, title, and single-line description for agents, guarding against missing identifier or title.
  • Define agentListStyles and itemStyles to control grid widths, wrapping, spacing, and text truncation for agent items.
  • Add VirtuosoLoading component dedicated to showing a centered spinning loader icon for virtuoso-based lists.
| `src/features/SkillStore/SkillDetail/AgentItem.tsx`
`src/features/SkillStore/SkillDetail/style.ts`
`src/features/SkillStore/SkillDetail/VirtuosoLoading.tsx` | | Update SkillStore SkillDetail agents list to use new AgentItem, list styles, and adjusted loading skeletons. |

  • Increase PAGE_SIZE from 6 to 12 to load more agents per page.
  • Adjust initial loading state skeletons to use smaller gap, add avatar placeholder, and reduce paragraph rows to match the new compact item layout.
  • Wire VirtuosoGrid itemClassName and listClassName to the new agentListStyles.item and .list classes.

  • Remove duplicated inline AgentItem and style definitions in favor of reusing SkillStore/SkillDetail AgentItem and agentListStyles.
  • Increase PAGE_SIZE from 6 to 12 for MCP plugin agents as well.
  • Update initial loading state skeletons to match the new compact layout (smaller gaps, avatar skeleton, single-row paragraph).

## Reviewer's Guide This PR bumps the app version and core dependencies, centralizes SSRF-safe media fetching and SSE utilities into dedicated packages, adds structured handling of model reasoning fields (especially for DeepSeek) across providers, and updates docs and tests accordingly. #### Sequence diagram for DeepSeek chatCompletion handlePayload reasoning transformation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI participant ChatService participant ModelRuntime as ModelRuntime participant DeepSeekProvider as DeepSeekProvider participant DeepSeekAPI as DeepSeek_API User ->> ChatUI: Send message ChatUI ->> ChatService: ChatStreamPayload ChatService ->> ModelRuntime: chat(payload) ModelRuntime ->> DeepSeekProvider: chatCompletion(payload) Note over DeepSeekProvider: params.chatCompletion.handlePayload DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekProvider: iterate messages DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekProvider: if message.reasoning.content DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekProvider: set reasoning_content = reasoning.content DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekProvider: remove reasoning field DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekProvider: set stream = payload.stream or true DeepSeekProvider ->> DeepSeekAPI: POST /chat DeepSeekAPI -->> DeepSeekProvider: streaming response DeepSeekProvider -->> ModelRuntime: tokens ModelRuntime -->> ChatService: tokens ChatService -->> ChatUI: render streaming reply ``` #### Updated class diagram for chat message reasoning handling ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +string content +LLMRoleType role +string name +MessageToolCall[] tool_calls +string tool_call_id +Reasoning reasoning } class Reasoning { +string content +number duration } class MessageCleanupProcessor { +process(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) OpenAIChatMessage[] } class convertOpenAIMessages { +convertOpenAIMessages(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) Promise~OpenAIChatMessage[]~ } class convertOpenAIResponseInputs { +convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) Promise~ResponseInputItem[]~ } class DeepSeekChatCompletionParams { +handlePayload(payload ChatCompletionPayload) ChatCompletionPayload } class ChatCompletionPayload { +OpenAIChatMessage[] messages +string model +boolean stream } class ResponseInputItem { } class ResponseReasoningItem { +summary SummaryText[] +string type } class SummaryText { +string text +string type } OpenAIChatMessage --> Reasoning MessageCleanupProcessor --> OpenAIChatMessage : preserves.reasoning convertOpenAIMessages --> OpenAIChatMessage : input convertOpenAIMessages --> OpenAIChatMessage : output convertOpenAIResponseInputs --> OpenAIChatMessage : input convertOpenAIResponseInputs --> ResponseInputItem : output convertOpenAIResponseInputs ..> ResponseReasoningItem : creates ResponseReasoningItem --> SummaryText DeepSeekChatCompletionParams --> ChatCompletionPayload : handlePayload ChatCompletionPayload --> OpenAIChatMessage class DeepSeekBehavior { +strip reasoning from request messages +map reasoning.content to reasoning_content +default stream true when undefined } DeepSeekChatCompletionParams ..> DeepSeekBehavior ``` #### Updated class diagram for LobeOllamaAI image and content conversion ```mermaid classDiagram class LobeOllamaAI { -client OllamaClient +chat(payload ChatStreamPayload, options ChatOptions) Promise~void~ -buildOllamaMessages(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) Promise~OllamaMessage[]~ -convertContentToOllamaMessage(message OpenAIChatMessage) Promise~OllamaMessage~ } class OpenAIChatMessage { +string|UserMessageContentPart[] content +string role } class UserMessageContentPart { +string type } class TextPart { +string type +string text } class ImageUrlPart { +string type +ImageUrl image_url } class ImageUrl { +string url } class OllamaMessage { +string content +string role +string[] images } class parseDataUri { +parseDataUri(value string) ParsedUri } class ParsedUri { +string mimeType +string base64 +string type } class imageUrlToBase64 { +imageUrlToBase64(url string) Promise~ImageBase64Result~ } class ImageBase64Result { +string base64 +string mimeType } LobeOllamaAI --> OpenAIChatMessage LobeOllamaAI --> OllamaMessage LobeOllamaAI --> parseDataUri LobeOllamaAI --> imageUrlToBase64 OpenAIChatMessage --> UserMessageContentPart UserMessageContentPart <|-- TextPart UserMessageContentPart <|-- ImageUrlPart ImageUrlPart --> ImageUrl parseDataUri --> ParsedUri imageUrlToBase64 --> ImageBase64Result ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Centralize image URL → base64 handling with SSRF-safe fetch and propagate to providers. |
  • Replace model-runtime imageUrlToBase64 import with @lobechat/utils implementation that conditionally uses ssrf-safe-fetch on the server and native fetch in the browser.
  • Update Google, Anthropic, BFL, and other provider/image creation code to use the shared imageUrlToBase64 helper for both images and videos, removing the old model-runtime imageToBase64 util and its tests.
  • Adjust tests to mock @lobechat/utils.imageUrlToBase64 and uriParser consistently, and change some Vitest environments from edge-runtime to node where needed.

## Reviewer's Guide Refactors the SPA navigation migration script for clarity and removes now-unneeded duplicate AddTopicButon components from agent and group layouts, while slightly tightening the regex used to detect and replace navigation imports. #### Flow diagram for migrate_spa_navigation hook migration logic ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start migrateFile for SPA file] --> B[Read file content] B --> C{Match import from @/libs/next/navigation} C -->|No match| Z[Return null] C -->|Match found| D[Extract imported hooks] D --> E[Initialize changes and newImports] E --> F{Iterate over each hook} F -->|usePathname| G[Add usePathname import from React Router hooks and record change] F -->|useSearchParams| H[Add useSearchParams import from React Router hooks and record change] F -->|useRouter| I[Add useRouter import from React Router hooks and record change] F -->|Other hook| J[Log unknown hook and keep original next/navigation import] G --> K{More hooks?} H --> K I --> K J --> K K -->|Yes| F K -->|No| L[Remove original next/navigation import line] L --> M[Insert new React Router based hook imports] M --> N{Content changed?} N -->|No| Z N -->|Yes| O[Write updated content back to file] O --> P[Return MigrationResult] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refactor migrate-spa-navigation script for readability and simplify imports/regexes while preserving behavior. |
  • Remove unused relative import helper from node:path in favor of only dirname and join
  • Remove an obsolete SPA_FILES entry for the deleted AddTopicButon component so the script no longer tries to migrate it

  • Align the replacement regex for rewriting imports with the new detection regex and formatting

### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/30c14e32bca2153bee51a69e5608946575db1dec/src/app/[variants]/(main)/community/(detail)/user/features/UserAgentList.tsx#L53-L54 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Add favoriteAgents to memo deps to avoid stale favorites** When the user switches to the “favorite” status, the memoized filter uses `favoriteAgents`, but the dependency list omits it. If `favoriteAgents` arrives or changes asynchronously (common for profile data), the component re-renders but `filteredAgents` stays stuck on the old memo value, so the favorites tab can appear empty until another dependency changes. Include `favoriteAgents` in the dependency array to keep results in sync. --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/30c14e32bca2153bee51a69e5608946575db1dec/src/app/[variants]/(main)/community/(detail)/user/features/UserGroupList.tsx#L51-L52 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Add favoriteAgentGroups to memo deps to avoid stale lists** The filtered groups memo uses `favoriteAgentGroups` but the dependency list doesn’t include it. If a profile loads favorites after initial render, `filteredGroups` won’t recompute and the “favorite” filter can remain empty until some other dependency changes. Adding `favoriteAgentGroups` to the dependency list fixes the stale memo behavior. --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/30c14e32bca2153bee51a69e5608946575db1dec/src/app/[variants]/(main)/community/(detail)/user/features/UserAgentList.tsx#L61-L64 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Avoid setState inside useMemo during render** This `useMemo` is used for a side effect (`setCurrentPage(1)`), which runs during render. In React this triggers a “state update during render” warning and can cause extra render loops (especially in Strict Mode) whenever the filter/search changes. This should be a `useEffect` tied to `[statusFilter, searchQuery]` instead.

body:
## Reviewer's Guide Adds defensive array type checks and safer parameter handling to several builtin tool inspectors and the notebook executor to prevent `.map is not a function` runtime errors when receiving malformed or incomplete parameters from AI agent responses. #### Sequence diagram for notebook executor create and update with validation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant AIAgent participant NotebookExecutor participant NotebookService User->>AIAgent: Request create notebook document AIAgent->>NotebookExecutor: execute createDocument(params) Note over NotebookExecutor: Validate and default parameters NotebookExecutor->>NotebookExecutor: content = params.content || '' NotebookExecutor->>NotebookExecutor: description = params.description || params.title || '' NotebookExecutor->>NotebookExecutor: title = params.title || 'Untitled Document' NotebookExecutor->>NotebookService: createDocument({content, description, title, topicId, type}) NotebookService-->>NotebookExecutor: document NotebookExecutor-->>AIAgent: { content: documentContent, success: true } AIAgent-->>User: Shows created document User->>AIAgent: Request update notebook document AIAgent->>NotebookExecutor: execute updateDocument(params) alt Missing id NotebookExecutor-->>AIAgent: { content: Cannot update document: document id is required, success: false } AIAgent-->>User: Shows error message else Valid id NotebookExecutor->>NotebookService: updateDocument(params) NotebookService-->>NotebookExecutor: updatedDocument NotebookExecutor-->>AIAgent: { content: updatedContent, success: true } AIAgent-->>User: Shows updated document end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Harden GTD Inspectors against non-array args to avoid `.map` errors. |
  • Replace falsy-coalescing patterns for `tasks`, `adds`, `items`, and `operations` with `Array.isArray`-based selection between `args`, `partialArgs`, and a safe empty-array default.
  • Ensure derived counts and iterations always operate on confirmed arrays in GTD inspectors.
| `packages/builtin-tool-gtd/src/client/Inspector/ExecTasks/index.tsx`
`packages/builtin-tool-gtd/src/client/Inspector/CreateTodos/index.tsx`
`packages/builtin-tool-gtd/src/client/Inspector/UpdateTodos/index.tsx` | | Harden Knowledge Base Inspector against non-array `fileIds`. |
  • Replace falsy-coalescing on `fileIds` with `Array.isArray` checks over `args.fileIds` and `partialArgs.fileIds`, defaulting to `[]` to guarantee safe `.map` usage.
| `packages/builtin-tool-knowledge-base/src/client/Inspector/ReadKnowledge/index.tsx` | | Make notebook executor robust to missing or invalid document parameters. |
  • Introduce defaults for `content`, `description`, and `title` when creating documents so missing fields do not cause runtime issues.
  • Add early validation for required `id` when updating documents, returning a structured failure instead of calling the service with an invalid payload.
| `packages/builtin-tool-notebook/src/executor/index.ts` | | Make topic mutation logic robust to unexpected non-array data in chat topic slice. |
  • Guard the `groups` argument with an `Array.isArray` check before mapping to avoid `.map` calls on non-arrays.
  • Defensively coalesce `group.topics` to an empty array before mapping to prevent runtime errors when `topics` is undefined or non-array.
| `src/store/chat/slices/topic/action.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#Bug: TypeError - h.map is not a function in favoriteTopic**: PR updates favoriteTopic with Array.isArray and topics fallback, exactly matching the issue’s described root cause and fix. ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

## Reviewer's Guide Adds centralized tRPC payload size validation utilities and applies them across key routers (user, importer, session, message, plugin, agent) to enforce byte-size limits on JSON / passthrough data, base64 avatars, and settings, plus localized error messaging and unit tests. #### Sequence diagram for tRPC request with payload size validation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Client participant TrpcRouter participant ZodSchema participant PayloadSizeValidator as PayloadSizeUtils.withPayloadSizeLimit participant ErrorFormatter Client->>TrpcRouter: send request with input payload TrpcRouter->>ZodSchema: parse(input) ZodSchema->>PayloadSizeValidator: superRefine(input) PayloadSizeValidator->>PayloadSizeValidator: getByteSize(input) alt payload within limit PayloadSizeValidator-->>ZodSchema: ok ZodSchema-->>TrpcRouter: parsedInput TrpcRouter->>TrpcRouter: execute resolver TrpcRouter-->>Client: success response else payload exceeds limit PayloadSizeValidator-->>ZodSchema: addIssue(PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) ZodSchema-->>TrpcRouter: ZodError with custom issue TrpcRouter->>ErrorFormatter: map ZodError to response ErrorFormatter-->>Client: error response Note right of Client: message key response.payloadTooLarge end ``` #### Class diagram for tRPC payload size validators and router integration ```mermaid classDiagram class PayloadSizeLimits { <> +AVATAR_BASE64: number +DEFAULT_JSONB: number +IMPORT_DATA: number +LARGE_JSONB: number +MESSAGE_METADATA: number +PLUGIN_MANIFEST: number +PLUGIN_SETTINGS: number +SESSION_CONFIG: number +USER_SETTINGS: number } class PayloadSizeUtils { <> +withPayloadSizeLimit(schema, maxSize, fieldName): ZodEffects +passthroughObjectWithLimit(maxSize, fieldName): ZodObject +passthroughPartialWithLimit(maxSize, fieldName): ZodObject +stringWithByteLimit(maxBytes, fieldName): ZodString +nullablePassthroughWithLimit(maxSize, fieldName): ZodNullable +anyWithLimit(maxSize, fieldName): ZodAny -formatBytes(bytes): string -getByteSize(value): number } class UserRouter { +updateAvatar(input) +updateSettings(input) } class ImporterRouter { +importByPost(input) +importPgByPost(input) } class SessionRouter { +batchCreateSessions(input) +updateSessionConfig(input) } class MessageRouter { +updateMessageMetadata(input) +updateMessagePluginError(input) +updateMessagePluginState(input) +updateMessageContentAndPluginData(input) } class PluginRouter { +createOrInstallPlugin(input) +createPlugin(input) +updatePlugin(input) } class AgentRouter { +createAgentOnly(input) +updateAgentConfig(input) } PayloadSizeUtils --> PayloadSizeLimits : uses UserRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses stringWithByteLimit UserRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses withPayloadSizeLimit ImporterRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses withPayloadSizeLimit SessionRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses withPayloadSizeLimit SessionRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses passthroughPartialWithLimit MessageRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses passthroughObjectWithLimit MessageRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses anyWithLimit MessageRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses nullablePassthroughWithLimit PluginRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses anyWithLimit AgentRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses passthroughObjectWithLimit AgentRouter ..> PayloadSizeUtils : uses passthroughPartialWithLimit ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce reusable Zod-based payload size validator utilities and limits for various payload types. |
  • Add PAYLOAD_SIZE_LIMITS constants defining per-type byte caps (avatars, imports, JSONB configs, plugin data, user settings, etc.).
  • Implement generic withPayloadSizeLimit wrapper that uses superRefine and JSON byte-size measurement for arbitrary Zod schemas.
  • Add helper factories (passthroughObjectWithLimit, passthroughPartialWithLimit, nullablePassthroughWithLimit, stringWithByteLimit, anyWithLimit) for common payload patterns.
  • Provide human-readable byte formatting and structured error params (actualSize, maxSize, code) for localization / handling.
| `src/libs/trpc/validators/payloadSize.ts` | | Apply payload size limits to user-related payloads, including avatar uploads and settings. |
  • Wrap updateAvatar input with stringWithByteLimit using AVATAR_BASE64 limit and field name 'avatar'.
  • Wrap updateSettings input schema with withPayloadSizeLimit using USER_SETTINGS limit and field name 'settings' while preserving keyVaults encryption flow.
  • Keep existing avatar upload-to-S3 logic unchanged apart from new validation on the input string.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/user.ts` | | Enforce payload limits on import endpoints to cap bulk import sizes. |
  • Wrap importByPost input schema in withPayloadSizeLimit using IMPORT_DATA and field name 'importData'.
  • Wrap importPgByPost input schema in withPayloadSizeLimit using IMPORT_DATA and field name 'importPgData'.
  • Leave importer service behavior unchanged, only guarding incoming payload size.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/importer.ts` | | Constrain session-related payloads, including bulk session creation and per-session config updates. |
  • Wrap batchCreateSessions array input with withPayloadSizeLimit using IMPORT_DATA and field name 'sessions'.
  • Replace generic passthrough config for updateSessionWithId.value with passthroughPartialWithLimit using SESSION_CONFIG and field name 'sessionConfig'.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/session.ts` | | Add size limits to various message metadata, plugin error, and plugin state payloads. |
  • Constrain message metadata updates to passthroughObjectWithLimit with MESSAGE_METADATA limit.
  • Constrain pluginError fields via anyWithLimit using DEFAULT_JSONB limit, including nullable and optional variants where used.
  • Constrain pluginState fields via passthroughObjectWithLimit using DEFAULT_JSONB limit across individual update endpoints and batch updates.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/message.ts` | | Limit plugin router payload fields (settings, manifest, custom params). |
  • Import PAYLOAD_SIZE_LIMITS and anyWithLimit into plugin router.
  • Apply PLUGIN_SETTINGS limit to customParams/settings and PLUGIN_MANIFEST limit to manifest for createOrInstallPlugin, createPlugin, and updatePlugin inputs.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/plugin.ts` | | Restrict agent configuration payload size for creation and updates. |
  • Wrap createAgentOnly.config in passthroughObjectWithLimit using LARGE_JSONB and field name 'agentConfig'.
  • Wrap updateAgentConfig.value in passthroughPartialWithLimit using LARGE_JSONB and field name 'agentConfig'.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/agent.ts` | | Add localized error message for payload-too-large responses. |
  • Introduce response.payloadTooLarge translation string with placeholders for actualSize and maxSize.
| `src/locales/default/error.ts` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Enhances the Scheduled Task user guide (EN and zh-CN) with step-by-step creation instructions, new UI screenshots, task pause behavior, delete semantics, and illustrative use cases for scheduled tasks. #### State diagram for scheduled task status (active, paused, deleted) ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> NotCreated NotCreated --> Active: Create_task Active --> Active: Edit_configuration Active --> Paused: Pause_task Paused --> Active: Resume_task Active --> CompletedByMaxExecutions: Max_execution_count_reached CompletedByMaxExecutions --> Active: Increase_max_execution_count Active --> Deleted: Delete_task Paused --> Deleted: Delete_task CompletedByMaxExecutions --> Deleted: Delete_task Deleted --> [*] ``` #### Flow diagram for scheduled task lifecycle and user actions ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Open agent conversation page] --> B[Locate Scheduled Tasks in left panel] B --> C[Click Add Scheduled Task] C --> D[Fill task name] D --> E[Set task frequency and execution time] E --> F[Set maximum execution count] F --> G[Configure task content Prompt and plugin usage] G --> H[Save scheduled task] H --> I[Task waits until scheduled time] I --> J[Task executes Prompt and plugins] J --> K{More executions remaining?} K -- Yes --> I K -- No --> L[Task stops due to max executions reached] H --> M[User can edit task configuration anytime] M --> H H --> N[User pauses task] N --> O[System preserves plan and Prompt but stops auto execution] O --> P[User re-enables task] P --> I H --> Q[User deletes task] Q --> R[System removes plan and Prompt and stops all future executions] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Expand scheduled task creation instructions with UI entry point, configuration details, and updated screenshot. |
  • Describe how to access Scheduled Tasks from the Agent conversation left panel and start task creation via the Add Scheduled Task button.
  • Explain configurable fields on the creation page including task name, frequency, execution time, max runs, and task content.
  • Replace the old local image path with a new hosted Create Task screenshot URL.
  • Detail how to author task content (prompt/instructions, plugin usage) and note that each trigger fully executes this content and can be modified later.
| `docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.mdx`
`docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.zh-CN.mdx` | | Document task pause/disable behavior with supporting screenshot. |
  • Add a Pausing a Task/暂停任务 section explaining disabling a scheduled task while preserving its schedule and prompt configuration.
  • Clarify that re-enabling resumes automatic execution from the preserved configuration.
  • Insert a Pause Task/暂停任务 screenshot using a hosted image URL.
| `docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.mdx`
`docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.zh-CN.mdx` | | Clarify task deletion behavior and introduce practical use cases for scheduled tasks. |
  • Expand Deleting a Task/删除任务 section to state that schedule and prompt configuration are removed and no further executions occur after deletion.
  • Add a Use Cases/使用场景 section outlining when scheduled tasks are appropriate (fixed cadence, continuous follow-up, periodic outputs).
  • Provide three concrete use case subsections: social media monitoring with notifications, periodic summaries/reports, and scheduled reminder notifications, in both English and Chinese guides.
| `docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.mdx`
`docs/usage/agent/scheduled-task.zh-CN.mdx` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#[Docs] Feedback for `usage/agent/scheduled-task`**: They both concern improving scheduled-task docs; the PR adds explicit deletion guidance addressing the feedback. - **#[Request] Support setting scheduled tasks with proactive result push**: PR documents scheduled tasks and proactive notification scenarios, directly addressing the requested scheduled tasks with result push. ---

## Reviewer's Guide Adds a comprehensive set of new unit tests for the textLength utilities, significantly expanding coverage of CJK/Unicode weighting and truncation behavior without modifying production logic. #### Class diagram for textLength utilities and expanded test coverage ```mermaid classDiagram class TextLengthUtils { +number calculateWeightedLength(text, cjkWeight) +string truncateByWeightedLength(text, maxWeightedLength, cjkWeight) } class TextLengthTests { +void test_ascii_and_special_characters() +void test_numbers_and_punctuation() +void test_cjk_compatibility_ideographs() +void test_cjk_extension_a() +void test_emoji_as_non_cjk() +void test_newlines_and_tabs_length() +void test_very_long_ascii_text() +void test_very_long_cjk_text() +void test_individual_ascii_characters() +void test_hangul_jamo_characters() +void test_truncate_cjk_boundaries() +void test_truncate_single_characters() +void test_truncate_negative_and_zero_limits() +void test_truncate_korean_hangul() +void test_truncate_japanese_characters() +void test_truncate_with_large_limit() +void test_truncate_mixed_numbers_and_specials() +void test_truncate_with_newlines_and_tabs() +void test_truncate_all_cjk_odd_limit() +void test_truncate_cjk_weight_one() +void test_truncate_very_large_custom_weight() } TextLengthTests --> TextLengthUtils ``` #### Flow diagram for truncateByWeightedLength decision logic as covered by tests ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start truncateByWeightedLength] --> B[Input text, maxWeightedLength, cjkWeight] B --> C{Is maxWeightedLength <= 0?} C -- Yes --> Z[Return empty string] C -- No --> D[Initialize totalWeight = 0 and result = empty] D --> E{More characters in text?} E -- No --> Y[Return result] E -- Yes --> F[Read next character] F --> G{Is character CJK?} G -- Yes --> H[charWeight = cjkWeight] G -- No --> I[charWeight = 1] H --> J I --> J J[Compute newWeight = totalWeight + charWeight] --> K{newWeight <= maxWeightedLength?} K -- Yes --> L[Append character to result] L --> M[totalWeight = newWeight] M --> E K -- No --> Y[Return result] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Expand calculateWeightedLength test coverage for diverse Unicode, CJK, and whitespace scenarios. |
  • Add tests for numbers, punctuation, and special symbols to validate they are treated as single-width characters
  • Add tests for CJK Compatibility Ideographs and CJK Extension A ranges to ensure they receive CJK weighting
  • Add tests confirming emoji are treated as non-CJK and counted with weight 1
  • Add tests covering newlines, tabs, and mixed CJK/ASCII content for correct aggregate weighted length
  • Add tests for very long ASCII and CJK strings to validate performance and length calculation at scale
  • Add tests for individual ASCII characters and Hangul Jamo characters to confirm weighting rules across edge Unicode ranges
| `src/utils/textLength.test.ts` | | Expand truncateByWeightedLength test coverage for boundary, CJK, and custom-weight truncation behavior. |
  • Add boundary tests to ensure no partial CJK characters are included at weighted limits
  • Add single-character and negative/zero max-length tests to define behavior for minimal and invalid limits
  • Add tests for Korean Hangul and Japanese Hiragana/Katakana truncation to confirm correct preservation at various limits
  • Add tests for very large max lengths to ensure inputs are returned unchanged when under limit
  • Add tests for mixed ASCII, CJK, numbers, special chars, and whitespace to verify consistent truncation semantics
  • Add tests for odd limits with even-weighted CJK characters, and for custom CJK weights including 1 and large values
| `src/utils/textLength.test.ts` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Fixes the OpenAI Responses API context builder so that tool call arguments are correctly propagated instead of incorrectly using the function name, and updates tests to reflect the correct behavior for function_call messages. #### Sequence diagram for OpenAI response tool_call conversion ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant convertOpenAIResponseInputs participant OpenAIMessage participant ToolCall participant ContextInputs Caller->>convertOpenAIResponseInputs: messages convertOpenAIResponseInputs->>OpenAIMessage: iterate messages OpenAIMessage-->>convertOpenAIResponseInputs: role assistant with tool_calls loop for each tool_call convertOpenAIResponseInputs->>ToolCall: read function ToolCall-->>convertOpenAIResponseInputs: function.name, function.arguments, id convertOpenAIResponseInputs->>ContextInputs: push { arguments: function.arguments, call_id: id, name: function.name, type: function_call } end convertOpenAIResponseInputs-->>Caller: ContextInputs ``` #### Class diagram for OpenAI response input conversion structures ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIMessage { +string role +string content +ToolCall[] tool_calls } class ToolCall { +string id +ToolFunction function } class ToolFunction { +string name +string arguments } class ContextInput { +string arguments +string call_id +string name +string type } class ContextBuilder { +convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages) Promise~ContextInput[]~ } OpenAIMessage "0..*" --> "0..*" ToolCall : has ToolCall "1" --> "1" ToolFunction : uses ContextBuilder --> ContextInput : creates ContextBuilder --> OpenAIMessage : processes ToolFunction --> ContextInput : maps_to_arguments ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Correct tool call argument mapping in OpenAI response context builder. |
  • Change function_call construction to use tool.function.arguments instead of tool.function.name for the arguments field.
  • Ensure call_id and name are still mapped from tool.id and tool.function.name respectively.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/openai.ts` | | Align tests with the corrected behavior of the OpenAI context builder for function_call arguments. |
  • Update expected arguments value for assistant tool call with JSON payload to match tool.function.arguments.
  • Update expected arguments value for assistant tool call with empty argument object to match tool.function.arguments.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/openai.test.ts` |

and transforming model strings across parseModelString, extractEnabledModels, and transformToAiModelList. #### Sequence diagram for parsing model string with capabilities and deployment names ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Tester participant parseModelString participant Console as console Tester->>parseModelString: parseModelString("azure", "gpt-4o->my-deploy=GPT-4o<128000:vision:fc>", true) activate parseModelString parseModelString->>parseModelString: split modelString by commas and Chinese commas parseModelString->>parseModelString: detect operation (+, - or removeAll) parseModelString->>parseModelString: extract modelId, deploymentName, displayName parseModelString->>parseModelString: parse contextWindowTokens and capabilities parseModelString->>Console: warn("Unknown capability: name") for each unknown capability parseModelString-->>Tester: AiModelParseResult(add=[AiModelAddEntry{id:"gpt-4o", displayName:"GPT-4o", abilities{vision,functionCall}, contextWindowTokens:128000, type:"chat", config{deploymentName:"my-deploy"}}], removed=[], removeAll:false) deactivate parseModelString ``` #### Class diagram for parseModels utilities and related types ```mermaid classDiagram class ParseModelsUtils { +parseModelString(providerId, modelString, withDeploymentName) AiModelParseResult +extractEnabledModels(providerId, modelString, withDeploymentName) string[] +transformToAiModelList(modelString, defaultModels, providerId, withDeploymentName) AiFullModelCard[] } class AiModelParseResult { +AiModelAddEntry[] add +string[] removed +bool removeAll } class AiModelAddEntry { +string id +string displayName +number contextWindowTokens +AiModelAbilities abilities +string type +AiModelConfig config } class AiModelAbilities { +bool reasoning +bool vision +bool functionCall +bool files +bool video +bool search +bool imageOutput } class AiModelConfig { +string deploymentName } class AiFullModelCard { +string id +string displayName +bool enabled +string type +AiModelAbilities abilities +AiModelConfig config } class LobeDefaultModelEntry { +string id +string providerId +string displayName +AiModelAbilities abilities } ParseModelsUtils ..> AiModelParseResult : returns ParseModelsUtils ..> AiFullModelCard : returns ParseModelsUtils ..> AiModelAddEntry : internal ParseModelsUtils ..> LobeDefaultModelEntry : uses AiModelParseResult o-- AiModelAddEntry : add AiModelAddEntry o-- AiModelAbilities : abilities AiModelAddEntry o-- AiModelConfig : config AiFullModelCard o-- AiModelAbilities : abilities AiFullModelCard o-- AiModelConfig : config ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Expand parseModelString tests to cover video capability, mixed capabilities, unknown capabilities, deployment-name parsing, and numerous edge/security input patterns. |
  • Add tests verifying parsing of video and mixed capabilities, including all supported capabilities at once.
  • Add tests asserting console.warn is called for one or multiple unknown capabilities and that supported capabilities still parse correctly.

create reasoning_content string
remove reasoning field ModelRuntime-->>ChatService: payload_with_reasoning_content_and_stream deactivate ModelRuntime ChatService->>DeepSeekAPI: POST /chat/completions DeepSeekAPI-->>ChatService: streaming response with reasoning ChatService->>ResponseBuilder: convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages) activate ResponseBuilder ResponseBuilder->>ResponseBuilder: for each message Note over ResponseBuilder: if message.reasoning.content exists
push ResponseReasoningItem
then push message without reasoning ResponseBuilder-->>ChatService: response_input_items_with_reasoning_blocks deactivate ResponseBuilder ChatService-->>ChatClient: Stream final messages and reasoning blocks ChatClient-->>User: Render answer and reasoning summary ``` #### Class diagram for reasoning-aware chat messages and DeepSeek handling ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +string_or_UserMessageContentPart_array content +string role +string name +MessageToolCall_array tool_calls +string tool_call_id +ReasoningMeta reasoning } class ReasoningMeta { +string content +number duration } class MessageCleanupProcessor { +process(messages) OpenAIChatMessage_array } class DeepSeekParams { +string baseURL +ChatCompletionConfig chatCompletion +DebugConfig debug } class ChatCompletionConfig { +function handlePayload(payload) Payload } class Payload { +OpenAIChatMessage_array messages +string model +boolean stream } class ConvertOpenAIMessages { +async convertOpenAIMessages(messages) OpenAI_ChatCompletionMessageParam_array } class ConvertOpenAIResponseInputs { +async convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages) ResponseInputItem_array } class ResponseReasoningItem { +SummaryItem_array summary +string type } class SummaryItem { +string text +string type } OpenAIChatMessage --> ReasoningMeta : has MessageCleanupProcessor --> ### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/4451353a84a39b0db73ec467ac783594e2b8688e/src/store/file/slices/upload/action.ts#L188 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Match storage-limit failures using structured error fields** This handler only recognizes quota failures when `error.message` contains the exact English phrase `beyond the plan limit`, so any wording change (different backend message text, localization, or wrapped TRPC error format) will bypass the branch and rethrow, which means users still get no targeted quota notification in the same upload-limit scenario this change is trying to fix. Use stable error metadata (for example TRPC code/cause payload) instead of substring matching. --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/4451353a84a39b0db73ec467ac783594e2b8688e/packages/model-runtime/src/providers/moonshot/index.ts#L212 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Fetch Moonshot models from the routed API mode** With this router config, chat requests can route to Anthropic mode when `baseURL` ends with `/anthropic`, but model discovery is still wired to a single OpenAI `models` fetcher; in `createRouterRuntime.models()` the functional `models` callback is invoked with the last router runtime client, so Anthropic-mode deployments can end up calling the OpenAI model-list API against an Anthropic base URL and `fetchMoonshotModels` then returns an empty list. This causes provider model loading to silently fail for that configuration.
