### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/e0cab2a00c56f3af552cfd16589f77dafced0920/.github/workflows/sync-main-to-canary.yaml#L44 **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Restore main-to-dev sync for release source branch** This change routes automatic sync PRs to `canary`, but release tooling still uses `dev` as the source branch (`scripts/releaseWorkflow/index.ts` lines 110–131 checkout/pull `dev`). Since `auto-tag-release.yml` now writes version bumps directly to `main`, those commits no longer propagate to `dev`, so later release runs can compute from stale version state and collide with already-created tags (causing skipped tagging/release steps). Keep a main→dev sync path, or migrate all release tooling to canary in the same change. --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/e0cab2a00c56f3af552cfd16589f77dafced0920/.github/workflows/auto-tag-release.yml#L150 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Rebase or retry before pushing version bump to main** This step performs a single `git push origin HEAD:main` after earlier setup; if another merge lands on `main` before this command executes, the push becomes non-fast-forward and the workflow aborts before tag/release creation. `git push -h` documents `-f, --force` as the mechanism for force updates, and this command uses neither force-with-lease nor any retry/rebase loop, so concurrent merges can intermittently break release automation.
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
Codex has been enabled to automatically review pull requests in this repo. Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. When you [sign up for Codex through ChatGPT](https://openai.com/codex), Codex can also answer questions or update the PR, like "@codex address that feedback".

## Reviewer's Guide Updates the main-to-canary sync workflow so it first attempts a direct merge into canary and push when conflict-free, and only falls back to creating a dated sync branch and PR (with duplicate-PR detection) when merge conflicts occur. #### Sequence diagram for optimized sync-main-to-canary workflow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Developer participant GitHub as GitHubRepository participant Actions as GitHubActionsWorkflow participant Git as GitClient participant GHCLI as GitHubCLI Developer->>GitHub: Push commits to main GitHub->>Actions: Trigger sync-main-to-canary workflow Actions->>Git: git checkout canary Actions->>Git: git pull origin canary Actions->>Git: git merge origin/main --no-edit alt merge succeeds (no conflicts) Actions->>Git: compare HEAD vs origin/canary alt no changes Actions-->>Actions: echo No changes to sync else has changes Actions-->>Actions: echo Merge succeeded, pushing directly Actions->>Git: git push origin canary end else merge conflicts Actions-->>Actions: echo Merge conflicts detected, creating PR Actions->>Git: git merge --abort Actions->>Git: git checkout -B sync/main-to-canary-YYYYMMDD origin/main Actions->>Git: git push origin sync/main-to-canary-YYYYMMDD -f Actions->>GHCLI: gh pr list --base canary --head sync/main-to-canary-YYYYMMDD --state open alt existing PR found GHCLI-->>Actions: return existing PR number Actions-->>Actions: echo PR already exists else no existing PR Actions->>GHCLI: gh pr create --base canary --head sync/main-to-canary-YYYYMMDD GHCLI-->>Actions: PR created for manual conflict resolution end end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Change sync strategy to merge main directly into canary and push when there are no conflicts or changes. |
  • Switch from creating a dated sync branch off main to operating directly on the canary branch.
  • Checkout and update canary from origin before attempting the merge with origin/main.
  • On successful merge, compare HEAD with origin/canary to skip pushing when there are no effective changes.
  • Push directly to canary when merge succeeds and there are actual changes to sync.
| `.github/workflows/sync-main-to-canary.yaml` | | Introduce conflict handling that falls back to creating a sync branch and PR, with duplicate PR prevention. |
  • On merge conflict, abort the merge and create a dated sync branch name (sync/main-to-canary-YYYYMMDD).
  • Force-push the sync branch based on origin/main instead of canary.
  • Use the GitHub CLI to detect an existing open PR for the same sync branch and avoid creating duplicates.
  • Create a PR targeting canary with a conflict-specific description when no existing PR is found.
  • Remove the previous unconditional PR creation step and its simpler "Automatic sync" description.
| `.github/workflows/sync-main-to-canary.yaml` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Implements browser-style Electron titlebar tabs backed by a new tab pages slice in the electron store, synchronized with React Router navigation via a dedicated hook, using the existing plugin system for URL/reference resolution and cached metadata, and wired into Topic/Page items via context-menu and double-click actions with localStorage persistence and restoration. #### Sequence diagram for opening a page in a new tab via context menu ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant PageListItem participant PageDropdownMenu participant pluginRegistry participant ElectronStore participant ReactRouter as ReactRouterNavigate participant useTabNavigation User->>PageListItem: Right-click page item PageListItem->>PageDropdownMenu: open menu User->>PageDropdownMenu: Click Open in New Tab PageDropdownMenu->>PageDropdownMenu: build url /page/pageId PageDropdownMenu->>pluginRegistry: parseUrl(/page/pageId, "") pluginRegistry-->>PageDropdownMenu: PageReference PageDropdownMenu->>ElectronStore: addTab(reference) PageDropdownMenu->>ReactRouter: navigate(/page/pageId) ReactRouter-->>useTabNavigation: location change useTabNavigation->>pluginRegistry: parseUrl(pathname, search) pluginRegistry-->>useTabNavigation: PageReference useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: read tabs, activeTabId alt tab already exists useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: activateTab(reference.id) else active tab exists but is different page useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: updateTab(activeTabId, reference, cached) end ElectronStore->>ElectronStore: persist tabs to localStorage useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: maybe updateTabCache with dynamic title ``` #### Sequence diagram for restoring Electron tabs on app start ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AppStartup participant TitleBar participant useTabNavigation participant ElectronStore participant TabPagesStorage as LocalStorage participant TabBar AppStartup->>TitleBar: mount TitleBar TitleBar->>useTabNavigation: call hook useTabNavigation->>useTabNavigation: first mount check useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: loadTabs() ElectronStore->>TabPagesStorage: getTabPages() TabPagesStorage-->>ElectronStore: {activeTabId, tabs} ElectronStore-->>useTabNavigation: state updated TitleBar->>TabBar: render with store state TabBar->>ElectronStore: read tabs and activeTabId via useResolvedTabs ElectronStore-->>TabBar: tab references TabBar->>pluginRegistry: resolve(reference, ctx) pluginRegistry-->>TabBar: ResolvedPageData list TabBar-->>AppStartup: show restored tabs in titlebar ``` #### Sequence diagram for double-clicking a topic to open a new tab ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant TopicItem participant pluginRegistry participant ElectronStore participant Router as ReactRouterNavigate participant useTabNavigation User->>TopicItem: Double-click topic TopicItem->>TopicItem: check isDesktop and active ids TopicItem->>pluginRegistry: parseUrl(/agent~or~group, topic=query) pluginRegistry-->>TopicItem: PageReference TopicItem->>ElectronStore: addTab(reference) TopicItem->>TopicItem: switchTopic or selectPage TopicItem->>Router: navigate to topic route Router-->>useTabNavigation: location change useTabNavigation->>pluginRegistry: parseUrl(pathname, search) pluginRegistry-->>useTabNavigation: PageReference useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: read tabs and activeTabId alt existing tab for reference useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: activateTab(reference.id) else active tab exists useTabNavigation->>ElectronStore: updateTab(activeTabId, reference, cached) end ElectronStore->>ElectronStore: persist updated tabs to LocalStorage ElectronStore-->>TabBar: updated activeTabId and tabs TabBar-->>User: active tab highlighted and content visible ``` #### Class diagram for Electron tab pages state and actions ```mermaid classDiagram class ElectronStore { +string~null activeTabId +PageReference[] tabs +void activateTab(id) +void addTab(reference, cached, activate) +PageReference~null getActiveTab() +void loadTabs() +string~null removeTab(id) +void reorderTabs(fromIndex, toIndex) +void updateTab(id, reference, cached) +void updateTabCache(id, cached) } class TabPagesState { +string~null activeTabId +PageReference[] tabs } class TabPagesActionImpl { -Setter #set -function #get +TabPagesActionImpl(set, get, api) +void activateTab(id) +void addTab(reference, cached, activate) +PageReference~null getActiveTab() +void loadTabs() +string~null removeTab(id) +void reorderTabs(fromIndex, toIndex) +void updateTab(id, reference, cached) +void updateTabCache(id, cached) -void #persist() } class TabPagesStorage { +string TAB_PAGES_STORAGE_KEY +TabPagesStorageData getTabPages() +boolean saveTabPages(tabs, activeTabId) } class TabPagesStorageData { +string~null activeTabId +PageReference[] tabs } class useTabNavigation { +void useTabNavigation() -void loadTabsOnMount() -void syncRouteToTabs() -void syncTitleToTabCache() } class pluginRegistry { +PageReference~null parseUrl(pathname, search) +ResolvedPageData~null resolve(reference, ctx) } class getCachedDataForReference { +CachedPageData~undefined getCachedDataForReference(reference) } ElectronStore <|.. TabPagesState ElectronStore ..> TabPagesActionImpl : creates slice TabPagesActionImpl ..> TabPagesStorage : uses TabPagesStorageData ..> PageReference : contains useTabNavigation ..> ElectronStore : useElectronStore useTabNavigation ..> pluginRegistry : parseUrl useTabNavigation ..> getCachedDataForReference : getCachedDataForReference ``` #### Class diagram for Electron titlebar TabBar components ```mermaid classDiagram class TabBar { +TabBar() -void handleActivate(id, url) -void handleClose(id) } class TabItem { +boolean isActive +ResolvedPageData item +TabItem() -void handleClick() -void handleClose(event) } class useResolvedTabs { +UseResolvedTabsResult useResolvedTabs() } class UseResolvedTabsResult { +string~null activeTabId +ResolvedPageData[] tabs } class ElectronStoreTabs { +string~null activeTabId +PageReference[] tabs } class pluginRegistry { +ResolvedPageData~null resolve(reference, ctx) } class usePluginContext { +PluginContext usePluginContext() } TabBar ..> useResolvedTabs : uses TabBar ..> ElectronStoreTabs : activateTab, removeTab TabBar ..> TabItem : renders TabItem ..> ResolvedPageData : consumes useResolvedTabs ..> ElectronStoreTabs : reads useResolvedTabs ..> pluginRegistry : resolve useResolvedTabs ..> usePluginContext : context ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Extract shared cached page data resolver for PageReference and reuse it in navigation and tab logic. |
  • Move getCachedDataForReference logic out of useNavigationHistory into a new navigation/cachedData module
  • Update useNavigationHistory to import the shared helper instead of defining it inline
| `src/features/Electron/navigation/useNavigationHistory.ts`
`src/features/Electron/navigation/cachedData.ts` | | Add a tab pages slice to the Electron Zustand store to manage tab state and persistence. |
  • Define TabPagesState, initial state, and TabPagesActionImpl with add/activate/remove/reorder/update operations and cache updates
  • Wire the new tabPages slice into the Electron store creator and initial state
  • Persist tabs and active tab to localStorage via helper functions with defensive parsing
| `src/store/electron/actions/tabPages.ts`
`src/store/electron/store.ts`
`src/store/electron/initialState.ts`
`src/features/Electron/titlebar/TabBar/storage.ts` | | Introduce a tab bar UI in the Electron titlebar that reflects and controls the tab state. |
  • Create TabBar component that renders resolved tab items, activates tabs on click, and closes tabs with correct next-active behavior and fallback navigation
  • Create TabItem presentation component and static styles for tabs, including hover, active, and close-button behavior
  • Mount TabBar in the main TitleBar component below the navigation bar and only render when at least two tabs exist
| `src/features/Electron/titlebar/TitleBar.tsx`

`src/features/Electron/titlebar/TabBar/styles.ts` | | Synchronize router navigation with tab state without auto-creating tabs and keep tab titles in sync. |
  • Add useTabNavigation hook to load tabs from storage, map URL changes to PageReference via pluginRegistry, activate existing tabs, and update the active tab’s reference when navigating within it
  • Update tab cached metadata when the current page title changes, using getCachedDataForReference to populate initial cache

`src/features/Electron/navigation/cachedData.ts` | | Resolve stored tab references into display-ready data using the existing plugin system. |
  • Add useResolvedTabs hook that maps stored PageReference items to ResolvedPageData via pluginRegistry.resolve and plugin context
  • Expose activeTabId and resolved tabs list for the TabBar UI
| `src/features/Electron/titlebar/TabBar/hooks/useResolvedTabs.ts` | | Wire tab creation and activation into TopicItem and PageItem interactions for desktop builds. |
  • Add "Open in New Tab" context menu action for page list items that parses the URL into a PageReference, calls addTab, and navigates to the page
  • Add "Open in New Tab" context menu actions for agent and group topics that build appropriate URLs/queries, add tabs, and navigate
  • Change double-click behavior on agent and group TopicItem components from opening new windows to adding/updating a tab and switching topic selection, and add similar double-click tab creation for PageItem
  • Inject useElectronStore addTab and react-router navigate/select methods where needed, and guard tab behavior behind isDesktop checks
| `src/app/[variants]/(main)/page/_layout/Body/List/Item/useDropdownMenu.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(main)/group/_layout/Sidebar/Topic/List/Item/useDropdownMenu.tsx`

## Reviewer's Guide Adds configurable memory effort and tool permissions to the chat/memory system, wiring user- and agent-level settings through server, context engine, and builtin memory tool so that memory search intensity and write access are controlled per chat/user. #### Sequence diagram for memory tool write operations with toolPermission ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as AgentRuntime participant Me as MemoryExecutor participant St as AgentStore participant Sel as ChatConfigSelectors participant Svc as UserMemoryService Agent->>Me: addContextMemory(params, ctx) activate Me Me->>Me: resolveToolPermission(ctx.agentId) Me->>St: getAgentStoreState() St-->>Me: state alt agentSpecific Me->>Sel: chatConfigByIdSelectors.getChatConfigById(agentId)(state) else currentChat Me->>Sel: agentChatConfigSelectors.currentChatConfig(state) end Sel-->>Me: chatConfig Me->>Me: check chatConfig.memory.toolPermission alt permission is read-only Me-->>Agent: throw Error(Memory tool is in read-only mode) else permission is read-write or undefined Me->>Svc: addContextMemory(params) Svc-->>Me: result Me-->>Agent: BuiltinToolResult end deactivate Me ``` #### Class diagram for updated memory configuration types ```mermaid classDiagram class UserMemoryEffort { } class UserMemorySettings { +UserMemoryEffort effort +boolean enabled } class AgentMemoryChatConfig { +MemoryConfig memory } class MemoryConfig { +UserMemoryEffort effort +MemoryToolPermission toolPermission } class MemoryToolPermission { } class LobeAgentChatConfig { +number autoCreateTopicThreshold +string compressionModelId +boolean disableContextCaching +string effort +boolean enableAdaptiveThinking +boolean enableAutoCreateTopic +boolean enableAutoScrollOnStreaming +boolean enableCompressHistory +boolean enableContextCompression +boolean enableHistoryCount +boolean enableMaxTokens +boolean enableReasoning +boolean enableReasoningEffort +boolean enableStreaming +string gpt5_1ReasoningEffort +string gpt5_2ProReasoningEffort +string gpt5_2ReasoningEffort +string gpt5ReasoningEffort +number historyCount +string imageAspectRatio +string imageResolution +string inputTemplate +LocalSystemConfig localSystem +number reasoningBudgetToken +string reasoningEffort +WorkingModel searchFCModel +SearchMode searchMode +string textVerbosity +string thinking +number thinkingBudget +string thinkingLevel +number toolResultMaxLength +boolean urlContext +boolean useModelBuiltinSearch } class LocalSystemConfig { +string workingDirectory } class WorkingModel { +string model +string provider } class SearchMode { } class MemoryChatConfigSchema { +memory object } class AgentChatConfigSchema { +object baseFields +merge MemoryChatConfigSchema } UserMemorySettings --> UserMemoryEffort : uses MemoryConfig --> UserMemoryEffort : uses MemoryConfig --> MemoryToolPermission : uses AgentMemoryChatConfig --> MemoryConfig : composition LobeAgentChatConfig --> AgentMemoryChatConfig : extends AgentChatConfigSchema --> MemoryChatConfigSchema : merges LobeAgentChatConfig --> LocalSystemConfig : uses LobeAgentChatConfig --> WorkingModel : uses LobeAgentChatConfig --> SearchMode : uses ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce shared memory config types for agents and users, including effort and memory tool permission. |
  • Add UserMemoryEffort type and optional effort field to UserMemorySettings with a default of medium in settings constants.
  • Extract AgentMemoryChatConfig and MemoryChatConfigSchema to model chat-level memory configuration (effort, toolPermission) and merge into existing agent chat config schema.
  • Wire memory property into LobeAgentChatConfig type so agent configs can express memory effort and tool permissions.
| `packages/types/src/user/settings/memory.ts`
`packages/const/src/settings/memory.ts`
`packages/types/src/agent/chatConfig.ts` | | Make memory search intensity depend on a normalized memory effort value derived from user settings. |
  • Define MemoryEffort type and normalizeMemoryEffort helper with a safe default of medium.
  • Add MEMORY_SEARCH_TOP_K_LIMITS constants mapping effort levels to per-layer topK limits.
  • Inject memoryEffort into MemorySearchContext from userSettings.memory and apply effort-based caps to requested search limits before querying the memory model.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/userMemories.ts`
`packages/const/src/userMemory.ts` | | Add per-chat memory tool permission that can make the memory builtin tool read-only. |
  • Resolve effective tool permission from current or specified agent chatConfig, defaulting to read-write when state/config is missing.
  • Introduce ensureWritable guard in MemoryExecutor and apply it to all mutating memory APIs by accepting BuiltinToolContext and checking agentId-specific permission.
  • Leave search APIs unchanged so that read-only mode still allows retrieval but blocks add/update/remove operations.
| `packages/builtin-tool-memory/src/executor/index.ts` | | Propagate memory effort into the context engine and memory tool prompt so the model can adapt its behavior. |
  • Extend context engineering context with MemoryContext, and compute effectiveMemoryEffort from chatConfig.memory.effort or user memory settings, defaulting to medium.
  • Pass memoryContext into contextEngineering and MessagesEngine and expose a memory_effort variable generator used by the builtin memory tool system role.
  • Annotate the memory tool system prompt with memory_effort and an explicit policy block describing low/medium/high behaviors.
| `src/services/chat/index.ts`
`src/services/chat/mecha/contextEngineering.ts`
`packages/context-engine/src/providers/UserMemoryInjector.ts`
`packages/context-engine/src/providers/index.ts`
`packages/builtin-tool-memory/src/systemRole.ts` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Updates the main-to-canary sync workflow to first attempt a direct merge into canary (with conflict detection, auto-closing/annotating prior sync PRs, and richer fallback PR handling) and tightens the auto-tag hotfix detection logic while bumping the @lobehub/ui dependency patch version. #### Sequence diagram for updated main-to-canary sync workflow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant GH_Actions as GitHub_Actions participant Workflow as sync_main_to_canary_workflow participant Git as git_cli participant GH as github_cli_gh participant OriginMain as origin_main participant OriginCanary as origin_canary GH_Actions->>Workflow: Trigger on push to main Workflow->>Git: git config user Workflow->>GH: gh pr list --base canary --state open GH-->>Workflow: existing sync PR info (optional) Workflow->>Git: git checkout canary Workflow->>Git: git pull origin canary Workflow->>Git: git merge origin/main --no-edit alt merge succeeds Workflow->>Git: compare HEAD vs origin/canary alt no changes Workflow-->>GH_Actions: exit (no sync needed) else has changes Workflow->>Git: git push origin canary alt push succeeds alt existing sync PR exists Workflow->>GH: gh pr close existing_pr --delete-branch end Workflow-->>GH_Actions: exit (direct sync completed) else push fails Note over Workflow,Git: Non fast forward or race Workflow->>Git: create branch sync/main-to-canary-date-runid Workflow->>Git: git push origin branch -f Workflow->>GH: gh pr create base=canary head=branch Workflow-->>GH_Actions: exit (fallback PR created) end end else merge conflicts Workflow->>Git: git merge --abort alt existing conflict PR exists Workflow->>GH: gh pr comment existing_pr (ask to pull latest main) Workflow-->>GH_Actions: exit (reuse existing PR) else no existing PR Workflow->>Git: git checkout -B sync/main-to-canary-date-runid origin/canary Workflow->>Git: git merge origin/main --no-edit alt merge still has conflicts Workflow->>Git: git add -A Workflow->>Git: git commit -m chore_merge_main_into_canary_has_conflicts end Workflow->>Git: git push origin branch -f Workflow->>GH: gh pr create base=canary head=branch with conflict_resolution_instructions Workflow-->>GH_Actions: exit (conflict PR created) end end ``` #### Sequence diagram for updated hotfix auto-tag detection ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Maintainer as actor_maintainer participant GH_Actions as GitHub_Actions participant Workflow as auto_tag_release_workflow Maintainer->>GH_Actions: Open PR from hotfix/x.y.z GH_Actions->>Workflow: Trigger on PR events Workflow->>Workflow: Check release PR conditions alt is release PR Workflow-->>GH_Actions: should_tag true via release path else not release PR Workflow->>Workflow: Read HEAD_REF and PR_TITLE Workflow->>Workflow: Test HEAD_REF starts with hotfix/ alt HEAD_REF not hotfix/* Workflow-->>GH_Actions: should_tag false (not hotfix PR) else HEAD_REF is hotfix/* Workflow->>Workflow: Validate PR_TITLE prefix Workflow->>Workflow: grep for style|feat|fix|refactor with optional gitmoji alt title matches allowed prefixes Workflow-->>GH_Actions: should_tag true (valid hotfix PR) else title does not match Workflow-->>GH_Actions: should_tag false (invalid hotfix title) end end end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refine main→canary sync workflow to merge directly into canary when possible and handle conflicts and existing sync PRs more intelligently. |
  • Remove the separate sync-branch preparation step and work directly from the canary branch.
  • On main pushes, fetch and merge origin/main into canary, attempting a direct push when there are no conflicts and actual changes.
  • If direct push succeeds, automatically close any existing open sync PR created from sync/main-to-canary-* branches as superseded.
  • If direct push fails (e.g., due to non-fast-forward), create a new uniquely named sync branch, push it, and open a fallback sync PR with explanatory body.
  • When merge conflicts occur, either comment on an existing sync PR to pull latest main or create a new conflict PR with conflict markers committed and detailed resolution instructions in the PR body.
| `.github/workflows/sync-main-to-canary.yaml` | | Tighten hotfix auto-tagging to require both a hotfix/* branch name and a PR title that matches specific commit-type prefixes. |
  • Continue to only consider PRs that are not already classified as release PRs.
  • Require the branch name to start with hotfix/; otherwise mark as not a hotfix PR and exit early.
  • Add a regex-based gate that checks the PR title for allowed prefixes (style/feat/fix/refactor with optional corresponding gitmoji).
  • Set should_tag to true only when both the hotfix branch prefix and the allowed title prefix conditions are satisfied, and update logging messages accordingly.
| `.github/workflows/auto-tag-release.yml` | | Update UI dependency to latest patch version. |
  • Bump @lobehub/ui dependency version from ^4.36.2 to ^4.36.3 in package.json.
| `package.json` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Fixes execution of multi-agent tasks when tasks are sometimes returned as a stringified JSON array, and documents the correct JSON shape for executeAgentTasks in the system role instructions. #### Sequence diagram for executeAgentTasks handling stringified tasks ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant LLM participant ExecuteAgentTasksInspector participant AgentGroupStore User->>LLM: Request executeAgentTasks LLM-->>User: Response with tasks (array or stringified JSON) User->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: Open ExecuteAgentTasks inspector with args/partialArgs ExecuteAgentTasksInspector->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: Read args.tasks or partialArgs.tasks as rawTasks alt rawTasks is string ExecuteAgentTasksInspector->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: tasks = safeParsePartialJSON_TaskItemArray(rawTasks) or [] else rawTasks is array or undefined ExecuteAgentTasksInspector->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: tasks = rawTasks or [] end ExecuteAgentTasksInspector->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: agentIds = tasks.map_agentId_filterTruthy ExecuteAgentTasksInspector->>AgentGroupStore: useAgentGroupStore(activeGroupId) AgentGroupStore-->>ExecuteAgentTasksInspector: activeGroupId and agents ExecuteAgentTasksInspector-->>User: Render multi-agent task execution UI ``` #### Flow diagram for executeAgentTasks tasks parsing and agentId extraction ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start] --> B[Read args.tasks or partialArgs.tasks as rawTasks] B --> C{rawTasks exists?} C -- No --> D[Set tasks to empty array] C -- Yes --> E{Type of rawTasks is string?} E -- Yes --> F[Parse with safeParsePartialJSON to TaskItem array] F --> G{Parse successful?} G -- Yes --> H[Set tasks to parsed TaskItem array] G -- No --> D E -- No --> I[Set tasks to rawTasks] D --> J[Compute agentIds from tasks map task.agentId filter truthy] H --> J I --> J J --> K[Use agentIds with AgentGroupStore and render inspector] K --> L[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Make ExecuteAgentTasks inspector robust to tasks being returned as a stringified JSON value instead of an array. |
  • Extend imported types to include TaskItem for proper typing of task elements.
  • Replace direct tasks selection with a memoized computation that normalizes tasks from args/partialArgs and parses string values using safeParsePartialJSON.
  • Adjust agentIds derivation to safely handle possibly undefined task items and agentId fields.

  • Add a prominent warning about the tasks field needing to be a proper JSON array rather than a stringified JSON.

body:
## Reviewer's Guide Implements a security fix in ModelRuntime parameter resolution to prevent leaking global API keys when a custom baseURL is provided, adds targeted tests for the affected providers, and applies minor style/lint cleanups. #### Sequence diagram for secure apiKey resolution with custom baseURL ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Client as ClientApp participant Server as ModelRuntimeModule participant AKM as ApiKeyManager participant Provider as ProviderRuntime User->>Client: Send JWT payload (provider, baseURL, optional apiKey) Client->>Server: initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload(provider, payload) Server->>Server: getParamsFromPayload(provider, payload) alt provider is OpenAI or Azure or AzureAI alt payload.baseURL is set Server->>Server: apiKey = payload.apiKey alt apiKey is missing or invalid Server-->>Client: throw InvalidProviderAPIKey else Server->>Provider: instantiate runtime with { apiKey, baseURL } Provider-->>Client: ready end else payload.baseURL is not set Server->>AKM: pick(payload.apiKey || globalApiKey) AKM-->>Server: apiKey Server->>Provider: instantiate runtime with { apiKey, optional baseURL } Provider-->>Client: ready end else provider is ComfyUI alt payload.baseURL is set Server->>Server: apiKey = payload.apiKey (may be undefined) else payload.baseURL is not set Server->>Server: apiKey = payload.apiKey || globalComfyUIApiKey end Server->>Provider: instantiate runtime with { apiKey, baseURL } Provider-->>Client: ready end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Change getParamsFromPayload so that when a custom baseURL is supplied for OpenAI-compatible, Azure, AzureAI, or ComfyUI providers, the apiKey must come from the user payload and will no longer fall back to global/server API keys. |
  • For OpenAI-compatible providers, derive apiKey directly from payload when payload.baseURL is set; only use ApiKeyManager and global keys when baseURL is not overridden.
  • For Azure providers, require apiKey in payload when payload.baseURL is set and otherwise continue to resolve via ApiKeyManager with AZURE_API_KEY.
  • For AzureAI providers, require apiKey in payload when payload.baseURL is set and otherwise resolve via ApiKeyManager with AZUREAI_ENDPOINT_KEY.
  • For ComfyUI, when payload.baseURL is set use payload.apiKey (which can be undefined) and do not fall back to COMFYUI_API_KEY; retain existing fallback behavior only when baseURL is not overridden.

## Reviewer's Guide Implements dynamic, topic-based timeout handling for user memory extraction tasks and adds corresponding test coverage, ensuring tasks that exceed their calculated time budget are automatically marked as timed out errors. #### Sequence diagram for dynamic timeout handling in user memory extraction status ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User as user participant Client as client_app participant Router as userMemoryRouter participant AsyncModel as asyncTaskModel User->>Client: Request memory extraction task status Client->>Router: getUserMemoryExtractionTaskStatus(taskId) Router->>AsyncModel: findById(taskId) AsyncModel-->>Router: task alt Task not found or user mismatch Router-->>Client: null else Task found Router->>Router: metadata = initUserMemoryExtractionMetadata(task.metadata) Router->>Router: timeoutMs = getUserMemoryExtractionTimeoutMs(metadata) Router->>Router: taskCreatedAt = new Date(task.createdAt).getTime() Router->>Router: isActiveTask = status is Pending or Processing alt Active and expired based on topic-based timeout Router->>Router: Build AsyncTaskError Timeout Router->>AsyncModel: update(task.id, { error, status = Error }) AsyncModel-->>Router: updatedTask Router-->>Client: { id, status = Error, metadata, error } else Not expired or not active Router-->>Client: { id, status: task.status, metadata, error: task.error } end end ``` #### Class diagram for user memory extraction timeout calculation and task handling ```mermaid classDiagram class UserMemoryExtractionMetadataProgress { +number totalTopics } class UserMemoryExtractionMetadata { +UserMemoryExtractionMetadataProgress progress } class AsyncTask { +string id +string userId +AsyncTaskStatus status +AsyncTaskError error +UserMemoryExtractionMetadata metadata +string createdAt } class AsyncTaskStatus { <> Pending Processing Error Completed } class AsyncTaskErrorType { <> Timeout Other } class AsyncTaskError { +AsyncTaskErrorType type +string message +AsyncTaskError(type, message) } class AsyncTaskModel { +AsyncTask findById(id) +AsyncTask update(id, fields) } class UserMemoryRouter { +getUserMemoryExtractionTaskStatus(taskId, ctx) } class TimeoutCalculator { +number USER_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_PER_TOPIC_MS +number getUserMemoryExtractionTimeoutMs(metadata) } class MetadataInitializer { +UserMemoryExtractionMetadata initUserMemoryExtractionMetadata(metadata) } UserMemoryExtractionMetadata --> UserMemoryExtractionMetadataProgress : has AsyncTask --> UserMemoryExtractionMetadata : has AsyncTask --> AsyncTaskStatus : has AsyncTask --> AsyncTaskError : has AsyncTaskError --> AsyncTaskErrorType : uses UserMemoryRouter --> AsyncTaskModel : uses UserMemoryRouter --> TimeoutCalculator : uses UserMemoryRouter --> MetadataInitializer : uses TimeoutCalculator --> UserMemoryExtractionMetadata : uses MetadataInitializer --> UserMemoryExtractionMetadata : creates ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce dynamic timeout calculation for user memory extraction tasks based on topic count and enforce it in getMemoryExtractionTask. |
  • Add a per-topic timeout constant and helper function to compute total timeout from metadata progress.totalTopics.
  • Normalize task metadata with initUserMemoryExtractionMetadata and reuse it for timeout calculation and response payloads.
  • Detect when an active task has exceeded its computed timeout since createdAt and convert it to an error state with a descriptive AsyncTaskErrorType.Timeout error, persisting the update via asyncTaskModel.update and returning the errored task payload.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/userMemory.ts` | | Add unit test coverage for the new timeout behavior and error typing in user memory extraction tasks. |
  • Import AsyncTaskErrorType into the test suite to assert timeout error type.
  • Reset timers to real timers in beforeEach to avoid cross-test interference, and use fake timers/system time in the new timeout test.
  • Mock an in-progress topic-based task that has exceeded the dynamic timeout and assert that it is updated to an error state with the expected timeout error message and returned accordingly.
| `src/server/routers/lambda/__tests__/userMemory.test.ts` | | Minor cleanup in memory-extraction webhook route. |
  • Add a small formatting adjustment (blank line) around the workflow scheduling response for readability.
| `src/app/(backend)/api/webhooks/memory-extraction/route.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#12345**: PR adds dynamic timeouts for memory extraction tasks, addressing memory analysis hanging indefinitely as described in the issue. ---

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. ## Reviewer's Guide Implements Google data protection enforcement that prevents using Gmail/Google tools together with restricted providers (Grok/xAI, DeepSeek) across server connection, message sending, and model switching flows, plus wires the hooks into the conversation and model switch UI, and updates the default persona text. #### Sequence diagram for Google tool connection with data protection check ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as KlavisServerItem participant GDP as useGoogleDataProtection participant StoreA as useAgentStore participant StoreT as useToolStore User->>UI: Click Connect Google tool UI->>GDP: useGoogleDataProtection() GDP->>StoreA: currentAgentModelProvider GDP->>StoreA: currentAgentModel GDP->>StoreT: getConnectedServers StoreA-->>GDP: providerId, modelId StoreT-->>GDP: connectedServers GDP-->>UI: { checkGoogleToolConnect } UI->>GDP: checkGoogleToolConnect(identifier) GDP->>GDP: isGoogleTool(identifier)? alt identifier is not Google tool GDP-->>UI: false (not blocked) UI->>UI: proceed with connection UI->>StoreT: createKlavisServer else identifier is Google tool GDP->>GDP: isGoogleRestrictedProvider(providerId, modelId)? alt provider is restricted GDP->>UI: show warning modal GDP-->>UI: true (blocked) UI->>UI: abort connection else provider is not restricted GDP-->>UI: false (not blocked) UI->>StoreT: createKlavisServer end end ``` #### Sequence diagram for model switch with Google data protection ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Panel as ModelSwitchPanel participant Hook as usePanelHandlers participant GDP as useGoogleDataProtection participant StoreA as useAgentStore User->>Panel: Select new model and provider Panel->>Hook: handleModelChange(modelId, providerId) Hook->>GDP: useGoogleDataProtection() GDP->>StoreA: currentAgentPlugins GDP->>StoreA: currentAgentModelProvider GDP->>StoreA: currentAgentModel StoreA-->>GDP: plugins, providerId, modelId GDP-->>Hook: { checkModelSwitch, state } Hook->>GDP: checkModelSwitch(providerId, modelId) GDP->>GDP: isGoogleRestrictedProvider(providerId, modelId)? alt provider is not restricted GDP-->>Hook: false (not blocked) Hook->>Hook: apply onModelChangeProp or updateAgentConfig else provider is restricted GDP->>GDP: state.hasEnabledGoogleTools? alt no enabled Google tools GDP-->>Hook: false (not blocked) Hook->>Hook: apply onModelChangeProp or updateAgentConfig else has enabled Google tools GDP->>Hook: show warning modal with tool names GDP-->>Hook: true (blocked) Hook->>Hook: abort model switch end end ``` #### Sequence diagram for sending a message with Google data protection hooks ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ConvArea as ConversationArea participant ConvProv as ConversationProvider participant HookFac as useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks participant GDP as useGoogleDataProtection User->>ConvArea: Click Send ConvArea->>HookFac: useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks({ messages }) HookFac->>GDP: useGoogleDataProtection() GDP-->>HookFac: { checkMessageSend, checkMessageHistoryForGoogleTools } HookFac-->>ConvArea: hooks.onBeforeSendMessage ConvArea->>ConvProv: onBeforeSendMessage() ConvProv->>HookFac: onBeforeSendMessage() HookFac->>GDP: checkMessageSend() GDP->>GDP: isGoogleRestrictedProvider(currentProvider, currentModel)? alt provider not restricted or no enabled tools GDP-->>HookFac: true (can send) else restricted and has enabled tools GDP->>ConvProv: show cannotSendMessage modal GDP-->>HookFac: false (block send) end alt checkMessageSend returned false HookFac-->>ConvProv: false ConvProv-->>ConvArea: blocked else checkMessageSend returned true HookFac->>GDP: checkMessageHistoryForGoogleTools(messages) GDP->>GDP: findGoogleToolsInMessages(messages) alt history has no Google tools GDP-->>HookFac: true HookFac-->>ConvProv: true ConvProv-->>ConvArea: proceed to send message else history has Google tools GDP->>ConvProv: show cannotSendWithHistory modal GDP-->>HookFac: false HookFac-->>ConvProv: false ConvProv-->>ConvArea: blocked end end ``` #### Class diagram for Google data protection hooks and utilities ```mermaid classDiagram class GoogleDataProtectionState { +string[] enabledGoogleToolIds +bool hasConflict +bool hasEnabledGoogleTools +bool isUsingRestrictedProvider } class useGoogleDataProtection { +GoogleDataProtectionState state +Promise~bool~ checkGoogleToolConnect(toolIdentifier string) +Promise~bool~ checkModelSwitch(newProviderId string, newModelId string) +Promise~bool~ checkMessageSend() +Promise~bool~ checkMessageHistoryForGoogleTools(messages UIChatMessage[]) } class useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks { +ConversationHooks useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks(params UseAgentGoogleProtectionHooksParams) } class UseAgentGoogleProtectionHooksParams { +UIChatMessage[] messages } class findGoogleToolsInMessages { +string[] GOOGLE_TOOL_IDENTIFIERS +bool isGoogleRestrictedProvider(providerId string, modelId string) +bool isGoogleTool(identifier string) } class usePanelHandlers { +handleModelChange(modelId string, providerId string) Promise~void~ } class KlavisServerItem { +handleConnect() Promise~void~ +handleToggle() Promise~void~ } class useAgentStore { } class useToolStore { } useGoogleDataProtection --> GoogleDataProtectionState useGoogleDataProtection --> googleDataProtectionConsts useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks --> useGoogleDataProtection useAgentGoogleProtectionHooks --> UseAgentGoogleProtectionHooksParams usePanelHandlers --> useGoogleDataProtection KlavisServerItem --> useGoogleDataProtection findGoogleToolsInMessages --> googleDataProtectionConsts useGoogleDataProtection --> useAgentStore useGoogleDataProtection --> useToolStore ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce centralized Google data protection logic and helpers to detect restricted providers, Google tools, and conflicts between them, including message history inspection. |
  • Add constants for restricted provider IDs, model name prefixes, and Google tool identifiers.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Removes the desktop-app guard from the `showClientFetch` visibility logic so that the "Fetch on Client" switch can appear and be toggled in desktop provider settings while preserving all other behavior and server-side defaults. #### Sequence diagram for toggling Fetch on Client switch in desktop provider settings ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant DesktopApp participant ProviderConfigComponent participant ProviderConfigStore User->>DesktopApp: Open provider settings DesktopApp->>ProviderConfigComponent: Render ProviderConfig ProviderConfigComponent->>ProviderConfigComponent: Evaluate showClientFetch Note over ProviderConfigComponent: showClientFetch depends on Note over ProviderConfigComponent: disableBrowserRequest Note over ProviderConfigComponent: defaultShowBrowserRequest Note over ProviderConfigComponent: showEndpoint and endpoint value Note over ProviderConfigComponent: presence of apikey ProviderConfigComponent-->>User: Display Fetch on Client switch (when showClientFetch is true) User->>ProviderConfigComponent: Toggle Fetch on Client switch ProviderConfigComponent->>ProviderConfigStore: Update fetchOnClient value ProviderConfigStore-->>ProviderConfigComponent: Confirm updated config ProviderConfigComponent-->>User: Render updated switch state ``` #### Flow diagram for updated showClientFetch visibility logic ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Evaluate showClientFetch] --> B{disableBrowserRequest is true?} B -- Yes --> Z[showClientFetch = false] B -- No --> C{defaultShowBrowserRequest is true?} C -- Yes --> Y[showClientFetch = true] C -- No --> D{showEndpoint is true?} D -- No --> E{apikey is present?} D -- Yes --> F{providerEndpointNotEmpty is true?} F -- No --> E F -- Yes --> Y E -- Yes --> Y E -- No --> Z ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Relaxed the visibility condition for the "Fetch on Client" switch so it can appear in the desktop app when all other criteria are satisfied. |
  • Removed the `!isDesktop` condition from the `showClientFetch` boolean expression that controls rendering of the client fetch switch
  • Kept all other conditions (browser request not disabled, default/showable endpoint, non-empty endpoint, and presence of API key) intact to avoid changing web behavior or validation logic
| `src/app/[variants]/(main)/settings/provider/features/ProviderConfig/index.tsx` |

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Fixes a race condition in TopicUrlSync’s bidirectional URL/store synchronization by replacing the generic store updater with explicit, ordered useLayoutEffect hooks, and updates/generated i18n locale JSON files (including new video.json per locale). #### Sequence diagram for the updated TopicUrlSync URL and store synchronization ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Browser participant TopicUrlSync participant useQueryState participant GenerationTopicStore rect rgb(230,230,250) User->>Browser: Navigate to /video Browser->>useQueryState: Read topic query param useQueryState-->>TopicUrlSync: topic value (may be null) end rect rgb(220,255,220) Note over TopicUrlSync: URL to store sync useLayoutEffect TopicUrlSync->>GenerationTopicStore: setState activeGenerationTopicId = topic or null end rect rgb(220,240,255) Note over TopicUrlSync: Store to URL sync useLayoutEffect TopicUrlSync->>GenerationTopicStore: subscribe to activeGenerationTopicId changes GenerationTopicStore-->>TopicUrlSync: initial activeGenerationTopicId alt activeGenerationTopicId differs from topic and is not null TopicUrlSync->>useQueryState: setTopic with new id else TopicUrlSync-->>useQueryState: No update (URL remains as is) end end Note over User,GenerationTopicStore: User clicks a topic in the sidebar User->>GenerationTopicStore: Select topic (activeGenerationTopicId updated) GenerationTopicStore-->>TopicUrlSync: activeGenerationTopicId changed TopicUrlSync->>useQueryState: setTopic with new activeGenerationTopicId useQueryState-->>Browser: Update URL ?topic=id (history replace) Note over User,Browser: User navigates to /video without topic User->>Browser: Navigate to /video Browser->>useQueryState: Read topic query param (null) useQueryState-->>TopicUrlSync: topic = null TopicUrlSync->>GenerationTopicStore: setState activeGenerationTopicId = null GenerationTopicStore-->>TopicUrlSync: activeGenerationTopicId changed to null TopicUrlSync-->>useQueryState: No setTopic call (URL stays without topic) ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refactor TopicUrlSync to use ordered useLayoutEffect hooks for deterministic URL ↔ store synchronization and to avoid persisting stale topic IDs. |
  • Remove the generic createStoreUpdater-based wiring between the URL query param and the Zustand store.
  • Introduce a URL → store useLayoutEffect that sets activeGenerationTopicId from the current topic query param (or null) on layout.
  • Ensure the store → URL useLayoutEffect subscribes to activeGenerationTopicId after the URL → store sync runs, and include useStore in the subscription effect deps.
  • Maintain URL updates via setTopic with history replace and throttling semantics as before.
| `src/features/GenerationTopicList/TopicUrlSync.tsx` | | Regenerate and extend i18n locale resources, including new video namespace files. |
  • Update existing per-locale JSON bundles (common, components, home, modelProvider, models, providers, spend, subscription) with the latest generated content.
  • Add new video.json namespace files for all supported locales (e.g., en-US, de-DE, etc.) to support video-related UI translations.

style, feat, fix, refactor, release alt Commit message matches style/feat/fix/refactor/release (gitmoji supported) ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow->>GitTagDB: Fetch latest stable tag ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow->>ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow: Calculate canary version ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow->>GitTagDB: Create vX.Y.(Z+1)-canary.N tag ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow-->>Developer: Canary build and release completed else Commit message does not match allowed prefixes ReleaseDesktopCanaryWorkflow-->>Developer: Skip canary build end ``` #### Flow diagram for new canary version calculation (patch+1 sequential) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start canary version calculation] --> B[Read latest stable tag latest_tag] B --> C[Strip v prefix from latest_tag to get base_version] C --> D[Split base_version into major, minor, patch] D --> E[Compute new_patch = patch + 1] E --> F[Set base_canary = major.minor.new_patch] F --> G[Initialize max_seq = 0] G --> H[Iterate tags matching v{base_canary}-canary.*] H --> I[For each tag t, extract numeric suffix seq] I --> J{Is seq non empty and seq > max_seq?} J -- Yes --> K[Set max_seq = seq] J -- No --> L[Keep current max_seq] K --> M{More matching tags?} L --> M M -- Yes --> H M -- No --> N[Compute next_seq = max_seq + 1] N --> O[Set version = base_canary-canary.next_seq] O --> P[Set tag = v{version}] P --> Q[Output version and tag] Q --> R[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Adjust canary versioning scheme from minor+1 timestamp-based to patch+1 sequential numbering per base version. |
  • Parse latest stable tag into major, minor, patch and compute base_canary using patch+1 while keeping major/minor unchanged.
  • Scan existing tags matching the new base_canary pattern to find the maximum existing canary sequence number.
  • Compute next_seq as max_seq+1 and build the new canary version/tag as X.Y.(Z+1)-canary.N.
  • Update workflow comments to document the new versioning strategy and example output.
| `.github/workflows/release-desktop-canary.yml` | | Expand canary build trigger conditions to include release-prefixed commits with optional gitmoji. |
  • Extend the grep-based commit message prefix check regex to accept release and 🚀 release prefixes in addition to style/feat/fix/refactor.
  • Update log messages and comments to reflect the new list of supported prefixes.
| `.github/workflows/release-desktop-canary.yml` | | Standardize sync main→canary PR titles to a gitmoji release style. |
  • Change gh pr create --title argument to use "🚀 release: sync main branch to canary" in both sync paths.
| `.github/workflows/sync-main-to-canary.yaml` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new unit test suite for the social service, thoroughly covering follow/unfollow, favorites, likes (including numeric vs string IDs), pagination behavior, and access token wiring by mocking the tRPC lambda client and asserting correct method calls and parameters. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce a comprehensive unit test suite for the social service API wrapper using a mocked tRPC lambda client. |
  • Add tests for follow/unfollow and follow status/count retrieval, asserting correct tRPC method calls and parameters.
  • Add tests for fetching followers/following lists and verifying pagination offset calculation based on page and pageSize.
  • Add tests for adding/removing/checking favorites and retrieving favorite agents/plugins per user.
  • Add tests for like/unlike/checkLikeStatus/toggleLike flows, including branches for numeric vs string identifiers and resulting method/argument selection.
  • Add tests for setAccessToken ensuring the lambda client is configured with the provided token.
| `src/services/__tests__/social.test.ts` |

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Extends Next.js standalone output file tracing configuration to ensure platform-specific @napi-rs/canvas native binding packages are included in Docker builds, preventing runtime errors like `DOMMatrix is not defined` when parsing PDFs. #### Sequence diagram for PDF parsing using @napi-rs/canvas in Docker after standalone tracing fix ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant DockerContainer participant NodeApp participant PdfParser participant CanvasModule participant PlatformBinding User ->> DockerContainer: Request PDF processing DockerContainer ->> NodeApp: HTTP request NodeApp ->> PdfParser: parsePdf(file) PdfParser ->> CanvasModule: require(@napi-rs/canvas) CanvasModule ->> PlatformBinding: Load platform-specific binding Note over PlatformBinding: Binding now present in Note over PlatformBinding: standalone output due to Note over PlatformBinding: new canvas-* glob PlatformBinding -->> CanvasModule: Native DOMMatrix implementation CanvasModule -->> PdfParser: Canvas API with DOMMatrix PdfParser -->> NodeApp: Parsed content NodeApp -->> DockerContainer: Response DockerContainer -->> User: PDF parsed successfully ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Broaden Next.js output file tracing includes to capture platform-specific @napi-rs/canvas native bindings required at runtime in standalone Docker builds. |
  • Add a glob pattern to include all platform-suffixed @napi-rs/canvas packages under node_modules in outputFileTracingIncludes alongside the existing generic canvas path
  • Keep existing pnpm-specific @napi-rs/canvas path patterns unchanged to continue capturing real package locations and platform bindings

## Reviewer's Guide Updates several provider model registries (Hunyuan, Wenxin, 360 Zhinao, InternLM/InternVL, Stepfun, Spark) to reflect new/latest model lineups and pricing, adds new image models, and switches Spark’s default API base URL to v2 while routing a small set of legacy models via v1 for backward compatibility. #### Sequence diagram for Spark chat request routing between v1 and v2 endpoints ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant SparkProvider participant SparkAPIv1 participant SparkAPIv2 Client->>SparkProvider: sendChat(model, payload) SparkProvider->>SparkProvider: baseURL = getBaseURLByModel(model) alt legacy_v1_model SparkProvider->>SparkAPIv1: POST /chat (model, payload) SparkAPIv1-->>SparkProvider: stream response else default_v2_model SparkProvider->>SparkAPIv2: POST /chat (model, payload) SparkAPIv2-->>SparkProvider: stream response end SparkProvider-->>Client: streaming chunks ``` #### Flow diagram for Spark getBaseURLByModel routing logic ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Start getBaseURLByModel(model)"] --> B[Apply v1Regex to model] B -->|matches lite
/generalv3
/pro-128k
/generalv3.5
/max-32k
/4.0Ultra| C[Return https://spark-api-open.xf-yun.com/v1] B -->|no match| D[Return https://spark-api-open.xf-yun.com/v2] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refresh Hunyuan chat model lineup, collapsing many legacy variants into a smaller set of current models and adjusting metadata (abilities, context windows, pricing, and release dates). |
  • Replace earlier Hunyuan T1/Turbo/TurboS/Standard/Large/vision/code/role variants with a trimmed set of core chat models
  • Reorder and relabel core models (e.g., introduce Tencent HY 2.0 Think/Instruct, move A13B and T1-latest, adjust enabled flags)
  • Normalize abilities (add/remove functionCall/search flags), contextWindowTokens, maxOutput, pricing units, and releasedAt fields on remaining models
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/hunyuan.ts` | | Extend Wenxin model registry with new ERNIE 4.5 vision and reasoning variants and Qwen image models, while deduplicating some existing entries. |
  • Add new ERNIE 4.5 Turbo VL (32K and long-context) chat models with pricing and vision ability
  • Add ERNIE 4.5 21B A3B Thinking and ERNIE X1.1/X1 Turbo 32K variants with reasoning/search/functionCall where appropriate
  • Introduce Qwen Image and Qwen Image Edit image models with size enums, parameters, and pricing
  • Remove older duplicate definitions of ERNIE X1.1 Preview and ERNIE X1 Turbo 32K at the bottom of the list to avoid duplication
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/wenxin.ts` | | Update 360 Zhinao provider to add new reasoning, vision, and third-party hosted models and modernize existing context windows and flags. |
  • Add new 360Zhinao3/2 o1.5 reasoning models, Pro 32K Thinking Vision, Turbo, and Turbo Qwen Plus with pricing and abilities
  • Adjust existing 360 Zhinao/GPT models’ contextWindowTokens and enabled flags to match current offerings
  • Register DeepSeek V3.2 (standard, Paratera, SophNet, Speciale) and seed Doubao 2.0 (Lite/Mini/Pro/Code) variants as chat models with abilities and pricing
  • Update DeepSeek R1 context length to 65,536 tokens
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/ai360.ts` | | Replace legacy InternLM/InternVL descriptors with the new Intern S1 series and InternVL3.5 entries. |
  • Introduce generic Intern-latest pointer plus concrete Intern-S1-Pro, Intern-S1, and Intern-S1-Mini models with reasoning/vision support and free pricing
  • Add InternVL3.5-latest pointer and concrete InternVL3.5-241B-A28B multimodal model with vision ability and metadata
  • Remove or repurpose prior InternLM3, InternLM2.5, InternVL2.5 latest-pointer semantics in favor of the new series
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/internlm.ts` | | Expand Stepfun chat and image model definitions with the latest Step 3.x family, cache-read pricing units, and image pricing. |
  • Add Step 3.5 Flash reasoning/vision model card with full abilities, 256K context, and CNY pricing including cacheRead
  • Augment existing Step 3.x chat models’ pricing with textInput_cacheRead units and adjust some textOutput rates to match provider docs
  • Add pricing metadata (including free and paid tiers) to existing DiT image models in the Stepfun image registry
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/stepfun.ts` | | Add Spark X2 model card and change Spark’s default base URL selection to prefer v2 while sending a whitelist of legacy models through v1. |
  • Register new Spark X2 (spark-x) chat model with reasoning, functionCall, search abilities, 128K context, and thinking extendParam, and reassign existing Spark X1.5 to model id x1
  • Change Spark provider base URL logic to use v2 by default, routing only a regex-matched set of legacy models (lite, generalv3, pro-128k, generalv3.5, max-32k, 4.0Ultra) to v1
  • Update the shared Spark params.baseURL default from v1 to v2 to keep new models on v2

ModelParamsResolver participant AnthropicCompatibleFactory participant AnthropicAPI User->>ClientApp: Send chat request with config ClientApp->>ModelParamsResolver: resolveModelExtendParams(ctx) ## Reviewer's Guide Refactors the single-message share screenshot preview to render via the standard conversation/message pipeline (with router context) so markdown and tool-call messages look identical to normal chat, and makes the generic Link component gracefully fall back to a plain anchor when used outside a React Router context. #### Sequence diagram for single-message screenshot preview rendering via conversation pipeline ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ShareMessageModal participant Preview participant MemoryRouter participant ConversationProvider participant MessageItem User->>ShareMessageModal: Open single-message share modal ShareMessageModal->>Preview: Render Preview with message Preview->>Preview: useConversationStore get context Preview->>Preview: useMemo create previewContext Preview->>MemoryRouter: Render MemoryRouter MemoryRouter->>ConversationProvider: Provide router context Preview->>ConversationProvider: Render with previewContext ConversationProvider->>ConversationProvider: Initialize with messages [message] ConversationProvider->>MessageItem: Render MessageItem id message.id index 0 MessageItem->>MessageItem: Render markdown, tool calls, errors MessageItem-->>Preview: DOM tree for message Preview-->>ShareMessageModal: Screenshot preview content ShareMessageModal-->>User: Display screenshot preview, Copy, Download ``` #### Class diagram for updated Preview and Link components ```mermaid classDiagram class Preview { +agentMeta +isBuiltinAgent +context +previewContext +displayTitle +displayDesc +render() } class ConversationProvider { +context +hasInitMessages +messages +skipFetch +render() } class MemoryRouter { +render() } class MessageItem { +id +index +render() } class Link { +href +children +otherProps +inRouterContext +render() } class RouterLink { +to +render() } class AnchorElement { +href +render() } Preview --> MemoryRouter : wraps MemoryRouter --> ConversationProvider : provides_router_context ConversationProvider --> MessageItem : renders_message Link --> RouterLink : uses_for_internal_routes Link --> AnchorElement : uses_for_external_or_no_router class LinkRenderingLogic { +isExternalLink +isInRouterContext +chooseAnchor() } LinkRenderingLogic <.. Link : encapsulates_logic LinkRenderingLogic : isExternalLink = href startsWith http LinkRenderingLogic : if isExternalLink use AnchorElement LinkRenderingLogic : else if not isInRouterContext use AnchorElement LinkRenderingLogic : else use RouterLink ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Use the standard ConversationProvider + MessageItem rendering path for single-message share previews so markdown/tool-call messages match normal chat UI. |
  • Removed bespoke preprocessing of message.content via normalizeThinkTags and processWithArtifact in the share preview component.
  • Pulled conversation context from the store and derived a preview-specific context that overrides agentId with the message’s agentId when present.
  • Wrapped the preview message rendering in a MemoryRouter and ConversationProvider configured with hasInitMessages and skipFetch to avoid network calls.
  • Rendered the preview message via MessageItem inside a Flexbox container to reuse full chat rendering behavior (markdown, tools, error states, etc.).
| `src/features/Conversation/components/ShareMessageModal/ShareImage/Preview.tsx` | | Stabilize Link behavior when rendered outside of a React Router context to prevent runtime errors in share modals and other portals. |
  • Imported useInRouterContext from react-router-dom in the shared Link component.
  • Detected when the component is rendered outside a router and in that case returned a plain tag instead of a RouterLink.
  • Kept existing behavior for external URLs (http/https) and for internal routes when a router context is available.
| `src/components/Link.tsx` | ### Assessment against linked issues | Issue | Objective | Addressed | Explanation | | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/11681 | Fix single-message screenshot so that the shared image correctly renders the message content (including markdown) instead of appearing empty or as raw/plain content. | ✅ | | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/11681 | Allow sharing of individual messages that invoked tools, ensuring the share action responds and the screenshot preview correctly renders tool-call messages. | ✅ | | ### Possibly linked issues - **#11681**: PR changes screenshot share to reuse normal MessageItem rendering, fixing raw Markdown display described in the issue. - **#11681**: The PR rewires single-message share preview to standard MessageItem rendering, fixing empty/tool-call message screenshots and share behavior. - **#11681**: The crash came from missing conversation/router context in single-message share; PR adds providers and fixes rendering. ---

updating docs, tests, and dependencies. #### Sequence diagram for DeepSeek reasoning message lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI participant ContextEngine as ContextEngine_MessageCleanupProcessor participant Runtime as ModelRuntime_DeepSeek participant OpenAIHelpers as OpenAI_ContextBuilders participant DeepSeekAPI User->>ChatUI: Send message ChatUI->>ContextEngine: Build message list ContextEngine->>ContextEngine: process(messages) Note over ContextEngine: Copies reasoning field when present ContextEngine-->>Runtime: OpenAIChatMessage[] (with reasoning) Runtime->>Runtime: params.chatCompletion.handlePayload Note over Runtime: For each assistant message Runtime->>Runtime: Transform reasoning to reasoning_content Runtime->>DeepSeekAPI: POST chat completion DeepSeekAPI-->>Runtime: Streaming or final response Runtime-->>OpenAIHelpers: OpenAIChatMessage[] (assistant reasoning attached) OpenAIHelpers->>OpenAIHelpers: convertOpenAIResponseInputs Note over OpenAIHelpers: If message has reasoning.content OpenAIHelpers->>OpenAIHelpers: Push ResponseReasoningItem OpenAIHelpers->>OpenAIHelpers: Push assistant message without reasoning OpenAIHelpers-->>ChatUI: ResponseInputItem[] (including reasoning item) ChatUI-->>User: Render reasoning trace and answer ``` #### Class diagram for updated OpenAI chat message and DeepSeek reasoning handling ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +string | UserMessageContentPart[] content +string role +string name +MessageToolCall[] tool_calls +string tool_call_id +ReasoningMeta reasoning } class ReasoningMeta { +string content +number duration } class DeepSeekPayload { +OpenAIChatMessage[] messages +string model +boolean stream } class DeepSeekParams { +ChatCompletionConfig chatCompletion } class ChatCompletionConfig { +function handlePayload(payload DeepSeekPayload) DeepSeekPayload } class MessageCleanupProcessor { +function process(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) OpenAIChatMessage[] } class ContextBuildersOpenAI { +async function convertOpenAIMessages(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) OpenAIChatMessage[] +async function convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) ResponseInputItem[] } class ResponseInputItem { +string role +string content } class ResponseReasoningItem { +SummaryItem[] summary +string type } class SummaryItem { +string text +string type } DeepSeekPayload o-- OpenAIChatMessage OpenAIChatMessage o-- ReasoningMeta DeepSeekParams o-- ChatCompletionConfig ChatCompletionConfig ..> DeepSeekPayload : transform MessageCleanupProcessor ..> OpenAIChatMessage : preserves reasoning ContextBuildersOpenAI ..> OpenAIChatMessage : consumes ContextBuildersOpenAI ..> ResponseInputItem : produces ContextBuildersOpenAI ..> ResponseReasoningItem : produces reasoning ResponseReasoningItem o-- SummaryItem class DeepSeekHandlePayloadImpl { +function handlePayload(payload DeepSeekPayload) DeepSeekPayload } DeepSeekHandlePayloadImpl ..|> ChatCompletionConfig DeepSeekHandlePayloadImpl ..> OpenAIChatMessage : map messages class ReasoningExtractionLogic { +function extractReasoning(message OpenAIChatMessage) ResponseReasoningItem } ReasoningExtractionLogic ..> ResponseReasoningItem ContextBuildersOpenAI ..> ReasoningExtractionLogic ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Harden media fetching against SSRF and centralize SSE/fetch utilities into a new shared package. |
  • Replace bespoke image URL fetching with ssrf-safe-fetch-based imageUrlToBase64 that uses SSRF-safe fetch on the server and native fetch in the browser.
  • Introduce @lobechat/fetch-sse package exposing fetchSSE, parseError, and helpers, and update chat services, Electron RPC fetch, and tests to consume it instead of '@/utils/fetch'.
  • Extend ssrf-safe-fetch package with browser/node conditional exports and add a browser implementation that simply delegates to window.fetch.
  • Update Google model-runtime video handling to reuse imageUrlToBase64 for binary URL->base64 conversion.

## Reviewer's Guide Refactors image fetching to use a new SSRF-safe fetch utility and shared SSE fetch package, adds DeepSeek “reasoning” compatibility handling across providers, improves OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/Ollama message conversions for reasoning and media, and updates docs, changelog, dependencies, tests, and GitHub workflow accordingly. #### Sequence diagram for DeepSeek reasoning handling and OpenAI response inputs ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI participant ChatService participant MessageCleanupProcessor participant OpenAIContextBuilder participant DeepSeekProvider as DeepSeekChatCompletionHandler participant DeepSeekAPI User->>ChatUI: Enter message ChatUI->>ChatService: send messages ChatService->>MessageCleanupProcessor: process(rawMessages) MessageCleanupProcessor-->>ChatService: cleanedMessages Note over MessageCleanupProcessor: Keeps reasoning object ChatService->>OpenAIContextBuilder: convertOpenAIResponseInputs(cleanedMessages) OpenAIContextBuilder->>OpenAIContextBuilder: extract reasoning.content OpenAIContextBuilder-->>ChatService: responseInputItems ChatService->>OpenAIContextBuilder: convertOpenAIMessages(cleanedMessages) OpenAIContextBuilder->>OpenAIContextBuilder: strip reasoning OpenAIContextBuilder-->>ChatService: requestMessages ChatService->>DeepSeekProvider: handlePayload({ messages: requestMessages, model: deepseek-r1 }) DeepSeekProvider->>DeepSeekProvider: move reasoning.content -> reasoning_content DeepSeekProvider-->>ChatService: payloadWithReasoningContent ChatService->>DeepSeekAPI: chatCompletion(payloadWithReasoningContent) DeepSeekAPI-->>ChatService: streaming response ChatService-->>ChatUI: render assistant reply ``` #### Class diagram for updated chat message, reasoning handling, and media conversion ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIChatMessage { +string | UserMessageContentPart[] content +string role +string name +string tool_call_id +MessageToolCall[] tool_calls +Reasoning reasoning } class Reasoning { +string content +number duration } class MessageCleanupProcessor { +process(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) OpenAIChatMessage[] } class OpenAIContextBuilder { +convertOpenAIMessages(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) Promise~OpenAIChatMessage[]~ +convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages OpenAIChatMessage[]) Promise~ResponseInputItem[]~ } class DeepSeekChatCompletionHandler { +handlePayload(payload ChatCompletionPayload) ChatCompletionPayload } ## Reviewer's Guide Migrates the LobeChat frontend from Next.js App Router to a Vite + React Router SPA while keeping the Next.js backend, by introducing a SPA entry and global provider, a Next.js catch-all route that serves Vite-built HTML with runtime config injection, refactoring the Next-specific abstraction layer and third‑party integrations to framework-agnostic adapters, updating env handling, and wiring new build/dev/Docker flows for dual desktop/mobile bundles. #### Sequence diagram for SPA HTML request via Next.js catch-all ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as Browser participant M as Middleware_define_config participant R as SPACatchAllRoute participant C as getServerGlobalConfig participant T as spaHtmlTemplates_or_ViteDev U->>M: GET /chat M->>M: Check path M->>M: isNextjsRoute = nextjsOnlyRoutes.some alt isNextjsRoute true M-->>U: Rewrite to Next.js auth route else SPA route M->>R: NextResponse.next()\npass to (spa)/[[...path]] R->>R: Detect isMobile from UA R->>R: Resolve locale\nfrom LOBE_LOCALE_COOKIE or headers R->>C: getServerGlobalConfig() C-->>R: GlobalServerConfig R->>R: getServerFeatureFlagsValue R->>R: buildAnalyticsConfig R->>R: buildThemeConfig R->>R: buildClientEnv R->>T: getTemplate(isMobile) alt NODE_ENV=development T->>T: fetch VITE_DEV_ORIGIN index.html T->>T: rewriteViteAssetUrls else production T->>T: read public/spa/[desktop|mobile]/index.html end T-->>R: HTML template R->>R: serializeForHtml(SPAServerConfig) R->>R: Inject window.__SERVER_CONFIG__\nReplace LOCALE, DIR placeholders R-->>U: HTML response U->>U: Load JS bundle\nBootstrap React Router SPA end ``` #### Class diagram for SPA server config and global provider ```mermaid classDiagram class SPAServerConfig { +AnalyticsConfig analyticsConfig +SPAClientEnv clientEnv +GlobalServerConfig config +Partial~IFeatureFlags~ featureFlags +boolean isMobile +string locale +SPAThemeConfig theme } class AnalyticsConfig { +GoogleConfig google +PlausibleConfig plausible +UmamiConfig umami +ClarityConfig clarity +PosthogConfig posthog +ReactScanConfig reactScan +VercelConfig vercel +DesktopAnalyticsConfig desktop } class SPAClientEnv { +string marketBaseUrl +string pyodideIndexUrl +string pyodidePipIndexUrl +string s3FilePath } class SPAThemeConfig { +boolean cdnUseGlobal +string customFontFamily +string customFontURL } class Window { +SPAServerConfig __SERVER_CONFIG__ } class SPAGlobalProvider { +render(children) } class ServerConfigStoreProvider { +featureFlags +isMobile +serverConfig } class BrowserRouter { } class Routes { } class desktopRoutes { } class mobileRoutes { } Window --> SPAServerConfig : holds SPAServerConfig --> AnalyticsConfig : has SPAServerConfig --> SPAClientEnv : has SPAServerConfig --> SPAThemeConfig : has SPAGlobalProvider --> SPAServerConfig : reads SPAGlobalProvider --> ServerConfigStoreProvider : composes SPAGlobalProvider --> BrowserRouter : wraps BrowserRouter --> Routes : renders Routes --> desktopRoutes : uses Routes --> mobileRoutes : uses ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Replace Next.js navigation and component adapters with SPA-compatible react-router-dom and plain React implementations while preserving the existing public API. |
  • Reimplemented navigation helpers (useRouter, usePathname, useParams, useSearchParams, redirect, notFound, useServerInsertedHTML) to use react-router-dom and custom error types, keeping the old API shape for callers.
  • Replaced the next/dynamic-based dynamic() wrapper with a React.lazy + Suspense implementation that accepts the same loader/options contract.
  • Replaced the next/image-based Image wrapper with a forwardRef adapter that supports StaticImageData-like objects and the fill layout behavior.
  • Replaced the next/link-based Link wrapper with a react-router-dom Link adapter that renders external URLs as plain elements.
  • Centralized these adapters behind src/libs/next/index.ts so existing imports continue to work in SPA mode.

GitHub-->>AutoTagWorkflow: Trigger workflow on PR event AutoTagWorkflow->>DetermineShouldTagStep: Run determine should_tag script DetermineShouldTagStep->>DetermineShouldTagStep: Test PR_TITLE against regex including build prefix alt Title matches build prefix DetermineShouldTagStep-->>AutoTagWorkflow: should_tag=true AutoTagWorkflow-->>GitHub: Proceed with hotfix auto-tag and release path else Title does not match any allowed prefix DetermineShouldTagStep-->>AutoTagWorkflow: should_tag=false AutoTagWorkflow-->>GitHub: Log that prefix is not style/feat/fix/refactor/hotfix/build end ``` #### Flow diagram for updated auto-tag-release PR title prefix evaluation ```mermaid flowchart LR PRTitle["PR title"] --> CheckPrefix["Match title against allowed prefixes: style|feat|fix|refactor|hotfix|build (each optionally with corresponding emoji)"] CheckPrefix -->|matches style| StylePath["Set should_tag=true"] CheckPrefix -->|matches feat| FeatPath["Set should_tag=true"] CheckPrefix -->|matches fix| FixPath["Set should_tag=true"] CheckPrefix -->|matches refactor| RefactorPath["Set should_tag=true"] CheckPrefix -->|matches hotfix| HotfixPath["Set should_tag=true"] CheckPrefix -->|matches build| BuildPath["Set should_tag=true (new behavior)"] CheckPrefix -->|no match| NoTag["Set should_tag=false and log that title prefix is not style/feat/fix/refactor/hotfix/build"] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Extend PR title regex gate so build-prefixed PRs trigger auto-tag-release. |
