body:
Update: added a dev-environment cold-start metric for the first browser open.

## Methodology

- Route: `/desktop-onboarding`
- Cold-start mode: `vite --force`
- Browser state: fresh Chrome profile, cache disabled
- Metric definition: time from starting the Vite command to the final LCP of the first browser navigation
- Reported as:
  - `route-ready`: time until the target route can be opened as a real page
  - `nav LCP`: LCP measured from browser navigation start
  - `total`: `route-ready + nav LCP`
- Samples: 2 valid runs per variant

## Results

| Variant | Route-ready | Nav FCP | Nav LCP | Total start -> LCP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Vite 7 | 1.61s | 13.79s | 30.50s | 32.11s |
| Vite 8 default | 16.83s | 0.07s | 5.96s | 22.79s |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle | 16.09s | 0.10s | 1.42s | 17.51s |

## Relative change

| Comparison | Delta |
|---|---:|
| Vite 8 default vs Vite 7 | -29.0% total |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle vs Vite 7 | -45.5% total |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle vs Vite 8 default | -23.2% total |

## Interpretation

- Under this cold-start dev metric, Vite 8 improves the end-to-end first-open experience materially versus Vite 7.
- The main shape of the improvement is different from production build metrics:
  - Vite 8 increases the route-openable wait before the first browser navigation.
  - However, once the page is actually opened, browser-side paint/LCP becomes much faster.
- DevBundle provides the best overall result in this measurement set.

## Note

The terminal `VITE ready in ...` banner stayed below ~0.5s in all three cases. The dominant difference in this benchmark therefore comes from route-level first-open work rather than the CLI-ready banner itself.
author: Innei

body:
Correction to the previous dev-environment metric comment: the earlier `Route-ready` figure for `Vite 8 default` was methodologically incorrect.

## What was wrong

The previous script inserted a **pre-navigation polling phase** before opening the browser:

- it repeatedly fetched the target route
- it waited until the route stopped returning the `Bundling in progress` placeholder
- only then did it launch the browser and start measuring LCP

That means the old `Route-ready` number was **not** “Vite default startup time”. It was an artifact of the harness, because it turned route pre-compilation / warm-up into a pseudo-startup metric.

This especially overstated `Vite 8 default`, where the previous comment showed an incorrect `Route-ready ~16s`.

## Corrected methodology

The corrected measurement is:

1. start the Vite command
2. wait for terminal `VITE ... ready in ...`
3. open the browser **immediately**
4. measure until the **final app page** reaches LCP

For DevBundle, the `Bundling in progress` placeholder is explicitly ignored; the measurement stops only after the real app page appears and its LCP stabilizes.

Route used for all runs: `/desktop-onboarding`

Samples: 2 valid cold-start runs per variant (`vite --force`)

## Corrected results

| Variant | Terminal ready | Browser open -> final LCP | Total start -> final LCP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vite 7 | 0.62s | 29.72s | 30.38s |
| Vite 8 default | 0.58s | 21.72s | 22.44s |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle | 0.49s | 15.78s | 16.29s |

## Relative change

| Comparison | Delta |
|---|---:|
| Vite 8 default vs Vite 7 | -26.1% total |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle vs Vite 7 | -46.4% total |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle vs Vite 8 default | -27.4% total |

## Interpretation

- The previous `Route-ready ~16s` for `Vite 8 default` should be ignored.
- Under the corrected methodology, all three variants have similar terminal-ready times (all below 1s).
- The real difference is in the browser-side first-open path after the terminal is ready.
- `Vite 8 default` is materially faster than `Vite 7`.
- `Vite 8 + DevBundle` is the best result in this dev first-open benchmark.
author: Innei

body:
Additional follow-up for upstream attention:

The corrected dev first-open benchmark still shows an inversion that looks suspicious.

## Why this is concerning

Our production SPA build is already down to **7.63s**.

But in dev mode, the first-open path is still significantly slower than that:

| Variant | Total start -> final app LCP |
|---|---:|
| production `build:spa` | 7.63s |
| Vite 8 default (dev cold start) | 22.44s |
| Vite 8 + DevBundle (dev cold start) | 16.29s |

So even after correcting the earlier measurement bug:

- `Vite 8 default` is about **2.9x** slower than production build
- `Vite 8 + DevBundle` is still about **2.1x** slower than production build

If we compare against the earlier rough internal observation of “~5s build”, the dev-bundled path is roughly **3x** slower.

## Why this likely needs upstream attention

A dev cold-start path being materially slower than a full production build is counterintuitive.

This does **not** look like a normal “dev is slower than prod at runtime” effect only. The gap is large enough that it suggests there may be avoidable overhead in the current dev bundling path itself, especially in the Rolldown / bundled-dev flow.

## Suggested follow-up

- treat this as an upstream follow-up item rather than only a local tuning task
- reduce the case to a minimal reproduction if possible
- check whether the dev bundled compile path is doing significantly more work than the production build pipeline

At minimum, this should be called out explicitly as an abnormal result from the current upgrade evaluation.
author: Innei

Experiment update: I tested production runtime metrics again after disabling `strictExecutionOrder` **only in production builds**, while keeping it **enabled in dev**.

## Change under test

Production output now uses:

- `strictExecutionOrder: false`

Dev output still uses:

- `strictExecutionOrder: true`

This isolates the production-only effect of `strictExecutionOrder` without changing dev-mode behavior.

## Verification path

- rebuilt production bundle with `bun run build:spa`
- served the rebuilt `dist/desktop` via local static server under `/_spa/`
- reran the same desktop Lighthouse cold-cache path as before
- samples: 2 runs averaged

## Build-side side effect

| Metric | Previous Vite 8 prod | `strictExecutionOrder` off in prod |
|---|---:|---:|
| Build time | 7.63s | 6.64s |
| Peak RSS | 4.76 GiB | 4.75 GiB |

## Runtime metrics

| Metric | Previous Vite 8 prod | `strictExecutionOrder` off in prod | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Performance score | 0.285 | 0.595 | +108.8% |
| FCP | 5.22s | 0.07s | -98.6% |
| LCP | 19.32s | 1.45s | -92.5% |
| Speed Index | 9.73s | 3.11s | -68.0% |
| TBT | 829ms | 1001ms | +20.8% |
| Interactive | 19.87s | 1.32s | -93.3% |
| CLS | 0.0089 | 0.0301 | worse |
| Total byte weight | 29.05 MB | 28.43 MB | -2.1% |
| Requests | 226 | 228 | +0.9% |
| Main-thread work | 1681ms | 1610ms | -4.2% |

## Initial-load graph impact

This change did **not** materially fix the initial graph by itself, but it did move it slightly in the right direction:

| Metric | Previous Vite 8 prod | `strictExecutionOrder` off in prod |
|---|---:|---:|
| `modulepreload` count | 191 | 187 |
| Initial JS count | 192 | 188 |
| Initial JS size | 19.93 MiB | 19.31 MiB |
| Initial JS gzip | 5.23 MiB | 5.06 MiB |
| `index.html` size | 25.51 KiB | 25.20 KiB |

## Interpretation

This experiment suggests that the runtime regression is highly sensitive to `strictExecutionOrder` in production.

The chunk explosion / initial-load graph is still present and should still be investigated independently, but this isolated switch alone appears to remove most of the observed runtime regression in the current Lighthouse benchmark.

Caveat: the runtime delta here is large enough that it is worth sanity-checking further, but the two reruns were internally consistent.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds a reusable composite GitHub Action for publishing desktop release artifacts to S3 and wires it into stable, canary, and nightly workflows so all channels upload their update manifests and installers to channel-specific S3 paths. #### Sequence diagram for canary desktop release publishing to S3 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Dev as developer participant GitHub as github_actions participant WF as workflow_release_desktop_canary participant JobBuild as job_build_release participant JobMerge as job_merge_mac_files participant JobVersion as job_calculate_version participant JobS3 as job_publish_s3 participant Action as action_desktop_publish_s3 participant S3 as s3_bucket Dev->>GitHub: push tag or dispatch canary release GitHub->>WF: start workflow_release_desktop_canary WF->>JobBuild: run build jobs and upload artifacts JobBuild-->>GitHub: artifact merged-release WF->>JobMerge: merge mac files JobMerge-->>GitHub: merged-release artifact WF->>JobVersion: calculate version JobVersion-->>WF: outputs version WF->>JobS3: start publish-s3 (needs merge-mac-files, calculate-version) JobS3->>Action: uses .github/actions/desktop-publish-s3 Action->>GitHub: download-artifact merged-release Action->>S3: upload installers to s3://bucket/canary/version/ Action->>S3: upload canary*.yml and latest*.yml manifests Action->>S3: upload optional canary-renderer.yml S3-->>Dev: hosts update manifests and installers for canary channel ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce a reusable composite action that encapsulates S3 upload logic for desktop releases, parameterized by channel and version. |
  • Create `.github/actions/desktop-publish-s3/action.yml` composite action that downloads the merged-release artifact and lists its contents.
  • Configure the action to accept channel, version, AWS credentials, and S3 configuration (bucket, region, endpoint) as inputs.
  • Implement upload script that pushes all release binaries to `s3://{bucket}/{channel}/{version}/` and logs the uploaded files.
  • Generate channel-specific updater YAML files from `latest*.yml`, rewriting URLs to include the version directory prefix.
  • Optionally generate a `{channel}-renderer.yml` manifest when a renderer tarball is present, including checksum, size, and release date metadata.
  • Upload manifest files (both `{channel}*.yml` and `latest*.yml`) to both the channel root and versioned channel directory in S3.
| `.github/actions/desktop-publish-s3/action.yml` | | Refactor the stable desktop release workflow to use the new composite S3 publish action instead of inline bash, preserving behavior while centralizing logic. |
  • Remove the large inline bash step that handled stable-channel S3 uploads, manifest generation, and logging.
  • Add a checkout step and invoke the `.github/actions/desktop-publish-s3` composite action in the `publish-s3` job.
  • Pass stable-specific parameters (channel `stable`, version from `check-stable`, and S3-related secrets) into the composite action inputs.
  • Keep existing job dependencies, conditions, and naming for the stable `publish-s3` job so triggering behavior remains unchanged.
| `.github/workflows/release-desktop-stable.yml` | | Enable S3 publishing for canary and nightly desktop release workflows using the shared composite action so those channels also upload update artifacts. |
  • Add a `publish-s3` job to the canary workflow that depends on `merge-mac-files` and `calculate-version`.
  • Within the canary `publish-s3` job, check out the repo and call the composite action with `channel: canary`, version from `calculate-version`, and S3-related secrets.
  • Add a similar `publish-s3` job to the nightly workflow with dependencies on `merge-mac-files` and `calculate-version`.
  • In the nightly job, call the composite action with `channel: nightly`, version from `calculate-version`, and the same S3 configuration inputs.
| `.github/workflows/release-desktop-canary.yml`
`.github/workflows/release-desktop-nightly.yml` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Adds UI and backend support for clearing desktop and web hotkey bindings by treating an empty accelerator as a disabled shortcut, prevents mutation of the default shortcut config, and updates UI dependencies and localization to support a clear-binding control. #### Sequence diagram for clearing a desktop hotkey binding ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant DesktopSettings as DesktopHotkeySetting participant HotkeyInput participant DesktopAPI as updateDesktopHotkey participant ShortcutManager User->>DesktopSettings: Click clear on hotkey DesktopSettings->>HotkeyInput: render allowClear, texts.clear User->>HotkeyInput: Clear binding HotkeyInput->>DesktopSettings: onClear() DesktopSettings->>DesktopAPI: updateDesktopHotkey(id, "") DesktopAPI->>ShortcutManager: updateShortcutConfig(id, "") ShortcutManager->>ShortcutManager: validate accelerator type ShortcutManager->>ShortcutManager: trimmedAccelerator = "" ShortcutManager->>ShortcutManager: shortcutsConfig[id] = "" ShortcutManager->>ShortcutManager: saveShortcutsConfig() ShortcutManager->>ShortcutManager: registerConfiguredShortcuts() (skip empty) ShortcutManager-->>DesktopAPI: { success: true } DesktopAPI-->>DesktopSettings: result.success DesktopSettings-->>User: Show hotkey.updateSuccess message ``` #### Updated class diagram for ShortcutManager clear-hotkey support ```mermaid classDiagram class ShortcutManager { - shortcutsConfig Map~string, string~ + loadShortcutsConfig() void + saveShortcutsConfig() void + registerConfiguredShortcuts() void + updateShortcutConfig(id string, accelerator string) UpdateResult + convertAcceleratorFormat(accelerator string) string } class UpdateResult { + success boolean + errorType string } class DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS_CONFIG { <> } ShortcutManager --> DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS_CONFIG : uses copy of ShortcutManager --> UpdateResult : returns ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Enable clearing desktop hotkey bindings in the settings UI and wire them to the desktop hotkey update API. |
  • Refactor desktop hotkey update logic in the settings screen into a reusable async updateHotkey helper that manages loading state and success/error messaging.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Limits when assistant message loading spinners are shown by threading the message generation state into DisplayContent and Assistant/Task/AssistantGroup message components, so that empty or LOADING_FLAT messages only render ContentLoading while the message is actively generating. #### Sequence diagram for assistant message loading indicator behavior ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant AssistantMessageContent participant DisplayContent participant ContentLoading participant ConversationStore User->>AssistantMessageContent: Trigger assistant generation AssistantMessageContent->>ConversationStore: generating = true AssistantMessageContent->>DisplayContent: render(id, content, isMessageGenerating = true) alt content empty or LOADING_FLAT and isMessageGenerating true DisplayContent->>ContentLoading: render(id) else content present or isMessageGenerating false DisplayContent-->>ContentLoading: do not render end User->>ConversationStore: Generation completes ConversationStore-->>AssistantMessageContent: generating = false AssistantMessageContent->>DisplayContent: render(id, content, isMessageGenerating = false) alt content empty or LOADING_FLAT and isMessageGenerating false DisplayContent-->>ContentLoading: render null else content present and isMessageGenerating false DisplayContent-->>ContentLoading: do not render end ``` #### Class diagram for updated conversation message loading components ```mermaid classDiagram class DisplayContent { +string id +string content +boolean hasImages +boolean isMultimodal +boolean isToolCallGenerating +boolean isMessageGenerating +render() } class AssistantMessageContent { +string id +string content +boolean generating +boolean showImageItems +render() } class TaskMessageContent { +string id +string content +boolean generating +boolean showImageItems +render() } class AssistantGroupMessageContent { +string id +string content +boolean hasTools +boolean isGenerating +render() } class ContentLoading { +string id +render() } class ConversationStore { +isMessageGenerating(id) } AssistantMessageContent --> DisplayContent : passes isMessageGenerating TaskMessageContent --> DisplayContent : passes isMessageGenerating AssistantGroupMessageContent --> ConversationStore : useConversationStore(isMessageGenerating) AssistantGroupMessageContent --> ContentLoading : conditional render DisplayContent --> ContentLoading : conditional render ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Gate loading spinner rendering on actual message generation state for generic DisplayContent. |
  • Add optional isMessageGenerating prop to DisplayContent component signature and props destructuring.
  • Update loading conditions to render ContentLoading only when content is empty or LOADING_FLAT and isMessageGenerating is true, otherwise render nothing.
  • Preserve existing isToolCallGenerating early return behavior while restructuring the loading branch.
| `src/features/Conversation/Messages/components/DisplayContent.tsx` | | Propagate generating state from Assistant and Task messages down into DisplayContent. |
  • Pass generating flag from Assistant message component into DisplayContent as isMessageGenerating.

| `src/features/Conversation/Messages/Assistant/components/MessageContent.tsx`

  • Read isMessageGenerating for the message id from the conversation store via messageStateSelectors.isMessageGenerating.
  • Change handling of empty content without tools to only render ContentLoading when isGenerating is true, otherwise render null.
  • Change LOADING_FLAT handling to only render ContentLoading when isGenerating is true, otherwise render null.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds two new evaluation modes: an LLM-based answer relevance judge and an external scoring mode, wires them through the rubric matcher/evaluation pipeline, exposes an external-eval API surface and CLI workflow, updates metrics/status handling and UI to reflect the new states, and introduces several new research dataset presets and import improvements. #### Sequence diagram for external evaluation workflow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor ExternalScorer participant CLI as cli_eval_command participant API as agentEvalExternalRouter participant RunTopicModel as AgentEvalRunTopicModel participant ThreadModel as ThreadModel participant RunService as AgentEvalRunService participant RunModel as AgentEvalRunModel %% 1. Discover topics awaiting external scoring ExternalScorer->>CLI: eval run-topics list --run-id CLI->>API: runTopicsList(runId, onlyExternal=true) API->>RunTopicModel: findByRunId(runId) RunTopicModel-->>API: topics(status=external,...) API-->>CLI: external topics CLI-->>ExternalScorer: display pending topics %% 2. Inspect messages for a topic/thread ExternalScorer->>CLI: eval messages list --topic-id --thread-id CLI->>API: messagesList(topicId, threadId) API->>ThreadModel: queryByTopicId(topicId) ThreadModel-->>API: threads API->>MessagesTable: select messages(topicId,threadId) MessagesTable-->>API: messages API-->>CLI: messages with content CLI-->>ExternalScorer: show conversation for scoring %% 3. Report a single scored result ExternalScorer->>CLI: eval run-topic report-result --run-id --topic-id --thread-id --score --correct --result-json CLI->>API: runTopicReportResult(runId, topicId, threadId, score, correct, result) API->>RunTopicModel: findByRunId(runId) RunTopicModel-->>API: runTopic API->>RunTopicModel: updateByRunAndTopic(runId, topicId, evalResult{awaitingExternalEval,externalThreadResults}, status) RunTopicModel-->>API: topic updated %% 4. Recompute run-level aggregation API->>RunService: evaluateAndFinalizeRun(run, runTopics) RunService->>RunModel: update(runId, metrics, status) RunModel-->>RunService: persisted run RunService-->>API: metrics, status (external|completed|failed) API-->>CLI: receipt(runStatus, topicFinalized,...) CLI-->>ExternalScorer: print success or error ``` #### Class diagram for updated eval matchers and rubric types ```mermaid classDiagram class RubricType { <> equals contains similar levenshtein external rubric answer-relevance } class RubricConfigLLM { +string provider +string model +string systemRole +string criteria +string judgePrompt } class EvalBenchmarkRubric { +string id +string name +RubricType type +any config +number threshold } class MatchContext { +string judgeModel +generateObject(payload) Promise~any~ } class MatchResult { +boolean passed +number score +string reason } class MatcherIndex { +match(input, actual, expected, rubric, context) Promise~MatchResult~ } class LlmEqMatcher { +matchLLMEq(question, actual, expected, rubric, context) Promise~MatchResult~ } class LlmRubricMatcher { +matchLLMRubric(actual, expected, rubric, context) Promise~MatchResult~ } class ExternalMatcher { +matchExternal() Promise~MatchResult~ } class EvaluateFunction { +evaluate(testCases, rubrics, context) Promise~void~ } RubricType <.. EvalBenchmarkRubric RubricConfigLLM <.. EvalBenchmarkRubric MatchContext <.. MatcherIndex MatchResult <.. MatcherIndex MatcherIndex ..> LlmEqMatcher : uses (answer-relevance) MatcherIndex ..> LlmRubricMatcher : uses (llm-rubric) MatcherIndex ..> ExternalMatcher : uses (external) EvaluateFunction ..> MatcherIndex : calls match() EvaluateFunction --> MatchContext EvaluateFunction --> EvalBenchmarkRubric ``` #### Class diagram for updated external eval run and topic types ```mermaid classDiagram class EvalRunStatus { <> aborted completed external failed pending running } class AgentEvalRunStatus { <> aborted completed external failed idle pending running } class EvalRunMetrics { +number totalCases +number passedCases +number failedCases +number errorCases +number timeoutCases +number externalCases +number passRate +number avgScore +number cost +number llmCalls +number duration } class EvalRubricScore { +string rubricId +number score +string reason } class EvalThreadResult { +string threadId +string status // error | external | failed | passed | running | timeout | completed +boolean passed +number score +number cost +number duration +number llmCalls +number toolCalls +string error +EvalRubricScore[] rubricScores } class EvalRunTopicResult { +boolean passed +number score +string completionReason +EvalRubricScore[] rubricScores +EvalThreadResult[] threads +boolean awaitingExternalEval +record externalResult +record externalThreadResults } class AgentEvalRun { +string id +string datasetId +AgentEvalRunStatus status +EvalRunMetrics metrics +record config +Date startedAt } class AgentEvalRunTopic { +string runId +string topicId +string testCaseId +string status // pending | running | passed | failed | error | timeout | external | completed +number score +boolean passed +EvalRunTopicResult evalResult } EvalRunMetrics <.. AgentEvalRun EvalRunStatus <.. AgentEvalRun AgentEvalRunStatus <.. AgentEvalRun EvalRunTopicResult <.. AgentEvalRunTopic EvalThreadResult <.. EvalRunTopicResult EvalRubricScore <.. EvalRunTopicResult EvalRubricScore <.. EvalThreadResult AgentEvalRun "1" o-- "*" AgentEvalRunTopic : aggregates topics ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce LLM-based answer relevance matcher and make matchers input-aware. |
  • Extend rubric match() API and evaluate() to pass the original testCase.input into matchers.
  • Add matchLLMEq LLM-as-judge matcher that compares question/actual/expected via a JSON-scored schema and integrates it under the new answer-relevance rubric type.
  • Harden matchLLMRubric to fail closed when the judge returns no score.
  • Update rubric and eval config types/locales and dataset edit UI to support answer-relevance and richer LLM judge configuration.

initialization hooks and tests accordingly. #### Sequence diagram for contextEngineering using persona-based user memory ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant ContextEngineering participant MemoryManager participant UserMemoryStore Caller->>ContextEngineering: contextEngineering(enableUserMemories=true, ...) activate ContextEngineering ContextEngineering->>MemoryManager: topicMemories deactivate MemoryManager ContextEngineering->>MemoryManager: resolveUserPersona() activate MemoryManager MemoryManager->>UserMemoryStore: getUserMemoryStoreState() UserMemoryStore-->>MemoryManager: memoryState MemoryManager-->>ContextEngineering: persona | undefined deactivate MemoryManager ContextEngineering->>MemoryManager: combineUserMemoryData(topicMemories, ContextEngineering ``` #### Class diagram for updated user memory model with persona ```mermaid classDiagram class UserMemoryData { +RetrieveMemoryResult activities +RetrieveMemoryResult contexts +RetrieveMemoryResult experiences +UserMemoryPersona persona +RetrieveMemoryResult preferences } class UserMemoryPersona { +string narrative +string tagline } class MemoryManager { UserMemoryData } class TopicMemoryResolverContext { <> } UserMemoryData --> UserMemoryPersona : uses MemoryManager --> UserMemoryData : builds MemoryManager --> UserMemoryPersona : reads MemoryManager --> TopicMemoryResolverContext : optional ctx ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Switch from global identities to a persona-based user memory model and adapt memory combination logic. |
  • Remove identity-based imports and selectors from the memory manager

  • Change contextEngineering to resolve user memories by combining topic memories with resolveUserPersona instead of resolveGlobalIdentities
  • Update memory manager exports to expose resolveUserPersona and stop exporting resolveGlobalIdentities

body:
## Reviewer's Guide Introduces an initial LobeHub CLI app that authenticates via device code flow, persists encrypted credentials, connects to a device gateway over WebSocket to execute local tools (filesystem and shell) on demand, and adds a reusable device-gateway client package (WebSocket + HTTP) shared by the CLI commands. #### Sequence diagram for CLI connect and remote tool execution ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor U as User participant CLI as lh connect participant Auth as resolveToken participant Cred as getValidToken / credentials participant GW as GatewayClient participant DG as Device gateway WS participant Tools as executeToolCall U->>CLI: Run `lh connect [options]` CLI->>Auth: resolveToken(options) alt explicit token Auth-->>CLI: token, userId else service token Auth-->>CLI: serviceToken, userId else stored credentials Auth->>Cred: getValidToken() Cred-->>Auth: accessToken (refreshed if needed) Auth-->>CLI: token, userId end CLI->>GW: new GatewayClient({ token, userId, gatewayUrl }) CLI->>GW: connect() GW->>DG: WebSocket connect /ws?deviceId=...&userId=... DG-->>GW: open GW->>DG: send auth message { type: auth, token } DG-->>GW: auth_success GW-->>CLI: emit connected loop heartbeat GW->>DG: heartbeat DG-->>GW: heartbeat_ack end DG-->>GW: system_info_request (optional) GW-->>CLI: emit system_info_request CLI->>GW: sendSystemInfoResponse(systemInfo) GW->>DG: system_info_response DG-->>GW: tool_call_request { apiName, arguments, identifier } GW-->>CLI: emit tool_call_request CLI->>Tools: executeToolCall(apiName, arguments) Tools->>Tools: map apiName→handler Tools->>Tools: parse JSON args alt file/shell tool executes ok Tools-->>CLI: { content, success: true } else error in tool Tools-->>CLI: { content: "", error, success: false } end CLI->>GW: sendToolCallResponse({ requestId, result }) GW->>DG: tool_call_response U->>CLI: Ctrl+C (SIGINT) CLI->>Tools: cleanupAllProcesses() CLI->>GW: disconnect() GW->>DG: close(1000, Client disconnect) GW-->>CLI: emit disconnected ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add filesystem helper tools for reading, writing, editing, listing, globbing, grepping, and searching local files for use by remote tool calls. |
  • Implement readLocalFile with optional line-range or full-content reading and metadata reporting with error fallback payloads instead of throwing.
  • Add writeLocalFile and editLocalFile utilities, including diff generation and line-add/delete counting for string replacements with optional replace-all behavior.
  • Provide listLocalFiles, globLocalFiles, grepContent (ripgrep-based with JSON output and fallback), and searchLocalFiles utilities that respect ignore patterns and handle errors gracefully.
| `apps/cli/src/tools/file.ts` | | Add shell execution tools that support foreground/background commands, streaming output retrieval, and process cleanup. |
  • Implement runCommand to spawn shell commands with configurable timeout, ANSI stripping and truncation of output, and background mode that tracks processes by UUID.
  • Implement getCommandOutput to incrementally read buffered stdout/stderr from background commands with optional regex filtering and running status reporting.
  • Implement killCommand and cleanupAllProcesses to terminate tracked background processes and clean internal state.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds persistence of the last-used OAuth provider on the sign-in page using localStorage, reorders the provider list to surface it first, and visually highlights it with a ribbon badge while wiring the state through the sign-in hook and page. #### Sequence diagram for social sign-in storing last used provider ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant SignInPage participant SignInEmailStep participant useSignInHook participant useBusinessSignin participant AuthServer participant LocalStorage User->>SignInPage: load SignInPage->>useSignInHook: call useSignIn useSignInHook->>LocalStorage: getItem(lobehub:auth:last-provider:v1) LocalStorage-->>useSignInHook: lastAuthProvider or null useSignInHook-->>SignInPage: handlers, lastAuthProvider, sortedProviders SignInPage->>SignInEmailStep: render with lastAuthProvider and oAuthSSOProviders User->>SignInEmailStep: click provider button SignInEmailStep->>useSignInHook: handleSocialSignIn(provider) useSignInHook->>useBusinessSignin: preSocialSigninCheck(provider) useBusinessSignin-->>useSignInHook: checkResult alt preSocialSigninCheck failed useSignInHook-->>SignInEmailStep: abort sign-in else preSocialSigninCheck passed useSignInHook->>LocalStorage: setItem(lobehub:auth:last-provider:v1, provider) useSignInHook->>useBusinessSignin: getAdditionalData() useBusinessSignin-->>useSignInHook: additionalData useSignInHook->>AuthServer: start sign-in with provider and additionalData AuthServer-->>User: redirect or sign-in result end ``` #### Sequence diagram for sign-in page rendering last used provider first ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant SignInPage participant useSignInHook participant SignInEmailStep participant LocalStorage User->>SignInPage: visit /signin SignInPage->>useSignInHook: call useSignIn useSignInHook->>LocalStorage: getItem(lobehub:auth:last-provider:v1) LocalStorage-->>useSignInHook: lastAuthProvider or null useSignInHook->>useSignInHook: resolve providers (ssoProviders or oAuthSSOProviders) alt lastAuthProvider exists useSignInHook->>useSignInHook: sort providers so lastAuthProvider is first else no lastAuthProvider useSignInHook->>useSignInHook: keep original provider order end useSignInHook-->>SignInPage: lastAuthProvider and sortedProviders as oAuthSSOProviders SignInPage->>SignInEmailStep: render with lastAuthProvider and oAuthSSOProviders loop for each provider in oAuthSSOProviders alt provider equals lastAuthProvider SignInEmailStep->>SignInEmailStep: wrap Button in Badge.Ribbon with last used label else provider does not equal lastAuthProvider SignInEmailStep->>SignInEmailStep: render Button without Badge.Ribbon end end ``` #### Class diagram for updated sign-in hook and components with lastAuthProvider ```mermaid classDiagram class UseSignInHook { - string|null lastAuthProvider - string[] oAuthSSOProviders - string[] ssoProviders - string[] resolvedProviders - string[] sortedProviders - boolean disableEmailPassword - boolean isSocialOnly - boolean loading - boolean socialLoading - string email - string step + UseSignInHook() + handleSignIn(values) + handleSocialSignIn(provider) } class SignInPage { + SignInPage() + render() } class SignInEmailStep { + boolean disableEmailPassword + form + boolean isSocialOnly + string|null lastAuthProvider + boolean loading + string[] oAuthSSOProviders + boolean serverConfigInit + function onCheckUser(values) + function onSocialSignIn(provider) + function onReset() + render() } SignInPage --> UseSignInHook : uses SignInPage --> SignInEmailStep : renders UseSignInHook --> SignInEmailStep : provides lastAuthProvider and sortedProviders_as_oAuthSSOProviders SignInEmailStep ..> UseSignInHook : calls onSocialSignIn ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Persist and expose last-used OAuth provider state in sign-in hook and propagate to UI |
  • Define a LAST_AUTH_PROVIDER_KEY constant for localStorage persistence
  • Initialize lastAuthProvider state from localStorage in a safe, try/catch-wrapped lazy initializer
  • On successful preSocialSigninCheck, write the chosen provider to localStorage inside a try/catch
  • Introduce resolvedProviders abstraction and compute sortedProviders that moves lastAuthProvider to the front
  • Return lastAuthProvider and sortedProviders via the hook, replacing direct oAuthSSOProviders usage
  • Plumb lastAuthProvider through SignInPage into SignInEmailStep props

## Reviewer's Guide Adds early support for the xAI Grok 4.20 model series, including new model cards, wiring of a Grok-specific reasoning-effort param throughout chat config, UI, and runtime, routing certain Grok models through the Responses API with encrypted reasoning content, and retiring older Grok entries. #### Sequence diagram for Grok 4.20 multi-agent request via Responses API ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as ModelSwitchPanel_UI participant Controls as ControlsForm participant ChatService as ChatController participant Resolver as resolveModelExtendParams participant Runtime as LobeXAI participant XAI as xAI_Responses_API User->>UI: Select model grok-4.20-multi-agent-experimental-beta-0304 User->>Controls: Adjust Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider (e.g. high) Controls->>ChatService: Submit chat with chatConfig.grok4_20ReasoningEffort=high ChatService->>Resolver: resolveModelExtendParams(ctx) Resolver->>Resolver: model.settings.extendParams includes grok4_20ReasoningEffort Resolver->>Resolver: set extendParams.reasoning_effort = chatConfig.grok4_20ReasoningEffort Resolver-->>ChatService: ModelExtendParams(reasoning_effort=high) ChatService->>Runtime: chat(payload model=grok-4.20-multi-agent-experimental-beta-0304, extendParams.reasoning_effort=high) Runtime->>Runtime: responsesAPIGrokModels.has(model) == true Runtime->>Runtime: set apiMode=responses Runtime->>Runtime: set include=['reasoning.encrypted_content'] Runtime->>XAI: POST /responses (model, messages, reasoning_effort=high, include=['reasoning.encrypted_content']) XAI-->>Runtime: stream with output and reasoning.encrypted_content Runtime-->>ChatService: normalized stream ChatService-->>UI: display answer (no raw chain-of-thought) UI-->>User: Render response ``` #### Class diagram for Grok 4.20 reasoning effort wiring ```mermaid classDiagram class LobeAgentChatConfig { +string? gpt4oReasoningEffort +string? gpt5_1ReasoningEffort +string? gpt5_2ProReasoningEffort +string? gpt5_2ReasoningEffort +string? gpt5ReasoningEffort +string? grok4_20ReasoningEffort } class AgentChatConfigSchema { +object shape } class ExtendParamsType { } class ExtendParamsTypeSchema { +enum values } class Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider { +string configKey +string defaultValue +string[] levels } class ControlsForm { -Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider grok420ReasoningEffortSlider } class ExtendParamsSelect { -Map~ExtendParamsType,PreviewMeta~ previewMeta -Map~ExtendParamsType,ReactElement~ extendParamPreview } class xaiChatModels { <> } class AIChatModelCard { +string id +string displayName +object abilities +number contextWindowTokens +string description +boolean enabled +object pricing +string releasedAt +AIChatModelSettings settings +string type } class AIChatModelSettings { +string[] extendParams +string searchImpl } class ModelParamsContext { +AIChatModelCard model +LobeAgentChatConfig chatConfig } class resolveModelExtendParams { +ModelExtendParams resolve(ctx) } class ModelExtendParams { +string? reasoning_effort +string? effort } class responsesAPIGrokModels { <> +'grok-4.20-multi-agent-experimental-beta-0304' } class LobeXAI { +handlePayload(payload) ChatStreamPayload +chat(payload) ChatStreamResult } class ChatStreamPayload { +string model +boolean? enabledSearch +boolean? stream +object tools +string apiMode +string[] include } class XAIProviderConfig { +boolean supportResponsesApi } LobeAgentChatConfig --> AgentChatConfigSchema : validatedBy ExtendParamsTypeSchema --> ExtendParamsType : enumOf Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider --> LobeAgentChatConfig : usesConfigKey_grok4_20ReasoningEffort ControlsForm --> Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider : renders ExtendParamsSelect --> ExtendParamsType : uses ExtendParamsSelect --> Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider : previewFor_grok4_20ReasoningEffort xaiChatModels --> AIChatModelCard : contains AIChatModelCard --> AIChatModelSettings : has ModelParamsContext --> AIChatModelCard : model ModelParamsContext --> LobeAgentChatConfig : chatConfig resolveModelExtendParams --> ModelParamsContext : reads resolveModelExtendParams --> ModelExtendParams : returns AIChatModelSettings --> ExtendParamsType : extendParamsIncludes_grok4_20ReasoningEffort resolveModelExtendParams --> LobeAgentChatConfig : reads_grok4_20ReasoningEffort resolveModelExtendParams --> ModelExtendParams : sets_reasoning_effort LobeXAI --> responsesAPIGrokModels : checks_model_membership LobeXAI --> ChatStreamPayload : builds LobeXAI --> XAIProviderConfig : createdWith XAIProviderConfig --> LobeXAI : configures_supportResponsesApi ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Register Grok 4.20 experimental chat models in the model bank and deprecate legacy Grok entries. |
  • Add three new Grok 4.20 model definitions (multi-agent, non-reasoning, and reasoning variants) with capabilities, pricing, and settings (including grok4_20ReasoningEffort)
  • Disable the previous Grok 4 flagship model by removing its enabled flag
  • Remove the legacy grok-2-vision-1212 model card
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/xai.ts` | | Introduce Grok 4.20-specific reasoning-effort configuration and UI control. |
  • Define grok4_20ReasoningEffort in the shared ExtendParamsType and LobeAgentChatConfig, including Zod validation and allowed levels
  • Expose grok4_20ReasoningEffort as an extend param option with shared reasoning-effort title aliasing and preview metadata
  • Add a dedicated Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider component and render it in the model controls form and extend-params preview map
| `packages/model-bank/src/types/aiModel.ts`
`packages/types/src/agent/chatConfig.ts`
`src/routes/(main)/settings/provider/features/ModelList/CreateNewModelModal/ExtendParamsSelect.tsx`
`src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/ControlsForm/ControlsForm.tsx`
`src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/ControlsForm/Grok420ReasoningEffortSlider.tsx` | | Wire Grok 4.20 reasoning-effort and Responses API behavior into the XAI runtime. |
  • Add responsesAPIGrokModels set and use it in the XAI runtime to force specified Grok models through the Responses API, regardless of enabledSearch
  • Map chatConfig.grok4_20ReasoningEffort into the generic reasoning_effort extend param when the model declares grok4_20ReasoningEffort
  • Configure the XAI runtime to always request encrypted reasoning content via include: ['reasoning.encrypted_content'] for responses API calls
  • Mark the XAI provider as supporting the Responses API and add locale hint text describing Grok 4.20 reasoning-effort behavior (agent counts per level)
| `packages/model-runtime/src/const/models.ts`
`src/services/chat/mecha/modelParamsResolver.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xai/index.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/modelProviders/xai.ts`
`src/locales/default/modelProvider.ts`
`locales/en-US/modelProvider.json`
`locales/zh-CN/modelProvider.json` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Adds support for the new gpt-5.4 model across model-bank and runtime, updates plan card and responses API model sets accordingly, and tightens reasoning payload pruning and logging behavior for OpenAI router requests. #### Sequence diagram for OpenAI router request with reasoning pruning and success logging ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant RouterRuntime participant PruneReasoningPayload participant OpenAIAPI Client->>RouterRuntime: createRouterRuntime request(model, payload) RouterRuntime->>PruneReasoningPayload: pruneReasoningPayload(payload) PruneReasoningPayload-->>RouterRuntime: cleanedPayload RouterRuntime->>OpenAIAPI: send cleanedPayload OpenAIAPI-->>RouterRuntime: response alt request used fallback RouterRuntime->>RouterRuntime: log request success with fallback else request did not use fallback RouterRuntime->>RouterRuntime: log request success without fallback end RouterRuntime-->>Client: streamed or json response ``` #### Updated class diagram for ChatStreamPayload and GPT 5.4 model registration ```mermaid classDiagram class ChatStreamPayload { +string model +string~array~ messages +string responseMode +boolean stream +string imageResolution +boolean logprobs +number max_tokens +object metadata +object reasoning +string reasoning_effort +object response_format +number temperature +number top_p +number top_logprobs +string truncation } class AIChatModelCard { +string id +string displayName +string type +string description +boolean enabled +number contextWindowTokens +number maxOutput +object pricing +object abilities +string releasedAt +object settings } class GPT5_4_ModelCard { +id = gpt-5.4 +displayName = GPT-5.4 +type = chat +abilities.functionCall = true +abilities.reasoning = true +abilities.search = true +abilities.vision = true +contextWindowTokens = 1050000 +maxOutput = 128000 +settings.extendParams~array~ } class ModelProviderCard_LobeHub { +AIChatModelCard~array~ openaiChatModels +string~array~ planCardModels +Set responsesAPIModels } GPT5_4_ModelCard --|> AIChatModelCard ModelProviderCard_LobeHub "1" o-- "many" AIChatModelCard : openaiChatModels class pruneReasoningPayload { +ChatStreamPayload pruneReasoningPayload(ChatStreamPayload payload) } pruneReasoningPayload ..> ChatStreamPayload : prunes fields class RouterRuntime { +createRouterRuntime() +log request success with fallback +log request success without fallback } RouterRuntime ..> pruneReasoningPayload : uses ModelProviderCard_LobeHub ..> GPT5_4_ModelCard : includes in openaiChatModels ModelProviderCard_LobeHub ..> ChatStreamPayload : target of requests ``` #### Flow diagram for pruneReasoningPayload reasoning and logprobs handling ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start pruneReasoningPayload with ChatStreamPayload] --> B{Is model in disableStreamModels?} B -->|Yes| C[Set shouldStream to false] B -->|No| D[Set shouldStream to true] C --> E[Strip stream_options, logprobs, top_logprobs into cleanedPayload] D --> E E --> F[Determine effort from payload.reasoning.effort or payload.reasoning_effort] F --> G{Is effort equal to none?} G -->|Yes| H[isEffortNone true] G -->|No or undefined| I[isEffortNone false] H --> J[Build result payload
keep temperature
keep top_p
keep logprobs
keep top_logprobs] I --> K[Build result payload
unset temperature
unset top_p
unset logprobs
unset top_logprobs] J --> L[Return pruned payload] K --> L ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add GPT-5.4 model definition and wire it into provider plan and responses API support. |
  • Define a new GPT-5.4 AIChatModelCard with abilities, pricing, and settings in the LobeHub OpenAI chat model list.
  • Update planCardModels to reference gpt-5.4 instead of gpt-5.2 for plan UI usage.
  • Include gpt-5.4 in the responsesAPIModels set so it is routed via the responses API path.
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/lobehub/chat/openai.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/modelProviders/lobehub.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/const/models.ts` | | Adjust reasoning payload pruning to correctly handle logprobs/top_logprobs and expanded reasoning_effort values. |
  • Extend ChatStreamPayload type to add logprobs and top_logprobs fields and expand reasoning_effort to include none and xhigh.
  • Update pruneReasoningPayload to strip stream_options, logprobs, and top_logprobs by default and only pass logprobs/top_logprobs/temperature/top_p through when reasoning effort is none, per OpenAI docs.
  • Ensure the pruned payload shape aligns with the new ChatStreamPayload typing for reasoning models.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/openai.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/types/chat.ts` | | Improve RouterRuntime success logging and fix parameter mismatch. |
  • Add an explicit success log path for non-fallback requests in RouterRuntime so all successful requests are logged.
  • Align the log message format and parameters between fallback and non-fallback success logging branches.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/RouterRuntime/createRuntime.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#[Bug] Reasoning models still send top_p/temperature parameters even when "Deep Thinking" is enabled**: PR’s pruneReasoningPayload change ensures reasoning models prune sampling/logprobs params correctly, directly addressing the reasoning bug. ---

## Reviewer's Guide Refactors the Docker Compose deployment to remove the intermediary network-service container in favor of direct bridge networking, adjust service wiring and volumes accordingly, and updates self-hosting docs to match the new networking model and S3/URL guidance while removing a broken doc link. #### Sequence diagram for rustfs-init configuring rustfs via service name ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant DockerCompose as DockerCompose participant Rustfs as rustfs participant RustfsInit as rustfs-init DockerCompose->>Rustfs: Start container lobe-rustfs Rustfs-->>DockerCompose: Healthcheck OK on http://localhost:9000/health DockerCompose->>RustfsInit: Start container lobe-rustfs-init RustfsInit->>Rustfs: HTTP mc alias set rustfs http://rustfs:9000 RustfsInit->>Rustfs: HTTP mc ls rustfs RustfsInit->>Rustfs: HTTP mc mb rustfs/lobe --ignore-existing RustfsInit->>Rustfs: HTTP mc admin info rustfs RustfsInit->>Rustfs: HTTP mc anonymous set-json /bucket.config.json rustfs/lobe RustfsInit-->>DockerCompose: Exit 0 (service_completed_successfully) ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Replace the dedicated network-service container and network_mode usage with direct service networking and explicit port bindings. |
  • Remove the alpine-based network-service container used as a shared network namespace.
  • Move the lobe application service earlier in the file and attach it directly to the lobe-network bridge network.
  • Replace network_mode: 'service:network-service' with normal networking and service-to-service URLs.
  • Adjust depends_on conditions for lobe to reference actual services (postgresql, redis, rustfs, rustfs-init).
| `docker-compose/deploy/docker-compose.yml` | | Improve storage and port configuration for database, cache, and RustFS services, including optional admin access. |
  • Switch from named or generic volumes to relative host directories for postgres, redis, and rustfs data to simplify persistence and backup.
  • Add comments explaining when to expose or adjust host ports for postgres and redis.
  • Expose RUSTFS_PORT and a new RUSTFS_ADMIN_PORT for rustfs, with comments on when external access is needed and the impact on conversation image uploads.
  • Attach rustfs explicitly to the lobe-network and keep its healthcheck and startup command intact.
| `docker-compose/deploy/docker-compose.yml` | | Update internal S3 and initialization wiring to use service names instead of the removed network-service container. |
  • Change rustfs-init mc alias endpoint from http://network-service:9000 to http://rustfs:9000 for bucket initialization.
  • Set S3_ENDPOINT in the lobe service environment (passed through from .env) and continue to use rustfs-related S3 credentials and bucket configuration.
  • Document different S3_ENDPOINT values for internal-only vs externally accessible usage in the docs.
| `docker-compose/deploy/docker-compose.yml`
`docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.mdx`
`docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.zh-CN.mdx` | | Align Docker Compose self-hosting documentation with the new networking model and add guidance for single-domain and INTERNAL_APP_URL usage while removing a broken reference. |
  • Add a tip callout describing single-domain deployments that distinguish services via different ports and clarifying Port Mode vs Domain Mode behavior.
  • Remove an info callout that linked to a non-existent server-database deployment page.
  • Add callouts describing when S3_ENDPOINT can be an internal rustfs URL and the limitations for conversation image uploads, with localized differences between English and Chinese docs.
  • Update INTERNAL_APP_URL recommendation from localhost-based URL tied to network_mode to using the lobe service name (http://lobe:3210) for container-to-container communication.
| `docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.mdx`
`docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.zh-CN.mdx` | | Prepare environment example files to reflect the new Compose behavior (placeholders for further updates). |
  • Touch or stage changes to the deployment .env example files to align them with the updated Compose stack (diff not shown, reviewer should verify variables like RUSTFS_ADMIN_PORT/S3_ENDPOINT).
| `docker-compose/deploy/.env.example`
`docker-compose/deploy/.env.zh-CN.example` | ### Assessment against linked issues | Issue | Objective | Addressed | Explanation | | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12748 | Remove the unnecessary `network-service` container from the Docker Compose deployment and have all services use the `lobe-network` bridge network directly, updating any dependent configuration accordingly. | ✅ | | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12748 | Fix the broken "Custom Deployment" documentation link to `/en/docs/self-hosting/server-database` (by removing or updating it) in both English and Chinese Docker Compose docs. | ✅ | | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12748 | Clarify Docker Compose deployment documentation regarding (a) the difference between Port Mode and Domain Mode and (b) when RustFS-related ports/S3 endpoints (e.g., `RUSTFS_PORT`, `S3_ENDPOINT`) need to be exposed, including impact on avatar vs conversation image uploads. | ✅ | | ### Possibly linked issues - **#12748**: The PR removes network-service, fixes the broken docs link, and clarifies Port/Domain modes and RustFS/S3 port behavior. ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. ## Reviewer's Guide This PR fixes issues with agent forking in the community deployment by making token refresh concurrency-safe and more reliable, and by enforcing market authentication before the fork-and-chat actions for both agents and group agents. #### Sequence diagram for concurrent token refresh in DiscoverService ```mermaid sequenceDiagram title Concurrent_token_refresh_handling_in_DiscoverService participant CallerA participant CallerB participant DiscoverService participant AuthServer participant BrowserCookieStore CallerA->>DiscoverService: injectMPToken() activate DiscoverService DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: getTokenStatusFromCookie() alt token_status_active DiscoverService-->>CallerA: return else token_status_not_active DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: _tokenRefreshPromise? alt no_existing_promise DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: _tokenRefreshPromise = _doRefreshToken() DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: await _tokenRefreshPromise DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: _tokenRefreshPromise = null DiscoverService-->>CallerA: return end end deactivate DiscoverService CallerB->>DiscoverService: injectMPToken() activate DiscoverService DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: getTokenStatusFromCookie() alt token_status_not_active_and_promise_exists DiscoverService->>DiscoverService: await _tokenRefreshPromise DiscoverService-->>CallerB: return deactivate DiscoverService end rect rgb(230,230,250) DiscoverService->>AuthServer: _doRefreshToken() ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a daemonized background mode and management subcommands to the `connect` CLI command, introduces a daemon manager module and API client wrapper, and prepares the CLI package for publishing as a compiled Node ESM binary with build tooling and updated tests. #### Sequence diagram for lh connect daemon start and child connection ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant CLI as CLI_connect_command participant Manager as DaemonManager participant Node as Node_runtime participant Child as Daemon_child_process participant GWClient as GatewayClient User->>CLI: lh connect --daemon [options] CLI->>CLI: handleDaemonStart(options) CLI->>Manager: getRunningDaemonPid() Manager-->>CLI: null (no running daemon) CLI->>Manager: spawnDaemon(args) Manager->>Node: spawn(process.execPath, [...execArgv, args, --daemon-child]) Node-->>Manager: child_pid Manager->>Manager: writePid(child_pid) Manager-->>CLI: child_pid CLI->>User: "Daemon started (PID child_pid)" Note over Child,Manager: Daemon child process flow Child->>Child: runConnect(options, isDaemonChild=true) Child->>GWClient: new GatewayClient({...logger: createDaemonLogger(), ...}) Child->>GWClient: connect() GWClient-->>Child: connected event Child->>Manager: writeStatus({connectionStatus: connected, ...}) Child->>Manager: appendLog("[INFO] ...") GWClient-->>Child: tool_call_request Child->>Child: executeToolCall(apiName, args) Child->>GWClient: sendToolCallResponse(...) Child->>Manager: appendLog("[TOOL] ...") ``` #### Sequence diagram for daemon lifecycle stop and status commands ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant CLI as CLI_connect_subcommands participant Manager as DaemonManager User->>CLI: lh connect stop CLI->>Manager: stopDaemon() Manager->>Manager: getRunningDaemonPid() alt daemon_running Manager->>OS: kill(pid, SIGTERM) Manager->>Manager: removePid() Manager->>Manager: removeStatus() Manager-->>CLI: true CLI->>User: "Daemon stopped." else no_daemon Manager-->>CLI: false CLI->>User: "No daemon is running." end User->>CLI: lh connect status CLI->>Manager: getRunningDaemonPid() alt daemon_not_running Manager-->>CLI: null CLI->>User: "No daemon is running." else daemon_running Manager-->>CLI: pid CLI->>Manager: readStatus() Manager-->>CLI: DaemonStatus CLI->>User: print PID, startedAt, connectionStatus, gatewayUrl, uptime end ``` #### Sequence diagram for ApiClient tRPC request flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as CLI_command participant Api as ApiClient participant Auth as Auth_token_store participant HTTP as HTTP_server CLI->>Api: ApiClient.create() Api->>Auth: getValidToken() alt token_missing Auth-->>Api: null Api->>CLI: log.error("Run 'lh login'") Api->>CLI: process.exit(1) else token_present Auth-->>Api: {credentials} Api-->>CLI: new ApiClient(serverUrl, accessToken) end CLI->>Api: query("procedure", input) Api->>HTTP: GET /trpc/lambda/procedure?input={json} HTTP-->>Api: HTTP_response alt !res.ok Api->>CLI: log.error("API request failed") Api->>CLI: process.exit(1) else ok Api->>Api: handleResponse() alt body.error Api->>CLI: log.error("message (code)") Api->>CLI: process.exit(1) else body.result Api-->>CLI: data.json end end ``` #### Class diagram for ApiClient and daemon manager APIs ```mermaid classDiagram class ApiClient { -string serverUrl -string token +ApiClient(serverUrl string, token string) +static create() ApiClient +query(procedure string, input any) Promise~T~ +mutation(procedure string, input any) Promise~T~ -handleResponse(res Response, procedure string) Promise~T~ } class DaemonStatus { +string connectionStatus +string gatewayUrl +number pid +string startedAt } class DaemonManager { +readPid() number +writePid(pid number) void +removePid() void +isProcessAlive(pid number) boolean +getRunningDaemonPid() number +writeStatus(status DaemonStatus) void +readStatus() DaemonStatus +removeStatus() void +getLogPath() string +rotateLogIfNeeded() void +appendLog(line string) void +spawnDaemon(args string[]) number +stopDaemon() boolean } class ConnectCommand { +registerConnectCommand(program Command) void +handleDaemonStart(options ConnectOptions) void +buildDaemonArgs(options ConnectOptions) string[] +runConnect(options ConnectOptions, isDaemonChild boolean) Promise~void~ +createDaemonLogger() DaemonLogger +formatUptime(startedAt Date) string } class ConnectOptions { +boolean daemon +boolean daemonChild +string deviceId +string gateway +string token +boolean verbose } class DaemonLogger { +debug(msg string) void +info(msg string) void +warn(msg string) void +error(msg string) void } ApiClient ..> DaemonStatus : uses_for_auth_status? ConnectCommand --> DaemonManager : uses ConnectCommand --> ApiClient : may_use_for_future_api ConnectCommand --> DaemonLogger : creates DaemonManager --> DaemonStatus : reads_writes ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add daemonized background mode and management subcommands to the `connect` command. |
  • Extend connect options to support daemon/daemon-child flags and route main action into a reusable `runConnect` helper.
  • Introduce `lh connect stop|status|logs|restart` subcommands wired to daemon lifecycle and log inspection operations.
  • Refactor connection setup and event handling (system info, tool calls, auth events, errors, signals) into `runConnect`, with different logging behavior for daemon vs foreground.
  • Change auth-expired handling to log via error channel instead of warn and remove legacy service-token/user-id options and logging.
| `apps/cli/src/commands/connect.ts` | | Introduce a daemon manager module to manage PID, status, and logging, and implement process lifecycle helpers. |
  • Add PID file helpers with process liveness checks and stale file cleanup to determine the running daemon PID.
  • Add status file read/write/remove helpers and a `DaemonStatus` type used by connect status reporting.
  • Add log file path resolution, rotation, and timestamped append helpers plus a simple logger adapter for daemon mode.
  • Add `spawnDaemon` to start a detached Node child process with log redirection and `stopDaemon` to terminate and clean up an existing daemon.
| `apps/cli/src/daemon/manager.ts` | | Update and extend tests to cover daemon behavior and new logging semantics. |
  • Mock daemon manager functions and internal state for the connect command tests, resetting state between tests.
  • Adjust expectations for auth-expired handling to use error logging and remove service-token related test coverage.
  • Add test cases for `--daemon`, `connect stop`, `connect status`, and `connect restart` subcommands, including already-running and no-daemon scenarios.
  • Update login command tests to mock `child_process.execFile` in addition to `exec` to prevent real browser execution.
| `apps/cli/src/commands/connect.test.ts`
`apps/cli/src/commands/login.test.ts`
`apps/cli/src/daemon/manager.test.ts` | | Add an API client wrapper for authenticated tRPC lambda calls used by CLI commands. |
  • Implement `ApiClient` with factory method `create` that obtains credentials using `getValidToken` and exits with an error if unauthenticated.
  • Provide `query` and `mutation` helpers that format tRPC-compatible URLs and payloads and attach bearer auth headers.
  • Centralize response handling with structured error logging (HTTP and tRPC errors) and process exit on failure.
| `apps/cli/src/api/client.ts` | | Prepare the CLI package for distribution as a built Node ESM binary using tsup. |
  • Switch package to ESM via `type: module`, point the `lh` bin to `dist/index.js`, and expose only the built `dist` directory in published files.
  • Add build tooling: tsup config for Node 18 ESM bundling with a shebang, `build`/`dev`/`prepublishOnly` scripts, and move some runtime deps to devDependencies with additional typings.
  • Add publish configuration for public npm registry and exclude test files from TypeScript compilation in `tsconfig.json`.
  • Add `ws` and `@types/ws` dependencies required for the device gateway client, and keep the client non-external in the bundle.
| `apps/cli/package.json`
`apps/cli/tsup.config.ts`
`apps/cli/tsconfig.json` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Hotfix adjusts the stable desktop release GitHub Actions workflow to archive renderer assets from the current Electron renderer output directory and adds a guard to ensure the directory exists, fixing Linux stable build failures at the renderer tarball step. #### Flow diagram for Linux renderer tarball creation step in CI ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start Linux packaging step] --> B[npm run desktop:package:app] B --> C[Electron builds renderer assets into apps/desktop/dist/renderer] C --> D{Does apps/desktop/dist/renderer exist} D -- no --> E[Fail job at directory check] D -- yes --> F[Create lobehub-renderer.tar.gz
tar -czf apps/desktop/release/lobehub-renderer.tar.gz
-C apps/desktop/dist/renderer .] F --> G[Renderer tarball available for release] G --> H[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Fix stable desktop Linux workflow step that archives renderer assets so it uses the correct output directory and fails early if assets are missing. |
  • Update tar command to archive from apps/desktop/dist/renderer instead of the removed out directory.
  • Add a directory existence check before creating the renderer tarball so the job fails clearly if the renderer output is missing.
| `.github/workflows/release-desktop-stable.yml` |

## Reviewer's Guide This PR simplifies several aspects of the UI (model switch panel, home layout, user panel, and input area) and introduces curated multi-locale starter questions, while removing or hiding some advanced/secondary controls (model config, memory shortcuts, extra sections) to streamline the main chat experience. #### Sequence diagram for simplified model switch panel ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatInput as ChatInput participant ModelSwitch as ModelSwitch participant ModelSwitchPanel as ModelSwitchPanel participant AgentStore as useAgentStore User->>ChatInput: Click_model_icon ChatInput->>ModelSwitch: Render_model_trigger User->>ModelSwitchPanel: Open_panel ModelSwitchPanel-->>User: Show_fixed_width_list_byModel User->>ModelSwitchPanel: Select_model(model,provider) ModelSwitchPanel->>ModelSwitch: onModelChange(model,provider) ModelSwitch->>AgentStore: updateAgentConfigById(agentId,{model,provider}) AgentStore-->>ModelSwitch: State_updated ModelSwitch-->>User: Updated_model_icon User->>ModelSwitchPanel: Close_panel ModelSwitchPanel-->>User: Panel_closed ``` #### Class diagram for updated model switch and panel components ```mermaid classDiagram class ModelSwitch { +string agentId +string model +string provider +string dropdownPlacement +handleModelChange(model,provider) } class ModelSwitchPanel { +string model +string provider +string placement +onModelChange(model,provider) } class Toolbar { +string searchKeyword +onSearchKeywordChange(keyword) } class PanelContent { +string model +string provider +boolean open +number panelHeight +onOpenChange(open) +onModelChange(model,provider) } class List { +string groupMode +string model +string provider +string searchKeyword +onModelChange(model,provider) +onOpenChange(open) } class ModelDetailPanel { +string modelId +string provider +string[] expandedKeys } ModelSwitch --> ModelSwitchPanel : wraps ModelSwitchPanel --> PanelContent : renders PanelContent --> Toolbar : uses PanelContent --> List : uses List ..> ModelDetailPanel : shows_details_for_selection ``` #### Class diagram for updated user panel and language button ```mermaid classDiagram class User { +string nickname +string username +boolean isSignedIn +string subscriptionPlan +string planName } class UserPanel { } class UserInfo { +boolean isSignedIn +string nickname +string username +onClick() } class LangButton { +string placement +number size +string language +buildItems() } class Menu { } class PanelContent { +closePopover() } class ThemeButton { +string placement +number size } User --> UserPanel : rendered_in UserPanel --> PanelContent : shows PanelContent --> Menu : renders_main_and_logout_items PanelContent --> LangButton : renders_language_menu UserInfo --> ThemeButton : shows_theme_toggle_when_signed_in ``` #### Flow diagram for simplified home layout and input area ```mermaid flowchart TD A_Enter_home --> B_Render_NavHeader B_Render_NavHeader --> C_Hide_right_header_controls C_Hide_right_header_controls --> D_Show_HomeContent D_Show_HomeContent --> E_Show_WelcomeText E_Show_WelcomeText --> F_Show_InputArea F_Show_InputArea --> G_Show_StarterList F_Show_InputArea --> H_Maybe_show_SuggestQuestions H_Maybe_show_SuggestQuestions{inputActiveMode} H_Maybe_show_SuggestQuestions -->|agent_group_write| I_Show_SuggestQuestions H_Maybe_show_SuggestQuestions -->|chat_or_undefined| J_Hide_SuggestQuestions G_Show_StarterList --> K_hideStarterList_check K_hideStarterList_check{inputActiveMode_in_agent_group_write?} K_hideStarterList_check -->|Yes| L_Hide_StarterList K_hideStarterList_check -->|No| M_Show_StarterList I_Show_SuggestQuestions --> N_User_clicks_question J_Hide_SuggestQuestions --> O_User_uses_StarterList L_Hide_StarterList --> I_Show_SuggestQuestions M_Show_StarterList --> O_User_uses_StarterList N_User_clicks_question --> P_Prefill_input O_User_uses_StarterList --> P_Prefill_input P_Prefill_input --> Q_User_edits_and_sends ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add curated, randomized starter questions for the chat input across locales, including a default "chat" mode. |
  • Populate suggestQuestions locale map with 40 en/zh starter prompts and titles under the chat.* keys.
  • Extend useRandomQuestions to treat a missing mode as a new "chat" mode and generate i18n keys based on a normalized modeKey.
  • Relax SuggestQuestions visibility guard so the component renders for undefined (chat) mode but still ignores unsupported modes.
  • Introduce/adjust suggestQuestions locale JSON files for en-US and zh-CN to back the new keys.
| `src/locales/default/suggestQuestions.ts`

`locales/en-US/suggestQuestions.json`
`locales/zh-CN/suggestQuestions.json` | | Simplify the model switch UI by removing advanced model config controls, fixed-widthing the panel, and flattening the toolbar/list presentation. |
  • Remove the extend-params/settings action and container styling from the chat input model switch trigger, leaving only the icon-bound ModelSwitchPanel.
  • Strip group-mode toggling (by model/provider) from the toolbar and hardcode list grouping to byModel, keeping only a search box.

  • Update the home BottomMenu to show Community (gated by showMarket), Resource, and Pages tabs, including support for item.hidden flags.

  • Hide secondary home modules (recent topics/pages/resources and community agents) by commenting them out, retaining only WelcomeText and InputArea in the home content.
  • Change StarterList to re-enable the hot Video starter card and adjust InputArea logic so the starter list hides only when in agent/group/write modes, while suggest questions show for chat/undefined mode and add distinct key/margin for the default chat state.

  • Simplify WelcomeText by replacing the animated TypewriterEffect/shuffle implementation with a single random sample string from welcomeMessages.
  • Change LangButton to render either a compact ActionIcon (when size is provided) or a full-width menu-row trigger, and use that trigger inside the dropdown instead of always using ActionIcon.
  • Enhance the user dropdown header block to display the user’s subscription plan label (except Free) under the name with proper ellipsis, and adjust displayName/plan selection.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Refactors the release GitHub Actions workflow to drop semantic-release in favor of a manual changelog generation step using conventional-changelog, adds a static changelog build, tightens checkout and push behavior, and updates the auto-commit message accordingly. #### Sequence diagram for updated release workflow changelog generation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Developer participant GitHubActions participant Repo Developer->>GitHubActions: Push to main / trigger release workflow GitHubActions->>Repo: actions_checkout ref main fetch-depth 0 GitHubActions->>GitHubActions: Setup Node.js and dependencies GitHubActions->>GitHubActions: Determine release version get-version GitHubActions->>GitHubActions: Generate Changelog using conventional-changelog GitHubActions->>Repo: Update CHANGELOG.md GitHubActions->>GitHubActions: Run bun workflow:changelog GitHubActions->>Repo: Build static changelog artifacts GitHubActions->>GitHubActions: Run bun workflow:readme GitHubActions->>Repo: Update README artifacts GitHubActions->>Repo: git add . GitHubActions->>Repo: git commit "docs(bot): Auto update changelog and readme" GitHubActions->>Repo: git push origin main ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refine checkout configuration to ensure full history on main branch for changelog generation. |
  • Configure checkout action to explicitly use the main branch.
  • Set fetch-depth to 0 so the workflow has full git history available.
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | | Replace semantic-release-based release step with manual changelog generation using conventional-changelog-cli and gitmoji preset. |
  • Remove the release step that ran the semantic-release-based `bun run release` command.
  • Introduce a Generate Changelog step that runs conventional-changelog-cli with the gitmoji-config preset.
  • Configure conventional-changelog invocation to read and write CHANGELOG.md in-place and only regenerate the latest release entry.
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | | Add build step for static changelog artifacts and adjust auto-commit behavior. |
  • Add a Build Static Changelog step that runs `bun run workflow:changelog`.
  • Update the workflow step that commits changes to use a new commit message reflecting changelog and readme updates.

### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/3858046ec348cbdbfc104074c47543f9ffadb5dd/apps/device-gateway/src/DeviceGatewayDO.ts#L169-L173 **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Defer stale-connection eviction until auth succeeds** The upgrade path closes any existing socket with the same `deviceId` before the new socket has authenticated, so a caller that can hit `/ws` and knows a device ID can repeatedly force a legitimate connection offline without presenting a valid token first. This is reachable because the new `/ws` route forwards on `userId` only and authentication happens later in `webSocketMessage`; eviction should happen only after `auth_success` (or after pre-upgrade token validation). --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/3858046ec348cbdbfc104074c47543f9ffadb5dd/apps/device-gateway/src/DeviceGatewayDO.ts#L204-L206 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Schedule auth timeout at the earliest pending deadline** `scheduleAuthTimeout` only sets an alarm when none exists, so if a heartbeat alarm is already scheduled (up to 90s away) and a new unauthenticated socket connects, the auth timeout check is delayed until that later alarm. In that case sockets can remain unauthenticated far beyond `AUTH_TIMEOUT` and continue consuming connection slots; this helper should update the alarm when `now + AUTH_TIMEOUT` is earlier than the current alarm.

## Reviewer's Guide This PR moves changelog generation from the tag-triggered release workflow into the auto-tag workflow by introducing a custom git-log–driven changelog generator, wiring it into CI via Bun, and removing the now-broken semantic-release step so that CHANGELOG.md and static changelog JSON are correctly updated as part of the tagging commit. #### Class diagram for changelog generation module generateChangelog.ts ```mermaid classDiagram class Commit { +string hash +string[] issues +string scope +string subject +string type } class TypeConfig { +string detail +string emoji +string summary } class GenerateChangelogModule { <> +string REPO_URL +string CHANGELOG_TITLE +string BACK_TO_TOP +Record~string,TypeConfig~ TYPE_MAP +string git(cmd) +string getLastTag() +string getPreviousTag(currentTag) +Commit[] getCommits(from) +Record~string,Commit[]~ groupByType(commits) +string formatSummarySection(groups) +string formatDetailSection(groups) +void run() } GenerateChangelogModule --> Commit : uses GenerateChangelogModule --> TypeConfig : uses ``` #### Flow diagram for new auto-tag release and changelog generation pipeline ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start_auto_tag_release_job] --> B{should_tag_release_or_patch} B -->|no| Z[End_job_without_changes] B -->|yes| C[Setup_Node_js] C --> D[Install_Bun] D --> E[Install_dependencies_with_bun_i] E --> F{Tag_does_not_exist} F -->|no| Z F -->|yes| G[Bump_package_json_version] G --> H[Generate_changelog_with_workflow_changelog_gen] H --> I[Build_static_changelog_JSON_with_workflow_changelog] I --> J[Configure_git_user_lobehubbot] J --> K[git_add_package_json_CHANGELOG_md_changelog_dir] K --> L[Commit_release_changes] L --> M[Push_to_main] M --> N[Create_git_tag_vX_Y_Z] N --> O[Push_tag] O --> P[Tag_push_triggers_release_workflow] P --> Q[Release_workflow_runs_tests_and_readme_only] Q --> R[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce a custom changelog generator that derives gitmoji-style release notes from git history and writes them into CHANGELOG.md. |
  • Add generateChangelog.ts script that shells out to git, parses conventional commits (with optional gitmoji), and extracts type/scope/subject/issue metadata
  • Define a TYPE_MAP for supported commit types and map hotfix to fix for grouping
  • Compute the commit range based on last and previous tags, grouping commits by type and emitting summary and detailed sections matching the existing changelog format
  • Insert the newly generated release section into CHANGELOG.md above existing content, preserving the title and back-to-top badge
| `scripts/changelogWorkflow/generateChangelog.ts` | | Update the auto-tag release workflow to run the new changelog generator and static changelog builder before committing and tagging. |
  • Install Node.js and Bun only when a release or patch tag should be created, then install dependencies via Bun
  • Bump package.json version without configuring git in that step, deferring git config to a dedicated commit step
  • Invoke the new changelog generation script and the existing static changelog builder when a new tag should be created and does not yet exist
  • Add and commit package.json, CHANGELOG.md, and changelog/ directory changes with a standard release commit message, then push to main before tagging
| `.github/workflows/auto-tag-release.yml`
`package.json` | | Simplify the main release workflow by removing the semantic-release-based changelog/version verification steps that no longer work with pre-created tags. |
  • Remove tag-derived version extraction and package.json version verification steps that depended on the tag ref
  • Remove the semantic-release execution step that previously handled changelog and release automation
  • Leave the remaining test and workflow steps intact so the release workflow still validates and runs post-release tasks
